storage.closedSets: Every closed set below is a CHECK constraint over TEXT, never an enum type (the 0259 practice), and admits exactly the values this file lists.
storage.ids: uuid(7), minted by Prisma. The database gives no id column a default.
storage.tenancy: Every table carries a non-null owner_id. wiki_space alone points at user (ON DELETE CASCADE); every other table reaches its parent through (parent_id, owner_id) -> parent(id, owner_id), ON DELETE CASCADE, so a child can never belong to a different owner than its parent, and deleting an owner still deletes every row through its spaces: the space for bindings, topics, entries and changesets; the entry for revisions and exposures; the revision for sources; the changeset for ops. A binding reaches its workspace the same way, through workspace(id, owner_id).
storage.whyNotUser: A foreign key check takes FOR KEY SHARE on the row it names, and the user row is rank 10 in docs/postgres-lock-order.md, the row lockOwnerTaskGraph holds FOR UPDATE. wiki_exposure is written from dequeueTurn with the session row (rank 30) already held, so a user key on it would take rank 10 after rank 30. Through the space, a wiki write locks only wiki rows.
storage.locks: Lock an entry with FOR NO KEY UPDATE (a plain UPDATE does), never FOR UPDATE: an op's and an exposure's foreign keys take KEY SHARE on the entry, which FOR UPDATE would block.
storage.entryLinks: supersedes_id and superseded_by_id point at wiki_entry(id, owner_id) with NO ACTION; both ends live in one space, so a space's cascade deletes them in one statement. wiki_changeset_op.entry_id and result_entry_id point at wiki_entry(id, owner_id) with ON DELETE CASCADE, because an op is reached from its space through its changeset and through its entries, and a NO ACTION check could run before the other cascade arrives.
storage.historyRefs: An id that points at Orbit's own history carries no foreign key: session, task, tool_call, conversation turn, run event, the user who authored a revision, the op a revision came from (wiki_entry_revision.changeset_op_id), and every wiki_source.ref. A deleted record leaves the id behind as a tombstone, and a wiki write takes no lock on those tables (the precedent is 0238's deciding_session_id; docs/postgres-lock-order.md I2).
storage.verificationTrail: wiki_changeset_op.verification_duplicate_of names the entry a duplicate verdict pointed at, and is the one in-wiki pointer with no foreign key: it is part of the verdict's trail (reviewModes.verification.trail), which outlives the entry it named the way a history reference outlives its record. A cascade from that entry would delete the op, and with it the trail; a SET NULL would rewrite what the verifier said.
storage.singleWriter: wiki_entry.status, trust, challenged and unsupported are written only by WikiService.applyOp and WikiService.recomputeFlags, and db-write-inventory registers those two writers and no other.
storage.appendOnly: wiki_entry_revision is only ever inserted. A revision is never updated; a change is a new revision.

search.text: title, summary, the aliases and every string value inside fields, space-separated, with * and ` removed exactly as 0095 and stripMarks in sessions.service.ts remove them.
search.rule: A query reaches the index only by calling the same function over the same four columns; any other spelling of the same text scans every row.

space.identity: One space per owner and codebase. owner_id is the hard boundary: nothing is ever read, written, listed or counted across owners.

repoUrlNorm.rule: The remote URL without its scheme, userinfo, trailing .git or trailing /, so both spellings of one repository compare equal.
repoUrlNorm.absent: NULL: a space with no repository behind it. Two such spaces never collide.

space.rootCommitSha: The repository's first root commit, 40 lowercase hex characters, once a runner reports it. It tells apart two repositories behind one URL; NULL until then.

binding.rule: A workspace has at most one row (workspace_id is unique), and only to a space of its own owner (the composite foreign key refuses any other). A row is what the owner or a session said, and it outranks the repository.
binding.automatic: A workspace on a space's repository is in that space with no row: its repo_url normalizes to the space's repo_url_norm. Membership is read that way (wiki/wiki-workspaces.ts) rather than written, so a workspace joins however its repo_url came to be, and a space made after its workspaces has them all. A session of a workspace still writes a row on first use, which makes the space when its repository has none yet.
binding.manual: A workspace with no repository is added by the owner in Wiki settings (POST /api/wiki/spaces/:id/workspaces). One on another repository is refused 400: that repository has its own space, and what its sessions teach would be dropped here as another repository's knowledge.
binding.leftOut: The owner leaves a workspace out in Wiki settings (DELETE /api/wiki/spaces/:id/workspaces/:workspaceId): wiki_space_workspace.left_out_at is set, on a row made for it if it was in by its repository alone. Its sessions feed no maintenance run and are refused the wiki tools, what it already taught stays, and it does not rejoin by itself. The same POST turns it back on.
binding.ownerChannel: Both writes are the account owner's: a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY and a personal access token OWNER_INTERACTIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED, because who is in a space is who reads its entries. Neither moves the cursor: a workspace that joins is read from the space's watermark on.
binding.unbound: A session whose workspace is in no space is refused WIKI_SPACE_UNBOUND, with one sentence saying how to bind it. A session of a workspace left out is refused the same code, saying so.
binding.projects: A project reaches its space through its codebase's canonical repository URL. There is no project-to-space table.

workspaces.shape: { workspaces, addable }, each a list of { id, name, runner, inWiki }: a public id, the workspace's name, the machine it is on as the app names it (null when no runner holds it), and whether it is in this space.
workspaces.workspaces: The live workspaces on the space's repository, and the ones a row of this space names, by name whatever the case, so a row stays where it is when its switch moves. A workspace left out stays on the list with inWiki false.
workspaces.addable: The live workspaces Wiki settings' Add workspace offers: no repository, and in no wiki. One the owner left out of another space counts as in none. inWiki is false in every row.
workspaces.clients: Web, macOS/iOS and Android draw it as the Workspaces section between Review mode and Maintenance (docs/mocks/wiki/38-workspaces).

delete.answer: { spaceId }. Another account's space, or one already gone, is the plain 404.
delete.who: The owner's alone: a request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY and a personal access token OWNER_INTERACTIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED. No agent tool and no CLI command reaches it.
delete.takes: The space and everything hanging off it, by foreign key in one transaction, its public link included. It cannot be undone, and a failure leaves all of it.
delete.keeps: Workspaces, sessions, tasks and projects. Text that names an entry keeps its words, and an orbit-wiki: link in it names nothing.
delete.runningJobs: Not waited for and not refused: a job's row goes with its space, so every write of its claim matches nothing, and its next write that needs the space fails, which ends the attempt with nothing left to requeue. A repository operation's result is answered 404, which a runner takes as the operation being gone.
delete.repository: A space with a repository is made again, empty, by the next session on that repository to use a wiki tool (`binding.automatic`), and asks for its plan's first draft like any new space. Its workspaces' rows went with the old space, a left-out mark among them. A space with no repository stays gone, and a session bound to it is refused WIKI_SPACE_UNBOUND.
delete.clients: Web has it on a wiki's sidebar row and at the foot of Wiki settings; macOS/iOS and Android at the foot of Wiki settings. Each asks first, naming the wiki and how many entries and documents go (docs/mocks/wiki-delete).

list.row: Every space of the owner, by slug: the space as GET /api/wiki/spaces/:id answers it, with pendingOps, planWaiting, chatWaiting, workspaceIds and docs, which the one-space read does not carry. A client reading a server older than the last four takes them as absent.
list.pendingOps: The ops of its changesets that wait in Review (decision pending). Plan proposals are not ops and are not in it. Over the owner's spaces it is what the Activity page's first banner and Review's head show.
list.planWaiting: The things of its plan that wait on the owner, one each: the draft, revision or build on its way (the job plan.routes.state shows) that is held — by the server (plan.jobs.held), or made and not started while the maintenance workspace's runner is offline; the draft or revision that failed with no version stored since it was asked for; the draft waiting to be confirmed; and every proposal waiting. What is only going on (queued, drafting, writing) and a build that failed are not counted. The runner is the one the space's maintenance workspace is on, online by the runners list's own rule (isRunnerOnline); with no maintenance workspace, or one deleted or without a runner, it is unknown, and unknown is not offline. The count web wikiPlanPending and OrbitKit WikiPlanLogic.pending make, held by all three to the vectors of src/shared/src/wiki-docs.fixture.json plan.states (each case's pending). Added to pendingOps over the owner's spaces, it is the number waiting on the owner that the drawer, the web sidebar and the Wiki's Activity badge show — the sum of the Activity page's amber banners.
list.chatWaiting: The space's applied chat cards whose rewrite waits on the owner, one each (chat.waiting, wikiChatWaiting): held up, or read the same or failed and not seen. Added to pendingOps and planWaiting over the owner's spaces it is W on web and iOS — the drawer, the sidebar and the Activity badge — and Activity draws it as one amber banner (chat.waiting.banner). A client without the chat (Android, this phase) reads no chatWaiting and its W stays the other two, every one of which it can open. Open cards and approvals are not in it (chat.waiting.notCounted).
list.workspaceIds: The workspaces in it (binding) that are not deleted: the ones a row keeps there in the order they were bound, then the ones on its repository: public ids, like every id on the user door.
list.docs: { written, total }: its confirmed plan's documents and how many are written, as docs.reads.directory counts them; null while it has no confirmed plan.

push.means: Deliver <orbit_wiki_context> to the sessions of the space's workspaces. The owner decided on 2026-09-25 that it is on by default and that each space can turn it off.

autoAcceptReinforce.means: A non-owner reinforce applies at once. Off: it waits for review (effectPolicy).

reviewMode.means: Which of what the effect policy holds back the space applies at once (reviewModes). A space is created with the default; a stored space whose settings name no mode was made before review modes existed and reads as unset, so none of them changes behaviour until the owner can see the setting in Wiki settings and chooses another.
reviewMode.channel: Written only by PATCH /api/wiki/spaces/:id on the user door, with no session header (WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY otherwise), by the spot checks sending the space back to manual, and by the verification sending an automatic space back to tiered.

automaticSpotChecks.means: Whether an automatic space draws spot checks at all (reviewModes.spotChecks.automatic): off, the owner is sent no spot-check card for what its verification applies; on, one in every rules.automaticSpotCheckEvery. Tiered draws its spot checks whatever this says.
automaticSpotChecks.channel: The owner's alone, like reviewMode: PATCH /api/wiki/spaces/:id on the user door with no session header, and WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY otherwise.

reviewModeChangedAt.means: When the review mode last changed. Absent until it first does. The spot checks' window and the verification's window count only what was answered since.

reviewModeChangedBy.means: Who changed it last: the owner, the spot checks sending the space back to manual, or the verification sending an automatic space back to tiered.

keys.enabled: boolean. Off by default: in a space whose maintenance is off, no fact starts a maintenance run.
keys.workspaceId: The owner's workspace whose checkout the space's repository is read from: its runner answers the server's repository operations (repoOps), the maintenance runs' and the plan's jobs' alike. Maintenance cannot be turned on without one.
keys.provider: Not a setting any more (P11, 2026-10-19): the server's runs call the deployment's System model (systemModel), so nothing runs on a provider and no request sets one — a write that names it has it dropped by the door's whitelist. The read still carries the stored value, or local-vllm, as history: no client shows it or sends it since their runner mode was removed (2026-10-19).
keys.dailyRunLimit: How many maintenance runs the space may make in one UTC day: a whole number within bounds.dailyRunLimit. Counted as the runs the space's jobs made since midnight UTC (wiki_maintenance_run.job_id), however they ended, but the runs made in catch-up that are not counted (maintenance.job.catchUp.dailyLimit); the plan's jobs are no maintenance runs (plan.jobs.notAMaintenanceRun). The trigger reads the count (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday) before it makes one.
keys.lookbackDays: How far back the cursor starts when maintenance is turned on (maintenance.cursor.start): a whole number of days within bounds.lookbackDays — 0 reads only the facts from then on — or null, which reads from the earliest fact. 14 by default: before it, a space's first run read from its oldest fact, and orbit's cursor was started 14 days back by hand (2026-09-28). It starts a cursor that has no position once, and never moves one that has.
keys.listId: Server-written and never taken from a request: the space's hidden Wiki maintenance task list, which the runner path made the first time maintenance was turned on, before server execution (P11, 2026-10-19). No list is made since; an old one is kept with its tasks as history, and its sessions' facts stay out of the backlog (maintenance.cursor.excluded). null for a space made since.

maintenance.channel: The owner's alone: PATCH /api/wiki/spaces/:id on the user door with no session header — or POST /api/wiki/spaces, whose maintenance is checked before the space is made and then written as the PATCH writes it (plan.jobs.trigger) — and WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY otherwise. A request names any of enabled, workspaceId, dailyRunLimit and lookbackDays (a provider it names is dropped, keys.provider); what it leaves out stays as it was, and lookbackDays null is a value (all history), not a key left out. A stored value out of bounds, or of a key this contract no longer has, reads as the default.

keys.workspaceId: The workspace this space's chats run in (chat.workspace): a public id on the user door, null until the owner first chooses. Only an eligible workspace is stored (chat.workspace.eligible); a stored one that stops being eligible is left as it is and not used, and the panel asks again.

chat.channel: The owner's alone: PATCH /api/wiki/spaces/:id on the user door with no session header — WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY otherwise — or the chat's create naming another workspace (chat.create.rules). A request names workspaceId or leaves the key as it was; null forgets it.

convention.invalidation: The owner revises it, or one of its anchors stops verifying.

decision.invalidation: Only superseded, never rewritten: an amend of a decision is refused WIKI_SCHEMA. What the push carries of it is the constraint its title and summary state.

pitfall.invalidation: Retired once its fix lands. After 28 days with no push hit, no pull and no re-check it becomes pull-only (phase 2), and is kept.

recipe.invalidation: Re-verified before it is revised; a re-verification that fails retires it (phase 2).

concept.invalidation: One of its anchors stops verifying.

assumption.sketch: dependency { purl | cli | url }, contract, probe
assumption.reserved: The storage CHECK admits the word, so phase 3 needs no migration for it. Every phase-1 door refuses it: WIKI_SCHEMA on kind. It has no KIND_SPECS entry until phase 3 gives it one.

fieldTypes.text: A string with something besides whitespace in it, at most limits.fieldTextMaxChars characters. pattern, when given, is a regular expression the whole string matches.
fieldTypes.textList: An array of text, at most limits.listMaxItems long and at least minItems (0 when absent).
fieldTypes.date: An ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) that exists, optionally followed by a time and a UTC offset.
fieldTypes.integer: A whole number within min and max when they are given.
fieldTypes.object: An object holding exactly the named fields. atLeastOneOf: of the fields it names, at least one holds a non-empty list or a text.
fieldTypes.objectList: An array of such objects, at most limits.listMaxItems long and at least minItems.
fieldTypes.strictness: A required field that is absent is an error, a key no schema names is an error, and an optional field that is present is held to its type. null reads as absent. Every error names its field by path, such as fields.alternatives[0].whyRejected.

entryContent.title: Required text, at most limits.titleMaxChars characters.
entryContent.summary: Required text, at most limits.summaryMaxChars characters: one sentence, the one cards and the agent slice show.
entryContent.topics: Optional, at most limits.topicsMax topic slugs (space.slug's pattern). Anchor paths also place an entry under a topic through wiki_topic.path_prefixes.
entryContent.aliases: Optional, at most limits.aliasesMax synonyms, each at most limits.aliasMaxChars characters: Chinese and English spellings of the same idea, which is what keyword search matches on besides the text.
entryContent.anchors: Optional, at most limits.listMaxItems, each shaped as anchorTypes says.
entryContent.kindIsFixed: A lineage keeps its kind. Another kind is a supersede, which starts a new lineage.

symbol.check: runner: git grep -n finds the symbol, and the hash of the lines after it is compared with regionSha256. A hot file is anchored by symbol, never whole.

commit.check: runner: git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main. It is checked every run, but for one last found verified whose sha the snapshot's commits still hold, which could only answer verified again (anchorRules.verify.skip): a sha that is not an ancestor poisons what depends on it.

criterion.check: server: the criterion's semanticHash is compared.

merge_evidence.check: server: is that evidence still observed.

command.check: the maintenance run runs it again (phase 2).

anchorRules.stored: The server keeps each anchor's last check beside it (its state, the ref it was checked on and when). A proposer never sends those: an anchor carrying a key its type does not name is refused WIKI_SCHEMA.
anchorRules.gitOnRunner: A check that needs git runs on a runner: the anchors repository operation a maintenance run asks of the space's runner (repoOps.kinds.anchors, phase 2). The apiserver runs no git.
anchorRules.invalidates: changed or missing takes the entry out of the push at once and files a system challenge for Review, where the owner re-confirms (a new baseline), amends or retires it.

verify.typesNote: The anchors git can check. The other four are the server's or a recipe run's to check, and no check writes them yet: an entry that carries one reads unchecked until one does (aggregate).
verify.who: The space's maintenance run — the server's maintain job (maintenance.job.server.anchors) — and nothing else: no door lists a space's anchors or takes a report since P11 (2026-10-19). What a check writes takes entries out of the push and files challenges in the owner's Review.

query.after: optional: the next a page gave; the page starts after that entry
query.limit: optional: entries a page carries, 1 to rules.listEntriesMax, default rules.listEntriesDefault

list.answers: The space's active entries that carry at least one git anchor, in id order: each with its current revision and its git anchors, each anchor with its index in the entry's anchors and, for a symbol, the regionSha256 it is held to (null before its first check found one). A proposal waiting in Review is not listed: it is checked once it applies. next names the last entry of the page while more remain.

body.ref: required: the 40-character sha refs/remotes/origin/main named after the fetch, the commit every check was made on
body.entries: required: 1 to rules.reportEntriesMax of { entryId, revision (as the list gave it), checks: [{ index, type, state, regionSha256 (a symbol found, and only that), identity? }] }, identity the anchor the check says it checked — a path for a path anchor, path+symbol for a symbol, the 40-character sha for a commit, each only its type names

report.identity: A check is written only on the anchor its identity names: the type and every identity field it carries must be the anchor's own at the reported index. A check that carries no identity is held to the type at the index alone. A check naming another anchor — another path, symbol or commit than the one at the index — is never written: its entry answers stale, nothing of it is written, and the maintenance run that carried the report fails, so a verdict a page-mate's index would have stolen is reported, not recorded.
report.each: Every entry is recorded on its own, in a transaction of its own, and answered recorded (with the entry's anchorState, trust, challenged, and the challenge this report filed or null), stale, or refused. An entry no longer active, no longer at the revision named, without an anchor of the reported type at a reported index, or whose check names an anchor different from the one at its index is stale: nothing of it is written, and the next run reads it again. A malformed entry is refused WIKI_SCHEMA naming its field; an entry of another space is refused 404.
report.status: A report that recorded an entry, or found one stale, answers 200. One every entry of which was refused answers the status of its first refusal, every outcome in the body. A report whose ref or entries do not have this shape is refused WIKI_SCHEMA whole.

verify.page: The server's own maintenance job hands the runner one page's anchors as ONE flat list, each anchor numbered by its place in that list, and maps each verdict back through that numbering to (entry, the anchor's place in its entry). The per-entry index alone is not unique across a page: mapping verdicts by it lays one entry's verdict on another, which is how the 2026-10-08 canary wrote a page-mate's checks onto entries and failed two runs.
verify.skip: A maintenance run leaves an entry alone — sends none of it to the runner, writes none of it — when every git anchor of it still holds at the commit the run is checking (anchorHoldsAt). An anchor holds when its last check was made on exactly that commit — check.ref equal to the snapshot's sha, character for character: a check's answer depends on the anchor and what the commit holds of it, so a second one there could only write what the first wrote, and this is what a run that replays after a REPO_OP_WAIT, or one on a space whose main has not moved, saves. It also holds (2026-10-10) when its last check found it verified on another commit — check.ref a 40-character sha — since which nothing its answer depends on has moved: a path, which the runner only asks to be there (checks.path), when the diff from check.ref to the snapshot's commit (git diff --name-status -M, repoOps.kinds.diff) names neither the path nor anything under it as anything but a modification — an A, a D, a T, either side of an R or the new side of a C checks it again, an M does not; a symbol held to the baseline its check adopted, when that diff names neither its file nor anything under it at all, an M included, since its region is read from the content; a commit, when the snapshot's commits (repoOps.kinds.snapshot: git rev-list of its sha) hold it, which is what git merge-base --is-ancestor answers for it. A path is matched as the runner spells it (checks.path); one that leaves nothing, or holds a . or .. part, never holds across commits. The diffs: one to the snapshot's commit from each other commit it reaches that the space's verified paths and symbols were last checked at, the commits most such anchors were checked at first and at most maintenance.job.server.rules.anchorDiffsMax of them, each asked once the one before it has settled; a diff the runner could not make vouches for nothing. Four, because a diff is one more operation (~1.6 s) and pays for itself only when it spares more than ~26 anchors' checks (~0.06 s each): replayed over the canary's 19 rounds of 2026-10-08/10 (11,565 anchors, 653 commits of main), four averaged ~44 s a round, eight ~47 s and no cap ~53 s, against ~763 s for checking them all. Everything else is checked again: an anchor never checked, a check whose ref is not a sha, one made on a commit past the cap or that the snapshot does not reach, one that found its anchor missing or changed — a missing path or commit may come back, and the challenge a broken entry files is the check's to file — and a symbol that names its own regionSha256 — a proposer's, or the region a Re-confirm wrote — because a Re-confirm leaves exactly the shape a plain check leaves and nothing on the anchor tells the two apart; the run prefers the check it can prove over the round it would save. On its own commit a symbol holds only when the check records the baseline it was compared against (check.baselineSha256, which a check writes only for an anchor that named no regionSha256 of its own) and that is still the baseline the anchor names (symbolBaseline). An entry any of whose anchors does not hold is re-checked whole, as it always was (anchorsDueAt), and its checks move onto the run's commit. An entry left alone is not written: its checks, anchor_checked_ref and anchor_checked_at stay those of the check that was made, so no ref is moved forward and no write is spent on an entry nothing happened to; since what is checked lands on the run's commit and what is past the cap is checked, a run leaves the paths and symbols it skipped on at most anchorDiffsMax commits besides its own. The entries that still owe a check go out together, whichever page they were read on, at most rules.listEntriesMax an operation.
verify.fetch: The runner fetches origin's main into refs/remotes/origin/main first (git fetch origin +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main) and checks every anchor on the commit that ref then names. A fetch that fails checks nothing and reports nothing.

checks.path: git cat-file -e <ref>:<path>, the path taken without a leading ./ or / and without a trailing /: found is verified, and not found is missing.
checks.symbol: git grep -n -w -F -I finds the first line, in the file (or in the first file under the path, in path order), on which the symbol occurs as a whole word. Its region is that line and the lines after it, rules.symbolRegionLines in all or fewer at the end of the file, each ended by a newline, and regionSha256 is the sha256 of the region in lowercase hex. No such line is missing. The server holds a found symbol to its baseline (baseline): the same hash is verified, any other changed.
checks.commit: git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> <ref>: an ancestor is verified. Anything else — a sha that is not an ancestor of origin/main, or one this repository does not have at all — is missing: a sha that is not on main poisons whatever depends on it.

verify.baseline: A symbol anchor is held to its own regionSha256. One that names none is held to the region its first check found, which that check adopts and keeps as its baselineSha256. A check that finds the symbol changed or missing never moves the baseline: only the owner's Re-confirm (answers.reconfirm) does.
verify.check: Each reported anchor's last check is kept beside it in wiki_entry.anchors, as check: { state, ref, at } and, for a symbol found, regionSha256 (what this check found) and baselineSha256 (the baseline a check adopted). A revision stores its anchors as they were written, without it, and an amend's conflict answer shows them the same way.
verify.aggregate: wiki_entry.anchor_state is missing when any anchor's last check is missing, else changed when any is changed, else unchecked when any anchor has no check or the entry has no anchor, else verified; anchor_checked_ref and anchor_checked_at are the ref and the time of the last check. applyOp writes them and nothing else does (storage.singleWriter): a check, and an amend that gives the anchors anew, which leaves them unchecked unless they carry the checks Re-confirm kept.
verify.challenge: A check that leaves an active entry changed or missing takes it out of the push at once (push.eligible.anchorStateNot) and, while no challenge of it is open, files one system challenge in the same transaction: a changeset of origin maintenance with no session, written through the one write entry point, whose challenge op says in its reason which anchors no longer hold and the ref they were checked on. It counts against no session's quota. While any challenge of the entry is open, no second one is filed.

answers.reconfirm: decide action reconfirm: the entry is kept as it stands on the ref its anchors were last checked on. A symbol whose region changed is held to the region that check found, written as its own regionSha256, and an anchor that check found missing is dropped — in a revision of the owner's, with the entry's sources, when that changed anything. It touches the anchors and nothing else, so a decision, which is never otherwise rewritten, is re-confirmed the same way. An entry whose trust is auto or unreviewed becomes confirmed. The challenge is accepted, and the entry is back in the push once nothing else holds it out.
answers.amend: decide action amend, with edited shaped as an amend's changes (at least one key): the owner's changes laid over the entry as the owner's revision, with the entry's sources, and confirmed as Re-confirm confirms. Anchors the changes leave alone are re-baselined as Re-confirm would; anchors the changes give are new and unchecked. A kind that is never rewritten (a decision) is refused WIKI_SCHEMA. The challenge is edited.
answers.retire: decide action retire: the owner's own retire of the entry at its current revision, recorded through the one write entry point with the note as its reason (or the challenge's reason when there is no note). The challenge is withdrawn with the entry, as every op of an entry that leaves active is.
answers.only: The three answer a challenge op and nothing else: on any other op they are refused WIKI_SCHEMA. A challenge of an entry that is not active any more is recorded conflict and applies nothing. accept, edit and reject keep their meaning for a challenge too.

verify.tiered: The Tiered pitfall rule reads anchor_state (reviewModes.tiered.auto.machineVerified.pitfall), so a check is how an add qualifies: a check that leaves verified a pitfall the Tiered mode applied as unreviewed — live, not tainted, its current revision the one a tiered op wrote — while the space is still Tiered makes it auto in the same transaction, when that op's own sources span rules.pitfallMinSessions independent sessions.

anchorStates.unchecked: not checked yet: the state of every new anchor
anchorStates.verified: the last check found it as recorded
anchorStates.changed: the last check found it, but not as recorded
anchorStates.missing: the last check did not find it

sourceKinds.turn: a conversation turn; { kind: 'turn', session: 'self' } cites the calling session
sourceKinds.evidence: a revision of a task's completion evidence
sourceKinds.note: an owner's note, or an imported file (phase 2)
sourceKinds.url: a web page: only for an assumption (phase 3), and it taints the entry

sourceInput.ref: The cited record's id, or a commit's sha: what each kind takes is refs. An id is either spelling of one, the UUID or the short public id Orbit shows. Required, except by a turn that cites the calling session. A ref of a rowIdKinds kind that is neither spelling of an id is refused WIKI_SCHEMA, errors[] naming it by its path (ops[i].sources[j].ref), and a ref is never compared with a row's id as it came.

refs.turn: the turn's id; a turn of the calling session takes no ref, and is { kind: 'turn', session: 'self' }
refs.tool_call: the tool call's id, or the tool_use_id its engine gave the call (toolu_…, call_…), which is the id a session reads in its own transcript and the one task_evidence_submit takes: the calling session's own call, or else the call of the one session of this owner's that made it
refs.evidence: nothing yet: no door resolves an evidence source
refs.owner_decision: the id of the project blocker the owner resolved with a note
refs.criterion: nothing yet: no door resolves a criterion source
refs.commit: the commit's full sha, as a merge receipt of this owner's carries it
refs.note: the note's id, as orbit wiki import registered it
refs.url: nothing yet: only an assumption cites a url, and assumptions are phase 3

sourceInput.toolUseId: A tool_call's ref is read as the tool call's id first, and as a tool_use_id when no tool call of this owner's has that id: the calling session's own call carrying it, else the call of the one other session of this owner's that carries it. A call recorded more than once in one session is one call, read from its first row; a tool_use_id no session carries, or that two sessions carry, is unresolved. What is stored is the row's id.
sourceInput.session: Only the word self, and only on a turn: the calling session. Its current turn may not be stored yet, so its quote is verified when the session settles, and the Review card says whether it was.
sourceInput.seq: Only beside session self: the event sequence number it cites, an integer from 0.
sourceInput.locator: Optional object: where in the record, such as a sequence range or a field name.
sourceInput.quote: Optional text, at most limits.quoteMaxChars characters, redacted before it is stored.

sourceRules.firstHand: A source is a first-hand record. A wiki entry, a topic summary or any other view is never a source: citing knowledge with knowledge is how retrieval collapses into itself.
sourceRules.resolution: Every source resolves among the owner's own rows, or the op is refused WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED, errors[] naming the source by its path and the message saying what its kind's ref is (sourceInput.refs).
sourceRules.quote: A quote, whitespace-normalized, is a substring of the text of the record it cites, or the op is refused WIKI_QUOTE_NOT_FOUND.
sourceRules.required: A non-owner add, amend, supersede or reinforce cites at least one source: a claim that cannot be cited is not ready (WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED). The owner's own writes may cite none.
sourceRules.attachedTo: A source row hangs on the revision it supports. A reinforce adds rows to the entry's current revision and changes nothing else.
sourceRules.url: Only an assumption may cite a url, and such a source is always tainted.

transitions.trigger: the session it cites went to Trash: its entries leave the push, and are kept because the session can come back
that session was restored from Trash
that session was purged
the record it cites was hard-deleted or purged

sourceStates.deleted: Delete means forget: in the transaction that deletes the record, quote and quote_sha256 become NULL, and a confirmed entry that no live source supports any more is marked unsupported and leaves the push. The owner's own entries are not touched.

body.path: required: where the file was read, relative to the directory the import named; at most rules.notePathMaxChars characters
body.text: required: the file's text; at most rules.noteMaxChars characters
body.readBy: required: server — the server reads the note (import.server). A body without it — an orbit wiki import that predates server execution, and would read the note with the session's own model — is refused WIKI_SERVER_EXECUTES before anything is registered (import.server.door).

note.redaction: The text and the path go through src/apiserver/src/common/secret-redaction.ts, with the owner's workspace.env values as literals, BEFORE anything is stored or hashed. Only the redacted text, its sha256 and the redacted path are kept: never the text as it was sent.
note.dedup: One content is one note in a space: UNIQUE (space_id, content_sha256), the sha256 of the redacted text. Registering a text the space already holds — the same file imported again, or the same text under another name — answers the note already there with created false, and makes no row.
note.answer: { id, spaceId, path, contentSha256, chars, redacted, created }: no text — the server reads it (import.server), and no session's model does.
note.who: A session this runner hosts for its owner (X-Orbit-Session-Id; a headless call is refused 400), into one of that owner's spaces (another owner's is a plain 404). A verifier, foreman or judgment session is refused WIKI_SESSION_EXCLUDED.

import.source: A note is cited as { kind: note, ref: <the note's id>, quote? }. It resolves only among its owner's notes — another owner's note is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED, as their turn or task is — and its text is the stored, redacted text: what a quote is checked against (sourceRules.quote) and what an automatic space's verifier reads. Its locator is { path }, the file it came from. A note is second-hand content an agent wrote, never the owner's own words (reviewModes.tiered), and a verdict that read nothing else is capped at unreviewed (reviewModes.verification.evidence.secondHand).

propose.made: By the server's import job alone (import.server.propose): since P11 (2026-10-19) no route takes an import's ops. POST /api/runner/wiki/spaces/:id/imports, which took what a session's own model had read, is gone, and a runner that still calls it is answered 404.
propose.origin: import, decided by the job and never by an op's field. What it records is treated as an agent's is (effectPolicy.origins.import): Manual keeps every add for Review, Tiered applies it as unreviewed, Automatic sends it to its verification, which the server's verify job runs for the calling session (reviewModes.verification.who.server) — and every floor holds (reviewModes.floors): a principle is refused WIKI_KIND_OWNER_ONLY, a tainted op waits, the circuit breaker counts, and no changeset holds more than limits.opsPerChangeset ops.
propose.who: The session that ran orbit wiki import (import.server.create.who) is recorded on the changeset: the ops that wait for their verification are verified as that session's, and limits.opsPerTurn and limits.opsPerSession count what of them waits for review.

cli.command: orbit wiki import --from <dir|file> --space <id> [--max-ops N] [--concurrency N] [--state FILE] [--json]
cli.tool: none: a CLI verb with no MCP tool beside it. It reads files on the machine it runs on and waits for the server's job, which is a runner's work rather than a tool call's.
cli.precondition: Import only the files the owner asked for, into the space they named, and never write an entry yourself: each entry is the System model's, read on the Orbit server from the file's redacted text, and it takes effect only as the space's review mode says.
cli.does: Registers each file that is not yet a note (import.note) and hands the notes to one import job of the server (import.server), which asks the System model for at most rules.entriesPerNote entries a note, checks the run's ops with a dry run and proposes the ones that passed (import.propose): at most rules.opsPerRun ops a run. The command waits for the job and prints its report (import.server.cli).
cli.files: A file is imported as it is. A directory is its *.md files directly inside it, the ones whose frontmatter says they are the owner's own guidance first (type feedback, then user, reference, project, then the rest), each group by name; MEMORY.md, a memory library's index, is left out. A file already imported, or holding a text the space already has, is not proposed from again.
cli.principles: A principle is the owner's alone (reviewModes.floors.principleOwnerOnly): the model is asked for none, and one it writes anyway is not proposed, only counted.
cli.batches: A dry run checks the run's ops first. An op refused for what it says is dropped and counted; from the first one refused for room — WIKI_QUOTA, or WIKI_REVIEW_QUEUE_FULL — the rest wait for a later run. What needs review therefore reaches Review a batch at a time, as limits.opsPerTurn, limits.opsPerSession and limits.pendingOpsPerSpace allow, never hundreds at once.
cli.resume: It remembers on the machine it runs on ($ORBIT_HOME/wiki-import, or --state) which files it registered, what the model found in each and which ops it proposed: a run picks up where the last one stopped, a file already imported is not sent to the model again, and one whose text changed is imported as the new note it is. A batch is proposed under an idempotency key made of its space and its ops, so one sent again after a lost answer writes nothing twice.

server.why: The import's model is the server's (design section 0): orbit wiki import runs on the runner, reads the files and their frontmatter and registers each as a note, and the entries are read by the deployment's System model in an `import` job of the wiki-worker (jobs.kindRuns.import); the command waits for the job and prints its report. No key, subscription or provider of the session's is spent, and the session needs none.
server.door: The note route takes only a body that says readBy server, and answers it without the text. One without it — an orbit wiki import that predates server execution, and would read the note with the session's own model — is refused WIKI_SERVER_EXECUTES before anything is registered, so that command stops at its first registration, before it has asked any model anything. No route takes the entries a session's own model read (import.propose.made).

executor.answer: { executor: server, model, modelState }: the path this account's import takes — the server's, always, since P11 (2026-10-19), where a server before it could answer runner — and the System model's name and state as systemModel.read says them, never its address or key.
executor.olderServer: Any answer but server — runner, from a server that left the account's wiki on its runners, or a 404 that names no refusal and no space, from a server without this route — is a server too old for the command, which says so and registers nothing: it has no model of its own to read with. Another 404 (a space that is not the caller's, a wiki that is off) or any other refusal is reported as it is, and nothing is registered either.

create.body: { id, maxOps, concurrency?, checkoutRoot?, notes: [{ noteId, file, date, ops?: [{ index, body }] }] }. id is the job's, named by the command (a uuid or a public id), so a request sent again after a lost answer is answered with the job it already made; maxOps is 1 to rules.opsPerRun; concurrency is the notes read at once, 1 to maxConcurrency (defaultConcurrency when left out); checkoutRoot is the git root of the directory the command ran in, if any; notes are in the order the run would read them, at most maxNotes, each the note's id as import.note answered it, the file's path as the command names it, its date (YYYY-MM-DD: the frontmatter's modified, else the file's time) and — for a note an earlier run read — the ops it found and did not propose, each at its index in that run's list.
create.rules: Every note must be one of this space's (another space's, or another owner's, is a WIKI_SCHEMA field error naming it); a body that is not this shape is WIKI_SCHEMA with every field named. The job is made with kind import, priority `priority`, the calling session in its input.
create.who: As import.note.who: a session this runner hosts for its owner; the calling session is what the job proposes as.

read.answer: { id, spaceId, state, waitingFor, attempts, error, failureKind, progress, report, createdAt, startedAt, endedAt, model: { name, state } } — the job row as jobs says it, and the System model's name and state so a command waiting on it can say why it waits.
read.who: Any session this runner hosts for the space's owner — a later run in another session collects a job an earlier one left — and a 404 for another owner's job or another space's.

server.systemPrompt: You compile durable engineering knowledge from one note about a code repository into wiki entries. You output only a JSON array.
server.reads: Each note to read is one request through the queue (modelQueue): step `steps.read`, unit the note's id, the system prompt above, max_tokens maxTokens, and the prompt orbit wiki import sent on the runner before P11, word for word (wikiImportPrompt: what is worth an entry, the one flat shape, the fictional example, the note under its path and date, and — for a note whose prose is Chinese — the language named last). Notes are read `concurrency` at a time, in order, until the run has maxOps ops; the queue's own perJob cap still holds what is in flight. A replayed job meets the rows it made: a note answered before is not asked again.
server.checks: As the runner checked before P11: the answer's JSON array is found bare, in a fence, wrapped as {entries}, or after reasoning, and mended (an unescaped quote in a quote, a trailing comma); the JSON is read as encoding/json reads it — the {entries} wrapper's key in any case, a lone surrogate in a string or key U+FFFD, a number past float64's range failing the whole parse, not reading as Infinity; each entry is held to its kind's fields, a title to the note's language when it is Chinese, a recipe's verify.command to a command the note writes in its code, a quote to the note's own words (else the note is cited with no quote); a principle is counted and never proposed; a second entry of one title is dropped; at most rules.entriesPerNote ops a note. An answer that does not parse, or entries that do not hold up, are asked about once more (step `steps.retry`) with what was wrong, and a note whose answers never parse is failed — not read again. A request the queue ends as no outage (the call's budget, a refusal the model gives for what was sent) fails its note the same way; one the platform could not finish (the wait limit) fails the job as infra, and the retried job asks again (modelQueue.identity).
server.deterministic: src/shared/src/wiki-import.fixture.json holds what the runner's Go code made of a set of notes and answers before P11 — the prompt, a note's language, the reading of an answer, a quote, a verify command, the ops and problems an answer becomes and the retry that names them, a path anchor — as its Go test wrote it, and src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-import-golden.spec.ts holds the server's implementation to it byte for byte. Where the server's reading of a note was let differ from the runner's in P10 (wikiImportNote), the server's is the one in force: nothing of the Go code is ported back.

snapshot.rule: The anchors are held to the space's snapshot (repoOps) instead of a checkout: a path its origin/main tree has, file or directory — an absolute one read under checkoutRoot, an Orbit worktree, or a directory named for the space's repository — and a commit origin/main reaches, a prefix of seven or more characters naming exactly one. When the space's repository can be read now (readiness ready), the job asks for a fresh snapshot (skipSha the one it holds, under an operation id made from the job's) and waits for it holding its lease, at most waitSeconds; otherwise, or when the snapshot fails or does not come in time, it holds the anchors to the snapshot the space already holds; with none, the anchors are left out. Only a job with a note to read asks.
snapshot.report: report.snapshot is { sha, fresh } of the snapshot the anchors were held to — fresh when it is the one this job asked for — or null.

server.propose: As import.cli.batches: the run's ops (at most maxOps, in note order) are checked with a dry run, and the ones that passed proposed in one changeset through WikiService.submitChangeset as the calling session, origin import, under idempotencyKey wiki-import:<the first 40 hex of sha256(space id, a newline, the ops as Go's json.Marshal writes them)> — a replay of the job, or a run that carries a batch whose answer was lost, writes nothing twice. The rationale names the System model and the notes. An op refused for what it says is dropped and counted; from the first refused for room (WIKI_QUOTA, WIKI_REVIEW_QUEUE_FULL) the rest wait for a later run, and a run that could propose nothing for want of room says so in summary.stopped. A refusal of the whole request fails the job as content.
server.report: { kind: import, model, snapshot, summary: { notes, read, entries, principles, dropped, failed, proposed, applied, pending, verifying, refused, deferred, calls, inputTokens, outputTokens, refusals[{file, title, code, why}], stopped }, notes: [{ file, noteId, status: read | failed | carried, why?, principles?, dropped?, ops: [{ index, body?, outcome: '' | applied | pending | verifying | refused, why?, opId?, entryId? }] }] }. A note read this run lists every op it gave (outcome '' for one with no room this run); a carried note lists the ops it carried; a note the run did not reach is absent. The summary's numbers are what the command prints.
server.progress: While it runs the job writes progress { step: snapshot | reading | proposing, notes, read, failed, ops } under its lease generation (jobs.progress).
server.cli: The command asks the executor route first, and goes on only when it answers server (executor.olderServer). It registers the files that are not yet notes (readBy server), hands the job every note to read and every note carrying ops in one create (at most maxNotes; the rest wait for the next run), writes the job's id into its memory before it waits, polls the read route, and on success writes the report into its memory as import.cli.resume keeps it — so the next run, on either path, picks up where this one stopped — and prints the report's numbers. It stops waiting, leaving the job to the server and its id in its memory, when the System model refuses the deployment's key (auth_failed) or is not configured, when the model has not been up, or the job has not started, for ten minutes, and when the job has failed three times over (its attempts); the next run collects that job before it makes another. A failed job leaves its notes registered for the next run's job. No ANTHROPIC_* variable and no Claude Code are needed.

born.proposed: an add or supersede that waits for review, or an add that waits for its verification (reviewModes.verification)
born.active: an add or supersede that applied at once: the owner's own, or an add the space's review mode applied (trust auto or unreviewed)

entry.endedMeans: No longer live: never pushed, never searched by an agent, and what a client shows as ended. A rejected lineage is ended without being terminal, because the one reopening a verification allows (reviewModes.verification.reopen) proposes it again.

transitions.trigger: the owner accepted the op that proposed it, as written or edited; or its verification found it supported (trust auto) or partly supported (trust unreviewed)
the owner rejected that op, or it expired or was withdrawn; or its verification found it unsupported or a duplicate. The row stays, as a counter-example the next similar[] shows with its reason
a supersede naming it applied; superseded_by_id names the successor, whose supersedes_id names it
a retire naming it applied

the owner rejected an entry the review mode applied at once and nobody has confirmed (trust auto or unreviewed): on its spot check, or from the entry itself. It stays as a counter-example, like a rejected proposal

the verdict that rejected it was reopened (reviewModes.verification.reopen): an unsupported verdict given when none of its sources could be read. It waits for its verification again. Every other rejection is final

invariants: superseded exactly when superseded_by_id is set
retired_at is set exactly when the status is ended (superseded, retired or rejected)
trust is proposed exactly when the status is proposed or rejected

transitions.trigger: its verification found it supported or partly supported, and the verdict applied it (reviewModes.verification.verdicts)
the verdict applied it and the draw made it a spot check (reviewModes.spotChecks.automatic): its effect stands, and the owner is asked to check it
its verification found it unsupported (not_true) or a duplicate of an entry the space holds (duplicate)
an amend whose entry moved, or passed into the owner's hands, before its verdict arrived: nothing applied
the owner reverted the run it belongs to, or an amend's entry left active, before its verdict arrived
the owner accepted it and it applied; on a spot check, the owner confirmed what the review mode applied
the owner edited it, accepted the edit, and the edit applied
the owner rejected it, naming one of rejectReasons; on a spot check, what the review mode applied is undone
the owner accepted it, but its baseRevision was no longer the entry's current revision, so nothing applied; on a spot check, the entry had changed since the op applied
it waited limits.pendingExpiryDays days
its entry left active before the owner decided it (another op superseded or retired it, or a revert undid it), so it can no longer apply
the owner rejected, from the entry itself, the add the review mode applied at once (reviewModes.entryReject)
the owner confirmed, from the entry itself, the entry the review mode applied it to (reviewModes.entryConfirm). Every other auto_applied op stays as it is
a tainted add or amend that waited for the owner was sent to its verification, in a space that is automatic now (reviewModes.verification.reopen)

its verdict was reopened (reviewModes.verification.reopen): an unsupported verdict given when none of its sources could be read, which moves into its verification_history. Every other rejection is final

invariants: decided_at is set exactly when the decision is neither pending nor verifying
decision_reason is set exactly when the decision is rejected, and is one of rejectReasons
an op waiting for its verification carries no verdict, and only an add or an amend ever waits for one or carries one
verification_history is a list, empty for every op never reopened, and holds each earlier verdict of one that was, oldest first

transitions.trigger: the last of its pending or verifying ops was decided, verified, expired or withdrawn
one of its ops was sent back to its verification (reviewModes.verification.reopen): it waits again, with a fresh expires_at, until nothing of it does

invariants: decided_at is set exactly when the changeset is settled
a pending changeset has an expires_at
changeset.note: A changeset is pending while any of its ops waits — for the owner, or for its verification — and settled once none does. One every op of which applied at once is settled when it is recorded. A request none of whose ops passed records no changeset at all. Review lists a pending changeset only while one of its ops waits for the owner: one that waits for its verification alone is not in it.

meaning.owner: the owner wrote it: an owner's own add or supersede
meaning.confirmed: an agent, a maintenance run, an import or a watch proposed it and the owner accepted it, as written or edited — or accepted its spot check, or confirmed it from the entry itself (reviewModes.entryConfirm), or applied a card of a chat (reviewModes.chat)
meaning.auto: the space's review mode applied it and no person has looked: Tiered for the owner's own words or a machine-verified entry, Automatic for what its verification found supported by the sources, a note's words alone not counting. Pushed; labelled Auto
meaning.unreviewed: Tiered applied it at once without the owner's words or a machine verification behind it; Automatic's verification found its sources support it only in part, could read none of them, or verified what a session that read the web proposed (reviewModes.verification.evidence); a revert or a rejected spot check restored it; or the close of a history backfill found it resting on a note with nothing first-hand beside it (maintenance.job.server.backfill.downgrade). Shown, labelled Unreviewed, and never pushed
meaning.proposed: not accepted: every proposed entry and every rejected one
meaning.external: it rests on web-derived sources (a phase-3 assumption citing a url). Never pushed

onApply.reviewModeAddOrAmend: auto or unreviewed (reviewModes.effect); in Automatic, what the verdict says (reviewModes.verification.verdicts): supported auto, partial unreviewed, and no more than unreviewed where its evidence caps it (reviewModes.verification.evidence)
onApply.chatApplied: confirmed: the owner's Apply or Edit of a chat's card (reviewModes.chat); a principle's is owner, the owner's own write

trust.edited: An owner who edits a proposal before accepting it is recorded as the author of the revision that results, and the entry's trust is still confirmed.

add.creates: a new lineage at revision 1: proposed, or active when it applies at once

reinforce.does: adds sources to the entry's current revision; content, status and trust stay as they are

keys.changes: required: any of title, summary, fields, topics, aliases, anchors; a key given replaces that key whole, a key omitted carries over from baseRevision

amend.does: a new revision of the same lineage; the kind stays

supersede.does: a new lineage that replaces the named one; when it applies, the named entry becomes superseded

retire.does: the entry leaves active for retired

challenge.does: sets challenged, which takes the entry out of the push at once. The owner answers it in Review: Re-confirm, Amend or Retire

opRules.promptedBy: The agent's note an op came from, { eventId, file }: the tool_use event that wrote it and the memory file's name, or { noteId, file } for an imported note a backfill named (maintenance.job.server.backfill) or for a session's wiki_note (agentSurface.note), whose row it names since one filed through the CLI has no event of its own, and whose file is wiki_note, in wiki_changeset_op.prompted_by (storage.promptedByMigration). The server's own field: only the space's maintenance run sets it, on the ops of its pass over the notes (maintenance.job.server.claims), through an argument of the writer no door hands on, and an op that carries the key is refused for its shape (WIKI_SCHEMA), whoever sends it. It is no source. It decides the op's evidence (reviewModes.verification.evidence.promptedBy) and is read for measurement and tracing; no read of an op shows it.
opRules.compareAndSet: amend, supersede and retire name the revision they were written against, and apply only while it is still the entry's current revision; otherwise WIKI_REVISION_CONFLICT with the current revision and a diff. There is deliberately no "whatever is current" spelling, as task_evidence_decide's evidenceRevision has none.
opRules.seq: An op is numbered by its 0-based position in the request's ops, and every answer names it by that number.
opRules.reason: A retire or a challenge says why in reason, which Review shows beside it.

effectPolicy.why: Design section 4.2: only the owner's own writes and the two safe ops take effect at once; everything else waits for the owner in Review — unless the space's review mode applies it (reviewModes), which reads this policy first and changes nothing it applies.

effects.applied: takes effect in the submitting transaction; the op is recorded auto_applied
effects.pending: recorded pending, and shown in Review until the owner decides it or it expires
effects.appliedUnlessOff: applied, unless the space's settings.autoAcceptReinforce is false, then pending

effectPolicy.taintedRule: An op is tainted when the calling session used WebFetch or WebSearch (codex's webSearch too) before it, or when a turn it cites comes from a tainted stretch, or when a note it cites was written by a session that used them (agentSurface.note), or names, as originSessionId in its frontmatter, a session of this owner's that used them: that value is the engine's id, read against session.runtime_session_id, and a note that names none it can find is not tainted. A tainted op of any origin but owner follows the tainted row instead of its origin's row, and its Review card carries the Web-derived warning. In an automatic space the review mode sends a tainted add or amend to its verification instead of to Review (reviewModes.floors.taintedWaits).
effectPolicy.challengeRule: A challenge applies at once from every origin, tainted or not: it only raises a flag, and the flag's whole effect is to take the entry out of the push until the owner answers it.

decide.reject: names one of rejectReasons, and may add a note
decide.edit: carries the owner's version, shaped as an amend's changes over the proposal
decide.challengeAnswers: reconfirm, amend and retire answer a challenge op, and only a challenge op: anchorRules.verify.answers.

reviewModes.why: Owner, 2026-09-26: not every entry needs a person, and a space can run as Wikova's does, in an Automatic mode. What the effect policy holds back, a space's review mode may apply; everything it applies is written through submitChangeset and applyOp like any other write, keeps its revision history, and can be rejected one entry at a time or undone a run at a time. Owner, 2026-09-27 (criterion 7, revision 3): Automatic verifies before it applies — a model, called apart from the call that proposed the op — the deployment's System model, in the server's verify job (jobs.kindRuns.verify), since server execution — checks each op against its own sources, and nothing an Automatic space takes in is live until a verdict says so (verification). Owner, 2026-09-27 (criterion 7, revision 4): a verification has to be able to read its evidence (verification.evidence), and what a session that read the web proposed is verified too, but never past unreviewed (floors.taintedWaits).

meaning.manual: The effect policy and nothing else: an agent's, a maintenance run's and an import's add, amend, supersede and retire wait for the owner, as in phase 1.
meaning.tiered: An add or an amend applies at once. It is auto, and pushed, when it is the owner's own words or machine-verified (tiered); anything else it applies is unreviewed: shown, never pushed, and the owner may Reject it later.
meaning.automatic: An add or an amend that passed every check waits for its verification, and its verdict decides it (verification.verdicts): supported applies as auto and is pushed, partial applies as unreviewed, unsupported is rejected with its reason, and a duplicate becomes a reinforce of the entry it duplicates. A verdict about an op none of whose sources could be read, about one whose only readable source is a note, or about a tainted op, applies nothing past unreviewed (verification.evidence). Without a verdict nothing applies, and nothing of it waits in Review.

effect.rule: The effect policy decides first. What it applies (the owner's own write, a reinforce, a challenge) is untouched by the mode; what it holds back, a mode other than manual takes when the op is an add, or an amend of an entry whose trust is auto or unreviewed — and the floors let it. Tiered applies what it takes at once; automatic sends it to its verification. A supersede and a retire end a lineage, which no revert or Reject could bring back, so they wait for the owner in every mode, and so does a reinforce the space's autoAcceptReinforce holds back.
effect.recorded: An op tiered applied is recorded auto_applied with applied_by_mode naming the mode, and its entry's trust is the one the mode gives it (trust.onApply.reviewModeAddOrAmend). An op automatic takes is recorded verifying, with applied_by_mode NULL until a verdict applies it: an add's lineage is born proposed meanwhile, and an amend changes nothing yet.

auto.ownerWords: A decision or a convention one of whose sources is the owner's own words, with its quote verified against the record: a conversation turn the owner sent (a message or a steer the user door filed with an explicit routing intent, under a client turn id that is a UUID — the runner door files neither, and a server-made turn carries a namespaced id), or an AskUserQuestion the owner answered (an approval allowed by a person, with answers).

machineVerified.recipe: Its verify command re-ran green in a maintenance run. Nothing reports such a run yet, so no recipe qualifies until one does: the classifier takes the result as an input and is handed false.
machineVerified.pitfall: Its anchors re-verified (anchor_state verified) and its sources span at least rules.pitfallMinSessions independent sessions. A new entry's anchors are unchecked, so an add qualifies only once the anchor re-verification has run; an amend that leaves the anchors as they are keeps its entry's state.

floors.why: None of these is loosened by any mode.
floors.principleOwnerOnly: A principle is the owner's to write: an add, amend or supersede of one from anyone else is refused WIKI_KIND_OWNER_ONLY.
floors.taintedWaits: A tainted op is never applied past unreviewed on anybody's say-so but the owner's. In manual and tiered it waits for the owner (effectPolicy.tainted). In automatic an add or an amend no other floor holds waits for its verification like any other op, and its verdict leaves it no more than unreviewed (verification.evidence.tainted): never pushed, never read by an agent — the runner door's wiki_search and wiki_get do not return a live tainted entry whose trust is not owner or confirmed — and no place in pendingOpsPerSpace; an unsupported verdict still rejects it. What rests on a web-derived record reaches an agent only once a person has vouched for it: the owner's Confirm (entryConfirm), or their acceptance in Review (push.eligible.taintedOnlyWithTrust). The owner reads it in the app as any other entry.
floors.ownerVouchedWaits: An amend, supersede or retire of an entry the owner wrote or confirmed — trust owner or confirmed, or any revision of it the owner authored — waits for the owner.
floors.circuitBreaker: A changeset may change, through ops the review mode applies, at most rules.breakerMaxChangedPercent percent of the entries the space held active when it began; the op that would pass that is refused WIKI_QUOTA and applies nothing. A space holding fewer than rules.breakerMinActiveEntries active entries has no breaker, so an empty space can take its first batch. What is counted is the distinct entries such ops add or amend.
floors.opsPerChangeset: No request holds more than limits.opsPerChangeset ops: the one past it is refused WIKI_QUOTA.

verification.why: Owner, 2026-09-27: what a model proposed is checked by a second, separate call against the records it cites, and only what that check bears out goes live. Wikova's lesson rides with it: a verdict that cannot be read is no verdict, and lets nothing through.
verification.waits: An op automatic takes (an add, or an amend of an entry whose trust is auto or unreviewed, past every floor) is recorded verifying. It is not applied and not pushed; it is not a Review card, and it counts toward neither pendingOpsPerSpace nor opsPerTurn and opsPerSession; the circuit breaker and opsPerChangeset count it as they count any op a mode takes. Its proposer's answer calls it pending, with waitsFor verification.
verification.noClock: Nothing but a fact moves an op out of verifying: no clock expires, withdraws or applies it, and limits.pendingExpiryDays does not reach it, so it waits for its verdict however long that takes. What else ends the wait is itself a fact: the owner reverting its run (withdrawn), and for an amend its entry leaving active (withdrawn) or, by the time its verdict arrives, having moved or passed into the owner's hands (conflict).
verification.notAutomatic: A verdict is recorded only while the space is automatic. Once the owner, or the verification itself (fallback), has moved the space to another mode, a verdict is refused 409 and its op keeps waiting, untouched, until the space is automatic again or its run is reverted: a verdict computed under a mode the space has since left does not overrule the mode it is in.

verdicts.supported: The sources bear the whole of it out: the op applies — an add's lineage becomes active, an amend's revision is written — with trust auto, and it is pushed, unless what it read caps it at unreviewed (evidence).
verdicts.partial: The sources bear out only part of it: the op applies with trust unreviewed — shown, labelled Unreviewed, never pushed, and the owner may Reject it.
verdicts.unsupported: The sources do not bear it out: the op is rejected with decision_reason not_true, and the verifier's reason is in its trail. An add's lineage becomes rejected and stays as a counter-example: the next similar[] that finds it says rejectedReason not_true and, as rejectedBecause, the verifier's reason.
verdicts.duplicate: It says what an entry the space already holds says. duplicateOf names that entry — one of the op's own similar[], or an amend's own entry — and it must be active. The op is rejected with decision_reason duplicate (an add's lineage with it), and its sources are added to the named entry as a reinforce adds them, content, status and trust untouched — unless the space's autoAcceptReinforce is off, in which case nothing is added: a reinforce the owner reviews is one a session proposes.

verification.applies: A verdict applies through applyOp and recomputeFlags like every other write (storage.singleWriter): a promote for an add, an amend for an amend, a reject, a reinforce. An op a verdict applied is recorded auto_applied with applied_by_mode automatic, so revert, entryReject and the spot checks treat it as one the mode applied.

trail.rule: Every verdict leaves its trail on its op, the four together or none of them: which of verdicts, the verifier's reason in one sentence (redacted as every stored text is, at most rules.verificationReasonMaxChars), the model that gave it (at most rules.verificationModelMaxChars), and when the server recorded it; verification_duplicate_of exactly when the verdict is duplicate. An op reads it back as verification: {verdict, reason, model, at, duplicateOf, evidence}, null until a verdict arrives.

evidence.why: Owner, 2026-09-27 (criterion 7, revision 4): a verification has to be able to read its evidence. A verifier handed no text judges the claim alone, and its verdict is no verdict about the records: in the preview space 95.7% of the ops whose sources were all tool, thinking and system events were found unsupported, against 0.9% of the ops with one source whose text it could read.
evidence.text: Every source is read as its record's text, and it is the same text a submission's quote is checked against and a dossier line's spans count in (maintenance.dossier.spans). A run event: user, assistant and thinking, its text; tool_use, its tool's name and its input; tool_result, its content — a string, or the text of its blocks — marked when the tool reported an error; error, its message; background_task, its command and its summary; turn_end, its subtype; system, only the words it carries (text, notice, stderr), so a system event that is counts has none. A tool call's row is the call and its result together: its tool's name, its input, then its output — a string, the text of its blocks, or the text of the blocks of a result that carries them as content. An approval is its answers and the owner's note, a line each, and for an ExitPlanMode the plan it decided. Each is its parts, one per line, in that order (src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-verify-evidence.ts). Empty or blank text is none: an empty thinking is a record with nothing in it to read, not evidence that says nothing. A verifier is handed the text redacted by the shared redactor, then cut at rules.verificationSourceMaxChars.
evidence.mark: unreadable when none of the op's sources has text; second_hand when some have, and every one of them is a note, or when the op came from an agent's note and none of them is first-hand for it (promptedBy); readable otherwise. Each op of the list carries it (evidence), so a verifier knows before it asks a model; and the server reads it again when it records a verdict, never taking the verifier's word for it, and stores it with the verdict. NULL for a verdict recorded before migration 0314, and while there is no verdict.

classes.why: docs/wiki-memory-claims-design.md section 6.1 audited active auto entries by where their sources' words came from: only memory read 16.3 points worse than observed, the rest under its threshold of 10. So the mark caps what rests on a note alone, and no other class; the classes are named so that what comes after can read them by one table.
classes.strongest: Strongest first. An op's class is its strongest source's, by wikiStrongestEvidenceClass in src/shared/src/wiki.ts.
classes.observed: A tool_call, or a tool_use or tool_result event, of any tool but one that writes a file (Write, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, apply_patch, ApplyPatch), one whose input is what the agent typed (agentInputTools), a read of the wiki (maintenance.dossier.wikiReads), and one that files a note (maintenance.dossier.noteCalls); a background_task; an error; a commit; a merge receipt. A tool_result whose call was not recorded names no tool to hold against it, and counts.
classes.owner_words: A turn isOwnerTurn says is theirs, an approval isOwnerAnswer says is theirs, and a blocker the owner resolved with a note (owner_decision), though Tiered's ownerWords does not read that one.
classes.agent_words: An assistant or thinking event, a call of a tool that writes a file, reads the wiki or is one of agentInputTools by its name without what its engine files it under (mcp__<server>__, orbit__), a turn another session sent (sender_session_id), and a parent session's opening of its child.
classes.no_intent_words: Any other message or steer, a user event from before turns were stored, and an approval isOwnerAnswer does not claim.
classes.task_text: A task run's opening turn, a task and a task comment, the owner's own included.
classes.orbit_or_shell: A turn isOrbitAuthoredTurn says the control plane wrote, a shell or interrupt turn, and a turn_end or system event.
classes.function: wikiEvidenceClass in src/shared/src/wiki.ts; WikiService.sourceText gives each record's.

evidence.promptedBy: An op of the pass over an agent's notes (opRules.promptedBy) needs a source first-hand for the note it came from, or its verifier has read no more than the note says: its mark is second_hand, as secondHand then says, and its supported is no more than unreviewed. A source counts when the verifier could read its text and its class is in classes.firstHand. One whose class is observed does not count if the text the verifier is handed repeats at least 60 consecutive characters of the note's words (markdown marks aside, curly quotes straight, a run of whitespace one space; wikiRepeatsNote): a stored tool result can hold a memory file's words with no memory path near them. The owner's words count however much of them a note copies. The note's words are read again from the write or the imported note promptedBy names, and one that can no longer be read holds nothing against a source. Only this op's mark changes: an op from no note reads as it did, whatever its sources' classes.
evidence.secondHand: A verdict that read only a note is about the note: an entry drawn from one says its words, so its verifier can show only that they were copied (design section 1.1). Supported and partial apply the op as unreviewed; unsupported rejects it; a duplicate is a reinforce of the entry it names (verdicts.duplicate). All of them count toward the fallback, because the model did read text. A note beside a source with text is not second_hand, whatever that source's class; beside a source with none (an empty thinking, a commit, whose text this database does not hold) it is: that source's words are not what the verdict read.
evidence.unreadable: A verdict about an op none of whose sources could be read is capped at unreviewed: supported, partial and unsupported all apply the op as unreviewed — shown, labelled Unreviewed, never pushed — and a duplicate is still a reinforce of the entry it names (verdicts.duplicate). None of them counts toward the fallback.
evidence.tainted: A verdict about a tainted op (effectPolicy.taintedRule) is capped at unreviewed too: supported and partial apply it as unreviewed; unsupported rejects it, and counts; and a duplicate is rejected with nothing added to the entry it names, so what a session that read the web cites never changes whether an entry the space already holds is pushed (a pitfall's independent sessions, a source that keeps it supported).

who.runner: Only the session that proposed the ops: the runner door requires X-Orbit-Session-Id (a headless call is refused), and counts the ops of that session's alone that wait (servedBy) and asks for their verification (routes.request); another session's op, and anything of another owner's, is not there. No session reports a verdict.
who.import: The one-off import the API server's container runs as {origin: import, authorKind: system} calls WikiService.listVerifications and WikiService.recordVerifications directly, and reaches the ops of import changesets that name no session. Its verdicts leave the same trail and apply the same way.
who.maintenance: The space's maintenance run — its maintain job (maintenance.job.server) — also verifies, in the worker, what ended sessions and the space's ended runs left waiting there (adoption): the ops nobody else is left to verify.
who.server: The ops a session proposed are verified by the server's own job (jobs.kindRuns.verify, agentSurface.verify.serverExecution): it is not a session, and it writes as none — the identity it reports a verdict under is the PROPOSING session's, taken from the job's input, and its writes are authored system, because the server made them on its own account. The rule that only a session's own ops may be verified is unchanged: the job reaches exactly the ops of the session it names, and the read it works from is the list (verification.list) of that session's ops.

verification.list: What the server's verify job reads of a session's ops that wait for their verification in the space (WikiService.listVerifications), oldest first, after the op it names and at most rules.verificationListMax of them: each with its op, its kind, the entry as it would read once applied (an add's draft, an amend's changes laid over its entry), its sources each with the text of its record read now and redacted (at most rules.verificationSourceMaxChars of it, marked when cut), and its similar[] as recorded, each neighbour's title, status and trust read now.
