maintenance.backlog: The facts after the cursor (maintenance.cursor.backlog), counted from the facts as the read is made — the status line's N to catch up. Counted only while maintenance is on: a space that is off reads 0.
maintenance.oldestPendingAt: The oldest of those facts, or null; null too while maintenance is off.
maintenance.lagSeconds: How long ago that fact was, in whole seconds; 0 when there is none.
maintenance.dailyLimitReached: The space has made settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit maintenance runs since midnight UTC (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday), however they ended — but the runs made in catch-up that are not counted — and the next run would count: no fact makes another today. False while the space catches up and its latest run was on a local endpoint (maintenance.job.catchUp.dailyLimit), whose runs the day does not count.
maintenance.held: maintenance.job.held as the cursor row keeps it: {reason, at}, or null.
maintenance.running: The run under way — its row has started and not ended, and its job is queued, running or waiting — as {sessionId, jobId, startedAt}, or null: jobId the job that runs it (P9), sessionId null; startedAt is when its latest attempt started (maintenance.job.recovery.attempts). A run of the runner path, from before server execution, has no job and is under way no more.
maintenance.lastRun: The run that ended last, as {sessionId, jobId, outcome, endedAt}, or null: what View run opens — the run's row on Activity (jobs.read) by its job (P9). sessionId is a runner-path run's, from before server execution, whose session View run opens instead.
maintenance.lastFailure: Of the runs whose latest attempt failed — outcome failed or truncated — the one that ended last, as {kind, reason, at, sessionId}: kind is its failureKind (maintenance.job.recovery.failureKinds), reason its error, at when it ended; null while no run's latest attempt failed. What a client tells the platform failing from the run failing by. Beside them jobId (P9), as lastRun's.

health.look: The first that holds, in the order of looks: off — maintenance is off; failing — consecutiveFailures is more than 0; running — running is not null; behind — the oldest fact after the cursor is older than maintenance.rules.maxPendingAgeHours; ok — none of those (wikiMaintenanceLook).

notify.push: PushService.notifyWikiMaintenanceFailing: one alert to the owner's devices, kind wiki-maintenance-failing, thread wiki-<space>, no badge — nothing is waiting for a reply.
notify.once: Sent by the one failure report whose increment made consecutive_failures exactly afterFailures. The increment is one UPDATE … RETURNING on the cursor row, so of reports racing only one reads that number back, and the streak's later failures read more. After the statement, outside any transaction, best-effort: the failure is recorded whether or not the phone rang.
notify.reset: A succeeded run sets consecutive_failures back to 0, so the next streak is told once more, at its own third failure.

notifyNoNotes.why: Claude's memory could leave the session's events without anything failing (docs/wiki-memory-claims-design.md section 8): runs would go on succeeding and see no write.
notifyNoNotes.when: The runs that ended last, afterRuns of them in a row however each ended, each read at least minSessions sessions a Claude engine ran with no write to a memory file among them: report.claims.claudeSessions and report.claims.seen 0 (maintenance.job.report). A report with no claims, from before the pass was wired in, is no such run.
notifyNoNotes.push: PushService.notifyWikiMemoryWritesQuiet: one alert to the owner's devices, as notify.push says, under the same kind and thread, so that it opens the same space on every client.
notifyNoNotes.once: Sent by the end of the one run that makes the streak exactly afterRuns long, off the run rows; after the run's row is written, best-effort: no run fails for it.
notifyNoNotes.reset: A run that is not such a run ends the streak, and the next is told once more, at its own third.

health.client: The Wiki home's status line, on the web at every width and on iOS: after the entries, the review count (desktop only) and the anchors, the maintenance part in the space's look — the same words and the same parts on both, locked by src/shared/src/wiki-health.fixture.json.
health.executor: jobs.executor.read (P9): { mode: server, serverExecutes: true }, since P11 the same for every account. Absent from a control plane that predates it, which a client reads as not saying so: it draws none of the server's parts (jobs.executor.read.readBy).
health.systemModel: The System model as systemModel.read answers its state — { state, model, since, checkedAt, workerSeenAt }, never its address or key — read while executor.serverExecutes holds, which since P11 it always does; null from a control plane that left the account on the runner, where the model was none of the account's business.

articles.doc: docs/wiki-contract.md section 18; design section 3 wiki_topic_summary and section 12.1
articles.means: Each topic of a space has an article the System model wrote from the topic's active entries, every sentence footnoted to one of them; a topic with more entries than rules.splitAbove has an overview and subtopic articles instead. Articles are a view of the entries and a disposable cache (wiki_topic_summary): rewritten only when the topic's entry set changed, never pushed, never a source, and never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get.
articles.categoriesNote: The demo's six categories in the demo's order (平台核心, Runner 与引擎, 客户端与界面, 数据与后端, 工程流程, 协作), named in English as all copy is (AGENTS.md section 5) — and so are the default topics' display names (defaultTopics), which the demo wrote in Chinese. wiki_topic.category is one of the keys, CHECKed; the directory lists the categories in this order. A topic row seeded before the default topics were English keeps the name it was given.

kinds.article: part 0 of a topic that was not split: the topic's one article
kinds.overview: part 0 of a topic that was split: what the topic covers, pointing at its subtopic articles
kinds.subtopic: part 1 or later of a split topic: one group of its entries, hanging on the overview (parent_id)

articles.rulesNote: An article's length is counted in characters (Unicode code points) of its kept sentences, footnote markers and headings left out: the demo's measure, whose articles averaged 1,052 against a 400-900 target. The writer aims inside the range and asks again once when a draft falls short of minChars; the server cuts what passes maxChars (validation.cap). splitAbove, groupTarget, groupsMax and groupMin are the writer's grouping (the demo's), entriesPerArticle the most entries one article is written from.
articles.jobNote: The server's articles job (articles.serverExecution): step is the queue's step for every one of its calls, which gives them the default wait limit and call budget, 15 minutes each (modelQueue.waitLimit, modelQueue.callBudget); priority is background work (jobs.priority), and the job yields its space's next round of maintenance once with no change of priority; articleMaxTokens is max_tokens of an article, overview or subtopic call — far above the 900 characters the server keeps — and nameMaxTokens of a group's name; parallel is how many of one topic's calls are in flight at once, the queue's own cap for one job; snapshotWaitSeconds is how long a job with no snapshot to name waits for the one it asked for.

membership.entries: A topic's entries are the space's active entries that no web-derived source tainted, each in exactly one topic.
order: paths: every repo-relative path the entry names (its path and symbol anchors, a pitfall's trigger.paths, a convention's scope up to its first wildcard) votes for the topic whose pattern claims the most of it (membership.patterns); the topic with the most votes wins, then the longer claim, then the earlier topic
declared: failing that, the first of the entry's own topics that is a topic of the space

text: failing that, the topic whose words its title, summary and aliases are closest to (tf-idf cosine over words and CJK bigrams against each topic's title, description and the entries the first two steps gave it); an entry close to none is in no topic
membership.why: The demo filed articles by the words alone, and a topic collected entries about something else (the sessions topic held articles on database writes and on running Nest). Where an entry is anchored in the code is the better witness, so it decides first.
membership.paths: A path is taken relative to the repository: a leading ./ and a checkout's absolute prefix (/root/orbit/, or a worktree's /.orbit/worktrees/<id>/) are dropped first.
membership.patterns: wiki_topic.path_prefixes holds prefixes and suffixes. A prefix claims a path that starts with it, as many characters as it has; one that ends in / claims the directory itself too (src/web claims what src/web/ does). A pattern that starts with * is a suffix: it claims a path that ends with the rest (*.swift claims a bare ConsoleModel.swift), as many characters as the rest has. So a directory's prefix outranks a suffix, and a suffix names what a bare file name is about when nothing longer does.

articles.fingerprint: sha256 of the lines <entry id>:<current revision> of the topic's entries, sorted by id and joined by a newline: the same entries at the same revisions give the same fingerprint, and an entry that joins, leaves or is amended changes it.
articles.regeneration: A topic's articles are rewritten only when its fingerprint differs from the one its part 0 was generated from, and never by a clock. Since criterion 3's revision 3 a maintenance run no longer rewrites the topic articles itself (maintenance.job.run.steps, docs): a maintenance run of the space that succeeded, recorded ops and was not made while the space was behind (its catch-up neither active nor paused, the documents' own rule) makes one articles job (articles.serverExecution, jobs.kindRuns.articles; the owner's decision of 2026-10-08); the job rewrites only the topics whose fingerprint changed. A write that names the stored fingerprint rewrites nothing (unchanged), and one that names a fingerprint other than the topic's current one is refused WIKI_ARTICLE_STALE.

validation.input: Each part is Markdown with footnote markers [n], and notes: the entry each n names, notes[n-1]. A subtopic part names the entries of its group too.
validation.sentences: The body is cut into sentences at 。！？, and at a full stop or an ASCII ? or ! followed by a space or the end of the line — not at an ASCII ? or ! after a space or another ? or !, which is code left outside backticks (a ?? b, a != b), and not inside a code span; a heading line starts a block, and a first-level heading is not part of the body.
validation.markers: A marker survives only when n is 1 to the number of notes and notes[n-1] is an entry of the topic (a subtopic may cite any entry of its topic). A marker out of range, naming another topic's entry or naming no entry of the space is stripped.
validation.sentencesWithoutNotes: A sentence left with no marker is deleted.
validation.cap: When the kept sentences pass rules.maxChars, the last sentence of the longest block with more than one is dropped, again and again, until they do not.
validation.numbering: Footnotes are renumbered 1, 2, … in the order they first appear, and citations records the entry and its revision behind each number.
validation.empty: A subtopic part with no sentence left is dropped; a part 0 with none is not written at all, and the topic stays as it was.

view.push: Never in <orbit_wiki_context>: the push reads wiki_entry and nothing else.
view.source: Never a source: no source kind names an article (sourceRules.firstHand), so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED.
view.agents: Never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get: both read entries alone, and an article's id is no entry's.
view.readers: The owner, on the user door. Another owner's space, topic or article is a plain 404.

who.write: The server's own articles job (origin maintenance, no session and no user, revisions authored system: articles.serverExecution), and an import the API server's container runs itself (origin import, no session and no user) for a preview space. No door builds either, and the user door has no write route: any other caller is an error of the server's own code (WikiArticles.assertWriter).
who.read: The owner, on the user door.

articles.seeding: A space with no topic yet is given articles.defaultTopics the first time a writer asks for its plan: their slugs, display names, categories, descriptions and path prefixes, in this order. A space that has topics keeps them.

reads.directory: The six categories in order, each with its topics (display name, description, the article's part 0 if there is one, and the subtopic parts under it), and the topics nothing has filed under a category.
reads.article: One part: its title, kind, blocks of sentences with their footnote numbers, and footnotes resolved to the entries they name (title, summary, kind, status, trust), with the topic, its category, the parts beside it, when and at which ref it was generated. It names every entry it was written from (entryIds, the pool its generation stored in wiki_topic_summary.entry_ids) and carries the first entriesListed of them as they stand now, the cited ones first (entries): what the list under the article is drawn from.
reads.index: Every article of the space, A to Z by title: its topic, its part and the entries it was written from.

serverExecution.who: Every account: the server writes every space's articles (P11, 2026-10-19).
serverExecution.made: One articles job per space, made where the server records the end of a maintenance run of the space that succeeded, recorded ops (a changeset of origin maintenance from the run's job) and was not made while the space was behind (owner, 2026-10-08). Background priority (articles.job.priority), and until it is first claimed it waits for the space's next round of maintenance — the first maintain job made after it — which it yields once and no other (jobs.priority); the end that queues it asks for that round at once (maintenance.job.server.trigger). At most one is queued or parked per space: a queued job reads the plan when it runs, and a parked one reads it again when it is replayed, so either covers every run that ends before it; one that is already running may have read it, so the next run's end queues another behind it. A failure to make it is logged and never the run's.
steps: plan: WikiArticles.plan as the job (who.write) — a space with no topic is given the default ones — and only the topics whose fingerprint changed are taken up; with none, the job succeeds having asked nothing

ref: the sha of the space's repository snapshot (repoOps.cache), which an article records as the commit it was written at. With none, the job asks the space's runner for one, once (repoOps.kinds.snapshot) and parks on it (repoOps.waiting, at most articles.job.snapshotWaitSeconds); it is replayed when the snapshot lands. A job that asked and got none — the operation failed, or did not settle in time — or whose space names no checkout to read writes without a ref, and its report says why

topic: its input (WikiArticles.input); a topic of more than rules.splitAbove entries grouped by tf-idf spherical k-means, anchor paths first, yielding the worker's event loop as it computes; each group named one after another, each told the names already taken; the subtopic articles and the overview, or the one article, written articles.job.parallel at a time; a draft that keeps fewer than rules.minChars characters, counted by the server's own validation, asked for once more when its pool has 8 entries or more

write: WikiArticles.write, so validation keeps a footnote only when it names an entry of the topic and the topic's rows are replaced only from its current fingerprint; model is the System model's name
serverExecution.prompts: The system prompt, the article, subtopic and overview prompts, the entry lines, the naming prompt and the retry suffix, word for word as the runner's writer had them before P11: src/shared/src/wiki-article-writer.fixture.json, which the runner's Go writer wrote, holds one answer — every call and the big topic's groups — and the worker's own specs (wiki-articles-job.spec.ts, wiki-articles-writer.spec.ts) hold the server's writer to it.
serverExecution.calls: Each call is a request of the queue (modelQueue) with step articles.job.step and unit <slug>@<first 12 of its fingerprint>/name-<n>, /part-<n> or /part-<n>/again, so a job replayed after its worker died reuses every answer it had, and a topic whose entries moved between two attempts is asked afresh. The queue retries a 5xx, a 429 and a dropped connection, and stops at a 401 for the whole deployment (modelQueue.retry.unauthorized).
serverExecution.ends: Every topic it took up written or unchanged: succeeded, its report the summary — seeded, ref and refWhy, topics [{slug, entries, outcome, why, parts}], written, unchanged, failed, calls, usage and the validation's stats. A topic left unwritten — a call that ended in a way that is the work's, a write refused (WIKI_ARTICLE_STALE among them) — fails the job as content once every other topic has been tried, its report on the row; the next job writes it from the entries as they stand. A failure of the platform (a request past its wait limit, the database) ends the attempt as infra; the worker stopping hands the job back with nothing counted (jobs.lease.handBack). Either way the replay starts over from the plan. Its report is the whole job's (jobs.carry): a replay starts from the plan again, and the topics an earlier attempt seeded, wrote or found written — which the plan no longer names — are carried on the job's row as each is done and counted in it, every topic once in the plan's order, with the ref they were written at when the replay wrote none; its calls and usage are every request the job made, each once.

plan.means: Before a space's documents are written, the System model drafts a plan: categories, the documents in each, every document's reader, scope, length and outline, and for every section the conditions its material is taken by. The server's gate checks each draft; the owner confirms one; documents are written only from the version the owner confirmed (guard). A plan is a record of what the owner agreed to, kept in versions, and not knowledge: it is never pushed, never a source, and never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get.

statuses.draft: stored after the gate passed it, waiting for the owner; a space has at most one, and a newer draft supersedes it
statuses.confirmed: the version the owner confirmed and the documents are written from; a space has at most one, and confirming a draft supersedes it
statuses.superseded: a version a newer draft or a confirmation replaced; kept, unchanged, as history

origins.maintenance: a whole draft the server's plan job drafted (plan.jobs.server)
origins.owner: the owner's edit of one document or section, or a proposal the owner accepted, through the user door

sectionKinds.overview: what the document covers, written last from what its other sections say
sectionKinds.concepts: a mechanism: what the things are; its material is the design documents, the code and the contracts
sectionKinds.flow: a mechanism: how it runs, step by step; its material is the design documents, the code and the contracts
sectionKinds.interface: a mechanism: the routes, tools, commands and their answers; its material is the contracts and the code
sectionKinds.data: a mechanism: the tables, fields and settings; its material is the migrations, the schema and the code
sectionKinds.ops: running it: deploying, operating, recovering; its material is the design documents and the scripts
sectionKinds.pitfalls: the known pitfalls; their material is what was said in sessions, found by the section's session condition
sectionKinds.decisions: the decisions and their reasons; their material is the owner's words and the records of decisions, found by the section's session condition
sectionKinds.conventions: the conventions to follow; their material is what was said in sessions, found by the section's session condition

plan.forAgents: A category with forAgents true holds the agents' development conventions (how to test, commit, land and run commands here): criterion 11 lists them as a category of their own, apart from the product and its mechanisms.
plan.rulesNote: docsMin and docsMax are the document count a draft is held to when its request names no target; a request may name its own (target: { min, max }), up to docsCeiling. Lengths are counted in characters (Unicode code points). errorsMax is the most errors one refusal lists; its message counts them all.
plan.schemaNote: Every field a draft may carry, at each level, and no other. A draft's categories and docs are lists: a document names its category by key (a slug), and categories and documents are listed in the directory's order. A category needs key and title; a document every field but protected and extra, with audience, scopeIn and sections not empty; a section every field but key and extra. length is { min, max } for a document and one number for a section. A section's sources lists design-document sections ({ path, section }), code files with their symbols ({ path, symbols }) and contracts ({ path }); its session condition (sessions, or null) names projects (each by id or exact title), a time window (since and until, YYYY-MM-DD or null), keywords, anchor paths, entry kinds, topics (slugs of the space) and, in words, the original words to look for (evidence). A section's key is a slug, stable within its document from version to version: a section sent without one keeps the key its title had in the version revised, or is given the next s<n>.

newFields.rule: A field the schema does not have is refused at the gate, unless the draft declares it in newFields ({ at, name, why }) as a field that needs adding, at category, doc or section; then its values go in that object's extra, by name, apart from the schema's own fields, and the version's gate report lists it (needsNewFields) for the owner to read. A declared name that is already a field of the schema is refused, and so is a name in extra that newFields does not declare. An owner's edit and a proposal may use the fields the version they change declared, and declare none.

plan.versions: Every draft, edit and accepted proposal is a new version, numbered after every version the space has had and written in one transaction under the space row's lock (FOR NO KEY UPDATE); a version's documents and sections are only ever inserted, and the one row of a version ever updated is its own wiki_plan row, when it is confirmed or superseded. So a confirmed version never changes: what the owner confirmed is, byte for byte, what the documents are written from. Each version names the version it revises (baseVersion) and, for an accepted proposal, the proposal. A draft or an edit names the version it is built on (baseVersion; null for a space's first draft), which must be the space's newest version that is not superseded — its draft when it has one, else its confirmed version; one built on another is refused WIKI_PLAN_STALE and nothing is written — unless it is a draft landing again under the idempotency key it was stored with (plan.idempotency), or an earlier round of the wiki_job whose own draft now stands on that version, which is gated on the version as it was (plan.jobs.server.strike). An acceptance is built on the newest version as it finds it, and is refused the same way when the plan moves while it is written.

idempotency.key: A draft may carry an idempotencyKey (at most 200 characters), the owner's as a changeset's is (refusalRules.idempotency): the version it stores keeps the key and the digest of its request — the request's JSON, keys sorted, with the space it names — and one key stores one version (UNIQUE (owner_id, idempotency_key)). An edit or an accepted proposal has none.
idempotency.replay: The same draft under the same key — the drafting job sends it again when the answer to its first send was lost on its way back — is answered with the version that key stored, replayed: true, before the plan is read and so before WIKI_PLAN_STALE: it writes nothing, publishes nothing and gates nothing, and the version is answered as it stands now. Two landings at once are one: under the space row's lock the second finds the first's version and is answered with it.
idempotency.reused: The same key with another request is refused WIKI_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED (409) and nothing is written.
idempotency.answer: A draft's answer is the version, whole, with replayed: false when it was stored by this request and true when it is a replay.
idempotency.runner: The drafting job derives the key from its plan job, its wiki_job and the draft it sends (wikiPlanServerDraftKey: wiki-plan-<the first 40 hex of sha256(the plan job's id, server:<the wiki_job's id>, the draft's JSON)>), so a replay of the job that sends the same draft again carries its key and is answered with the version it stored, and another draft another key.

gate.schema: Every field is one the schema has at its level (schema), or one declared as needing adding (newFields), of the right type and within rules; a section's kind is one of sectionKinds; category keys, document slugs and a document's section keys are unique.
gate.docCount: A plan has rules.docsCeiling documents at most. Its target — rules.docsMin to rules.docsMax unless the request names its own — is what the drafting job is held to, and the owner may confirm a draft outside it; a change to a version (a proposal) may not take it further out than it stands, and an edit, which leaves the count alone, is not counted.
gate.protected: A document the revised version protects is in the new version exactly as it was: the same slug, category and fields, and the same sections in the same order (their keys aside). Only the owner protects a document, so a draft or a proposal that protects one is refused. The owner's own edit is not checked: protecting is theirs.
gate.references: Every project a session condition names is one of the owner's (by id, or by an exact title only one project has), every topic a topic of the space, every entry kind one of the entry kinds; every document's category is one of the plan's categories, and every document a scope leaves something to (scopeOut[].docs) one of the plan's documents. A proposal's facts are an entry of the space or a session of the owner, or a commit named by its full sha (plan.proposals.factKindsNote). A topic that is none of the space's is refused with the space's topics after it, oldest first, as the drafting job's materials list them (wikiPlanTopicsBrief: Existing topics (slug «name» · active entries): wiki «Wiki» · 3; …, or that a session condition names no topic when the space has none), so the next round has them to name: on the canary a maintenance run's proposal failed on made-up topics twice, told only that each was none (2026-10-09 54755b7b, the same two in rounds 2 and 3; 2026-10-10 3b2bd5f2, wiki-maintenance — a document's slug — in round 3).
gate.values: A message that names a value the request gave writes it as a JSON string — in double quotes, every character that would not show (a control or format character, a line or paragraph separator, a space other than U+0020) written as \uXXXX — so a backtick, an invisible character and a space at either end all show: on 10-01, «`decision` is no kind of entry: one of principle, convention, decision, …» read as decision refused for being decision, and the model wrote it the same way three rounds running. A closed-set value — a section's kind, a session condition's entryKinds and topics, a declared new field's at, a fact's kind — is read with the whitespace at either end and whatever backticks or quotes (` " ' “” ‘’ 「」 『』 «») wrap the whole of it taken off, as often as they do, a pair counting as a wrapping only with no more of either inside; nothing else is read loosely, so `decision` is the entry kind decision while Decision, decisions and decision with a zero-width space after it are none. The whitespace at the edge is every Unicode space (U+0085 among them) and U+FEFF (P10, 2026-10-08: the union of what the server's gate and the runner's trimmed, so a value either accepted is read here). The plan job's own gate (plan.jobs.run) and a maintenance run's check of its proposal read and write values the same way.
gate.repo: Files, docs sections, symbols and contracts exist only in a checkout, which the server has none of: the drafting job checks them on the space's snapshot of a commit, which the runner made (plan.jobs.server.repository), and reports repoCheck { sha, checked, missing: [{ kind, ref, at }] } with the draft (kind one of file, docSection, symbol, contract). The server keeps the report and its sha beside the version (repo_sha, repo_check) and does not judge it; An owner's edit and an accepted proposal are not checked again and carry the check of the version they change: the same sha, each miss moved with its reference and gone with it, checked counted again. A version made from one that was never checked carries none.
gate.errors: A request the gate refuses is WIKI_PLAN_GATE with errors[]: everything it found, each { check, path, message }, the path from the request's root (a draft's plan.docs[3].sections[2].sources.sessions.projects[0], an edit's doc. or section., a proposal's change.doc.) — and for what an edit or a proposal would make of the whole plan, from that plan's (plan.docs[20].protected) — the first rules.errorsMax listed. Nothing is stored, so the drafting job hands the list to the model and asks again.
gate.author: Errors go to whoever wrote the thing (owner, 2026-11-02). The author of a draft is the model, so the gate's errors go back to it, and the owner never reads them; the owner's own edit is refused to the owner. A stored version always meets the schema and can always be confirmed and built from: what a drafting job's last round leaves it settles itself (plan.jobs.server.settle). Why: of two drafts on 2026-11-02, one read 4 of 953 references wrong and one kept the template's labels on 9 category keys and 31 slugs with all 1,099 references found; both were the pipeline's faults, and both reached the owner as a red page whose only door, Redraft, reran the same pipeline.
gate.notes: What a stored draft says to look at: gate.notes, [{ check, text }], at most rules.notesMax, text a sentence the server writes in English for the owner, which clients draw under that check. Left out when there is none, and carried by an edit and an accepted proposal. References not found and a count outside the target are no notes: clients read those from repoCheck.missing and from gate.docs against gate.target.
gate.report: A version the gate let through keeps its report: { checkedAt, checks (each passed, or skipped for protected on an owner's edit), docs, target, needsNewFields: [{ at, name, why, values }] }.

proposals.means: Knowledge a maintenance run found that fits no section of the confirmed plan is a proposed change to it: why (reason), the document as it should read — one of the plan's by its slug, or a new one, with the category it opens when it needs one the plan does not have (change: { doc, category }) — and the facts that led to it (facts: [{ kind, id }]). It is gated against the confirmed version, protection included, and stored pending. It changes no version until the owner accepts it.

statuses.accepted: the owner accepted it: its document was applied to the plan's newest version and made a new draft (resultVersion) for the owner to confirm
statuses.rejected: the owner rejected it; the plan is as it was

proposals.factKindsNote: A fact is an entry of the space, a session of the owner, or — for a design document that landed on origin/main and that no section cites — the commit that added it, named by its full sha (40 hex characters). The server has no checkout: it holds a commit to its shape, and the maintenance run found it on origin/main.
proposals.accept: Applies the document to the plan's newest version — in place of the document of its slug, or after the last document of its category — and gates the result again, protection included, since the plan may have moved since it was proposed: a result the gate refuses is WIKI_PLAN_GATE and the proposal stays pending. Otherwise the new draft and the proposal's settling are one transaction.
proposals.reject: Settles the proposal, with the owner's note if there is one; no version changes.
proposals.author: Who filed it (migration 0407): the server's maintenance run (author_job_id) — or, for a proposal filed before server execution, a maintenance session (author_session_id) — exactly one, held by wiki_plan_proposal_author_chk. An owner's decision on the proposal is neither: decided_by_user_id is on the row beside them.

plan.guard: requireConfirmedPlan(db, { ownerId, spaceId }) in src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-plan.ts: the space's confirmed version ({ id, version, confirmedAt }), or WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED. Every writer of a space's documents calls it before it writes one, so no document is written from a plan the owner did not confirm; a maintenance run's proposal needs it too.

who.draft: The server's plan job drafts and revises (plan.jobs.server) and the server's maintenance run proposes (maintenance.job.docs.proposal), in process: no door takes a draft or a proposal, nor answers a read of the plan to a session, since P11 (2026-10-19).
who.owner: The owner, through the user door and only there: every read of the plan, an edit, a confirmation, an acceptance or a rejection. A request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY before anything is read, whatever the session's role; the runner door has no route of the plan. Another owner's space, version or proposal is a plain 404.

reads.state: { spaceId, confirmed, draft, proposals, job }: the version in force and the draft, each whole or null, the pending proposals, oldest first, and the space's plan job (plan.jobs.read), or null when it never had one.
reads.versions: Every version, newest first: { id, version, status, origin, baseVersion, proposalId, docCount, createdAt, confirmedAt, supersededAt }.
reads.version: One version whole: its status, origin, baseVersion, categories, newFields, target, gate report, repoCheck, model, who made and confirmed it and when, and its documents in order, each with its sections in order; a session condition's projects are { id, title } with the title as it stands now (null for a project since deleted).

requests.draft: { baseVersion, target?, plan: { categories, docs, newFields? }, repoCheck, model?, idempotencyKey? }
requests.edit: { baseVersion, docSlug, doc } for a whole document (a new slug renames it), or { baseVersion, docSlug, sectionKey, section } for one of its sections
requests.propose: { reason, change: { doc, category? }, facts: [{ kind, id }] }
requests.redraft: { instructions? }: with instructions (at most plan.jobs.rules.instructionsMaxChars characters) a revision, without them a draft

plan.view: Not knowledge: no source kind names a plan, so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED; the push and the agent's search and get read entries alone.
plan.tool: none: no MCP tool reads, confirms or decides anything of the plan (hard constraint 2). Drafting is the server's plan job's (plan.jobs.server).

jobs.means: A space's plan is drafted, revised and built by jobs the wiki-worker runs (plan.jobs.server): no task and no session is made for one. A fact asks for a job — the space's creation, or its owner — never a clock.

kinds.draft: a whole plan drafted from the repository at origin/main and what the space already knows, keeping every document the version it revises protects (wiki_job plan_draft, plan.jobs.server)
kinds.revise: the space's newest version revised with the owner's instructions; a space with no version yet is drafted with the instructions as the owner's guidance (wiki_job plan_revise)
kinds.build: the documents of a confirmed version written section by section (wiki_job docs_build, docs.build.server), which the owner's confirmation asks for; a section whose material did not change since it was written is left as it is, so after a small change only what changed is written again

triggers.space_created: the space was created: through POST /api/wiki/spaces, or on the first proposal of a session whose workspace's repository had no space yet
triggers.owner: the owner asked on the plan page: for a draft or a revision, POST /api/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/redraft; for a build, by confirming a version, POST /api/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/versions/:version/confirm, or by asking for the documents of the version in force again, POST /api/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/versions/:version/build (rebuild)
triggers.support: an administrator asked for the documents of the version in force again, for support: POST /api/admin/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/build, with a reason recorded in Activity (rebuild.support, migration 0429)

states.queued: recorded and not made yet: a request makes it at once (request), so a job stays queued only when its making did not happen, and the owner's next request or settings change asks again
states.held: the space's maintenance names no workspace (held.reason); the job is made when the owner's next change to the maintenance settings, or their next request, finds that settled
states.running: its wiki_job is made — queued, running or waiting in the worker — with the gate round it is on, a build with how far it has got (progress)
states.succeeded: its job stored a draft (version), the last round's errors settled when any were left (server.settle); a build's wrote the documents of a confirmed version (version) and left no section unwritten
states.failed: its job left no draft to show (noDraft): error says why, in a sentence for the owner — or its wiki_job ended before it said how it went. A job that ended before 2026-11-02 also carries the gate's errors on its last round and its last draft, and its error reads It didn’t pass the plan check.

held.where: wiki_plan_job.held_reason and held_at, served as the job's held: { reason, at }, or null. Written when a job is not made for one of the reasons, keeping the time the reason first held, as maintenance.job.held is on the cursor; cleared when its job is made.
held.no_maintenance_workspace: settings.maintenance.workspaceId names no workspace of the owner's: a draft runs where maintenance runs.
held.maintenance_provider_unusable: No longer given (P11, 2026-10-19): the runner path held a job whose space's maintenance pinned a provider no run could start on. A job held so before is made when it is asked again; the value stays for the clients that read it.

jobs.request: A request asks for a draft, or with instructions a revision. The space's draft or revision that has not ended answers it (one open a space, a partial unique index) and is asked again whether it may be made now; a made job whose wiki_job already ended, or is gone, without saying how — or one a task made before server execution — is ended failed first, so it cannot stand in the way. Otherwise a job is recorded and asked at once: held when the settings say so; else made (plan.jobs.server.make). A build is asked for by the owner's confirmation of a version, after it commits and never failing it: the space's build that waits (queued or held, one a space, a partial unique index) answers it, pointed at the newer version, and is asked again; a build already made does not stand in the way — it writes the version it was made for, and the waiting one the next. A build names its version from the start (version), and keeps it when it fails. The documents of the version in force asked for again (rebuild) are answered by that version's own build that has not ended, and otherwise asked for as a confirmation asks.
jobs.trigger: The space's creation and the owner's requests ask for a job (request), and the owner's change to a space's maintenance settings asks its held and queued jobs again (resumeWikiPlanJobs). No clock asks anything.
jobs.staggered: A job does not wait for the space's maintenance runs, nor they for it: each is a wiki_job of its own, and the worker runs one job of a space at a time, in the space's own order (jobs.onePerSpace, jobs.priority) — the owner's job, at the owner's priority, before the background runs. A held job waits for the owner's settings and stands in no run's way.
jobs.notAMaintenanceRun: A job is not a maintenance run: it is not counted against settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday counts the run rows alone), the day's limit does not hold it back, and it runs whether or not maintenance is turned on. A build asked for again (rebuild) is the same job, and is neither counted nor held back either.
jobs.read: The plan's read (plan.reads.state) carries the space's job that has not ended, else the one that ended last: { id, spaceId, kind, trigger, state, instructions, requestedAt, held, waitingFor: { taskId, title, sessionId, startedAt } for a queued one, taskId, provider, sessionId, madeAt, startedAt, endedAt, attempt, attemptsMax, progress, version, errors, error, report, draft } — draft being the last draft of a job that failed before 2026-11-02, as its run sent it to the gate, and progress a build's { docs: { done, total }, current: { slug, title } | null }, null for a draft. waitingFor, taskId, provider and sessionId are the runner path's: null for a job the server ran — a job a task made before server execution keeps its taskId and sessionId. No client reads waitingFor, taskId or provider (2026-10-19); a job that kept its session opens it as its run.
jobs.noDraft: The only way a draft or a revision fails: no draft to show. Its catalogue could not be read; no document was written; the platform's retry limit; the plan changed while the job ran; or the server's gate refused a settled draft, which is a fault. error is one sentence for the owner, with no field path and no word of the model's: what the run knows beyond it goes to its log and its wiki_job. Redraft is the owner's next step.
jobs.doors: Clients offer two doors onto POST …/plan/redraft. With a version stored, Redraft… needs words, because it reads that version; a fresh draft over one is Start over… in the ⋯ menu, behind its own confirmation, and sends no instructions. With nothing stored, Redraft… may go empty. After a job that left no draft, the box opens holding its instructions.

who.redraft: The owner, on the owner channel only: a request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY before anything is read. Its answer is { created, job }: the job made, or the space's draft that had not ended.
who.build: The owner, on the owner channel only, as redraft (rebuild.who). Its answer is { created, job }: the build made, or the one of the version in force that had not ended.
who.support: An administrator (AdminRoleGuard), signed in: never an access token (PatForbidden ADMIN), nor while viewing Orbit as another account (IMPERSONATION_FORBIDDEN). supportBuild answers { created, job, ownerId } and records Activity; supportSpaces reads an account's spaces as rebuild.supportSpaces says.

jobs.progress: { attempt }: the gate round a draft's or a revision's job is on, 1 to rules.attemptsMax; a build's { docs: { done, total }, current: { slug, title } | null }: the documents of the confirmed version it went through, and the one it writes now — what the plan page shows while it runs (plan.jobs.server.progress).
jobs.finish: { outcome: succeeded | failed, version?, errors?, error?, report?, draft?, attempt? }: a job that succeeded names the version its draft became, a draft of the space this very wiki_job stored; one that failed carries why, in a sentence for the owner (noDraft; redacted, at most rules.errorMaxChars); errors (at most plan.rules.errorsMax) and draft (at most rules.draftMaxBytes of JSON) are what jobs ended with before 2026-11-02, read but no longer sent. The report is at most rules.reportMaxBytes of JSON. A build that succeeded names the confirmed version it wrote, one the owner confirmed; one that failed keeps the version it was made for, and its report is WikiPlanBuildReport (buildReport). The plan job is ended with it once, by the wiki_job it was made with (plan.jobs.server.finish); a plan job ended already keeps what it said first.
jobs.materials: { spaceId, title, asOf, repo, workspace, projects: [{ id, title, status, createdAt, tasks, sessions }], sessions: { days, total, items: [{ title, month, task, project, provider }] }, entries: [{ kind, status, count }], topics: [{ slug, title, category, pathPrefixes, active, recent: [{ kind, title }] }] }: the owner's projects (at most rules.materialsProjectsMax, oldest first), the sessions of the space's workspaces of the last rules.materialsSessionDays days (at most rules.materialsSessionsMax, newest first, with the total), and how the space's entries and topics are spread. Every title is redacted; the plan job counts and clusters (plan.jobs.server.materials).
jobs.report: What a run reports when it ends (WikiPlanJobReport): categories, docs, sections, target, attempts [{ attempt, local, server, checks }] — each gate round's errors found by the job's own gate (local) and by the server's (server), by check — repo { sha, checked, missing }, tokens { input, output, calls }, seconds, model, and rulesDraft: the fourth step's draft of the rules, cut to fit.
jobs.buildReport: What a build's run reports when it ends (WikiPlanBuildReport): planVersion, repoSha, docs { total, written }, sections { written, unchanged, failed }, tokens { input, output, calls }, seconds, model.

steps: context: the job, the space and its repository, and the version it revises with the documents that version protects (plan.reads.state)

snapshot: the space's snapshot of origin/main (repoOps.kinds.snapshot) through the maintenance workspace's runner, as plan.jobs.server.materials says; a checkout that is not the space's repository fails the job

materials: the repository at the snapshot's sha — its modules and entry points, the docs heading tree (docs/mocks and docs/evidence left out), the contracts and the code's symbols (plan.jobs.server.repository) — and the plan's materials (plan.jobs.materials): the owner's projects, the space's sessions counted and clustered by title, and its entries and topics

draft, in four steps: the catalogue's skeleton (categories and documents), each category's documents in detail, each document's outline with where every section's material comes from, and a draft of the rules; one request to the System model a unit, through the queue (plan.jobs.server.calls), in a compact line format

gate: the job's own gate first — schema, docCount, protected, references (files, docs sections, symbols and contracts at the snapshot's sha, every project and topic, and every → x.y or see x.y a document of the plan — and the 见 x.y of a version written in Chinese) and, for a revision, sections moved out only of kind conventions — then the server's (plan.gate, WikiPlans.submitServerDraft)
redo: whatever either gate found is handed back to the model, unit by unit, and the draft gated again: rules.attemptsMax rounds in all; what the last leaves is settled (plan.jobs.server.settle)
finish: the plan job ended with the version the draft became, or with why there is no draft (plan.jobs.noDraft, plan.jobs.finish, plan.jobs.server.finish)
run.revise: A revision asks the model for the new catalogue — each document with the documents of the version it revises that it is made from, and the sections it moves into a category for agents — then writes again only the documents that merge or are new; one made from a single document of the version keeps its outline, less the sections moved out. The documents it hands the model, and a document a redo hands back, name their session conditions' projects by title, as every drafting prompt names a project, and never by an id the model would have to copy; a project keeps its id only where its title is one another project shares, or the materials' list of projects may have been cut. A protected document is carried as it is, and a move out of one, or of a section of any kind but conventions, is refused by the job's own gate.
run.model: Every call is a request to the System model through the queue (plan.jobs.server.calls), thinking off, what has arrived kept as the request's partial while it runs; a 401 stops the whole queue (modelQueue.retry).
run.build: A build is the docs_build job (docs.build.server): every document of the confirmed version, section by section (docs.build), its progress on the plan job as each document is taken up (plan.jobs.progress), and the plan job ended with the version it wrote and its report: succeeded when no section was left unwritten, failed with why otherwise.

server.why: The plan's model is the server's (design section 0): a draft or a revision is a wiki_job the wiki-worker runs with the System model — the runner's pipeline ported to src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-plan-*.ts before the runner's was removed (P11), its repository read from the space's snapshot — and no task, session or provider of the account's is made or spent.
server.make: advanceWikiPlanJob makes a draft as a `plan_draft` wiki_job and a revision as `plan_revise`, at priority, with input { planJobId }, in the transaction that marks the plan job made with it (wiki_plan_job.job_id). The space's maintenance workspace is what it needs — the worker reads the repository through that workspace's runner — so a space without one is held no_maintenance_workspace; the provider is not asked, since no session's model is. One running job a space and the queue keep the model from being asked by two jobs of a space at once. No task is made.
server.build: A build is made as a `docs_build` wiki_job on the same path (P7, docs.build.server): by advanceWikiPlanJob, at docs.build.server.priority with input { planJobId }, in the transaction that marks the plan job made with it — held no_maintenance_workspace without a workspace and the provider not asked, as a draft. Its run says how far it got on the plan job ({ docs, current }, plan.jobs.progress) and ends it as plan.jobs.finish says a build's — the version it wrote, the build's report — with no session (docs.build.server.progress, docs.build.server.end). A build asked for again of the version in force (rebuild) is made the same way.
server.priorityRule: Owner-initiated (jobs.priority): the space's creation and the owner's redraft are both the owner's, so every request of the job goes before background maintenance.
server.systemPrompt: You are the chief editor of this repository's documentation. You plan its product and technical documents from the materials you are given. Use only the file paths, section headings, symbols and project names that appear in the materials, and invent none. Write in English; keep code names, paths and commands as they are. Output only what is asked for.
server.calls: Every call is one queue request (modelQueue): step one of steps — each `plan_*`, so it waits at most modelQueue.waitLimitSeconds.plan and runs at most modelQueue.callBudgetSeconds.plan, sixty minutes — and unit `a<round>/<unit>@<the first 12 hex of the call's sha256>`, each unit named as the runner's pipeline named it, so a replay meets the request it already made, an answer that does not read is asked again with the format said once more (formatTries calls a unit at most), and a changed question is a new request. maxTokens a call, the system prompt above, one user message; what has arrived is kept as the request's partial while it runs (modelQueue).
server.materials: Read once, at the job's first run, and kept on the plan job (wiki_plan_job.materials, migration 0404): the space's snapshot's sha — a fresh snapshot when its runner can take one, waited for at most snapshotWaitSeconds, else the snapshot the space holds, else the job waits as infra — the plan's materials (plan.jobs.materials, wikiPlanMaterials), the day they were read, and the texts at the sha the snapshot does not carry: the overview's documents and schema.prisma, through the runner's read (repoOps.kinds.read), waited for at most readWaitSeconds. A replay reads them back, so it asks the model the questions it asked; a snapshot that moved under the job (another job of the space took a newer one) makes it start over at the snapshot as it is.
server.materialCapsRule: The caps, in characters (the runner's pipeline's, kept): a catalogue reads the overview at full, the structure and the documents' heading tree at full; a category's details read them at detail; a document's outline reads the overview at doc and its code's symbols within codeExcerpt (bytes, as the runner's builder counted them).
server.repository: The repository is read from the snapshot index at the job's sha: the files with their sizes (the structure, hasPath), every document's headings (the heading trees, hasDocSection), every source file's symbols (the code excerpt, hasSymbol), the contracts' top-level keys (the contracts list). A symbol the index does not name is looked for as a word of its file's text — the whole text of the file, read at the sha before the round is gated (repoOps.kinds.read). The index carries an object's keys only: a contract whose JSON is an array or empty reads as not JSON.
server.gate: The job's own gate first — plan.jobs.run's checks, word for word, with every file, docs section, symbol and contract checked on the snapshot — then the plan's gate on the server (plan.gate), which the job reaches in process (WikiPlans.submitServerDraft) under the draft's idempotency key; repoCheck is the snapshot's sha and what this gate found. Whatever either finds goes back to the model unit by unit, plan.jobs.rules.attemptsMax rounds in all. A way of writing a key or a slug is no error of the draft (names), and what the last round leaves is settled (settle).
server.author: A stored version names the wiki_job that drafted it (wiki_plan.author_job_id, migration 0404; authorJobId on the read), where a version a session drafted before server execution names its session; origin maintenance, model the System model's name.
server.names: A category's key and a document's slug are identifiers, not the model's words, so a way of writing one is no error and costs no round. When a catalogue is adopted (wikiPlanAdoptCatalogue) the template's label comes off (<slug: storage> reads storage) and the rest is written in lowercase letters and digits joined by single hyphens, 64 characters at most (wikiPlanIdentifier). What is nothing after that falls back: a category to its number c<n>, a document to its title, then to a digest of its title doc-<8 hex>, so the same answer names the same again and what was written stays. One that repeats takes -2, -3. How many were changed goes to the run's log.
server.settle: What the last round leaves is not the draft's end (wikiPlanSettle), and nothing here decides for the owner. Repository references stay on their sections, listed in repoCheck.missing as a protected document's are; the page marks them and the build looks again at its own sha. A value that cannot be stored goes and the rest stays, with a note: a project, a topic or an entry kind nobody has, out of its session condition; a section kind outside the closed set becomes other. What the server's gate refuses of the same kind on the last round goes the same way, and the draft is submitted once more. A count outside the target stays, and a plan with no category for the agents is noted. A protected document is carried back as it was, with its category and the documents its scopeOut names; a move that cannot be is called off, with a note. A document never outlined is left out, with a note. Every other field is put within rules: text cut, required text filled from the catalogue's card or a default, a length worked out from the sections'. There is no floor of quality: the numbers are the owner's to read. A section with no source found is still written, its sentences unsourced and marked Needs review.
server.progress: The plan job says where the run is, as plan.jobs.progress says: started_at at the job's first run, attempt at each round — what the plan page reads. The wiki_job's own progress (jobs.progress) is { planJobId, attempt, step }.
server.finish: The run ends its plan job as plan.jobs.finish says, held to its rules (WikiPlans.finishServerJob): succeeded with the version its draft became — a version of the space this wiki_job stored — or failed, with no draft to show, with why (noDraft) and the report; the wiki_job ends with { kind, planJobId, outcome, version, error, plan: the report }. A failure of the platform — a request past its wait limit, the space's runner away — is not the draft's: the wiki_job is retried (jobs.retry) and the plan job stays running. Nor is the worker stopping: the wiki_job is handed back with nothing counted (jobs.lease.handBack), and the plan job stays running. A wiki_job that ends without its plan job ended leaves it to be ended failed when the space next asks for a job (request), or at the retry limit with the wiki_job (jobs.retry.limit).
server.deterministic: src/shared/src/wiki-plan.fixture.json holds the answers the runner's pipeline gave before P11 — written by its Go test from a real checkout read the runner's way — and src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-plan-golden.spec.ts holds the server's implementation to them: the line format read back, the references found, the materials, every step's prompt, each round's draft, gate errors and repository check.

rebuild.why: A build is asked for by a confirmation (build), and a confirmation takes only a draft: once the one build of a version in force had failed, nothing could ask for its documents again. Production, 2026-10-15/16: a space's build of v1 (34 documents) ended failed/infra after 10 attempts (REPO_OP_FAILED, the workspace's directory was not a git checkout); the maintenance runs after the repository was mended were all catching up and skipped the documents (maintenance.job.catchUp), and once caught up the space had no fact to start another — 0 of 34 written, and no door for anybody to ask again.
rebuild.who: owner: the space's owner, signed in, on the owner channel only — a request with a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY before anything is read, an access token is refused (OWNER_INTERACTIVE, as every route of the plan), another account's space or version is a plain 404. support: an administrator (support).
rebuild.when: Whenever the owner asks, of the version in force: the server executes every account's wiki (P11, 2026-10-19). Clients draw the action only when jobs.executor.read says serverExecutes, which a server since then always says.
rebuild.version: owner: :version must be the space's version in force. No such version: 404; the space has no confirmed version: WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED; a draft or a superseded version: WIKI_PLAN_STALE, naming the version in force — a page left on an older version cannot ask for another version's documents. support takes no version: it is always the version in force.
rebuild.makes: The job a confirmation asks for (kinds.build, trigger owner or support, version the version in force, requested_by_user_id the one who asked), made as plan.jobs.server.build says: a docs_build wiki_job at docs.build.server.priority, owner-initiated work ahead of background maintenance and articles; no task, no session, no runner slot; held no_maintenance_workspace when the space's maintenance names no workspace; run whether or not maintenance is turned on. The build writes as docs.build.server says: every section never written, every section whose material fingerprint changed or whose sentences were withdrawn (stale_at); a section whose fingerprint is the one stored is left as it is and asks no model — asking again once everything is written costs a snapshot and reads from the space's cache.
rebuild.idempotent: Read and made under the wiki_space row lock (FOR NO KEY UPDATE, the lock a confirmation and an edit take). A made build whose wiki_job ended without saying how — or one a task made before server execution — is ended failed first (request). The version in force's own build that has not ended — queued, held, or made with its wiki_job queued, running or waiting — answers the request, created false, and a held one is asked again whether it may be made now. Otherwise the space's waiting build (queued or held, one a space) answers it pointed at the version in force, as a confirmation's request does; otherwise a build is recorded and asked at once, created true. Two requests at once are answered with one job.
rebuild.limits: Not a maintenance run (notAMaintenanceRun): not counted against settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit, nor held back by it — owner's call 2026-09-29 for the builds a confirmation asks for; the daily limit protects the review queue, and a build proposes no op; wikiMaintenanceRunsToday counts run rows, and a build has none. What bounds it: one build of the version in force on its way at a time (idempotent), one job of a space running at a time (jobs.lease), and the deployment's ORBIT_WIKI_MODEL_CONCURRENCY with each job's own in-flight cap (modelQueue.concurrency).
rebuild.failure: As docs_build's (jobs.retry, docs.build.server): the platform's failures (the space's runner away or its repository unreadable, a request or a read past its wait, a worker that crashed) are retried on the backoff and end failed/infra at jobs.retry.maxAttempts; a worker stopping hands the job back without counting; a section left unwritten ends it failed/content once every other section was tried. The plan job ends failed with why, the plan page's card says so (read), and the build can be asked for again. A build has no run row: the maintenance cursor and consecutive_failures are not touched.
rebuild.audit: Who asked and when: the plan job's row — trigger, requested_by_user_id, created_at (read as requestedAt). What it did: its wiki_job, model requests and repository operations, which Activity's Runs card reads (jobs.read). The owner's own request writes no Activity row, as a confirmation or a redraft writes none; an administrator's does (support).
rebuild.answer: { created, job } (WikiPlanBuildResult): job as the plan's read gives it (read). wiki.changed for the space after the commit.
rebuild.support: POST /api/admin/wiki/spaces/:id/plan/build, body { reason } (trimmed, 1 to rules.reasonMaxChars characters, else 400): the version in force of any account's space, the same job, made and answered the same way (idempotent, limits, failure), with trigger support and requested_by_user_id the administrator. In the same transaction as the job, one Activity row, the administrator's (actor_id, credential_kind LOGIN): type activity, payload { userId, spaceId, version, planJobId, created, reason } — every request that is answered a job writes one, one answered with a build already on its way included; a refused one writes none. A space that is no account's: 404; the wiki off for its owner (agentSurface.rollout): WIKI_DISABLED; WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED as the owner's. Its answer is { created, job, ownerId }. No CLI: administration is never open to an access token, and a CLI command would need a runner release.
rebuild.supportSpaces: GET /api/admin/wiki/users/:id/spaces: { userId, serverExecutes, spaces: [{ id, title, confirmedVersion, docs: { written, total } | null, building }] } — an account's spaces, oldest first, as much as picking one to build needs: no entry, document, session or plan content. An account that does not exist: 404.
rebuild.clients: The web only (owner's call 2026-10-17): the plan page, on the version in force while the server executes the account, draws Update documents in the head's actions after Redraft…, disabled while the version's build is queued, held or running; the administrators' Users page has Update wiki documents… in an account's menu (a space and a reason). macOS/iOS and Android draw neither; their copy and the shared fixtures are unchanged.

docs.means: A space's documents, written section by section from the plan its owner confirmed (plan.guard): a document is a plan document, named by its slug, and a section a plan section, named by its key. Every footnote points at a first-hand original — a design-document section, code or a contract at a commit, or one of Orbit's own records — with its verbatim quote, and the entry it was found through is kept as the via entry: an entry is the way in, never the source. What each sentence is, and how each footnote was checked, is stored sentence by sentence. A document is a view for people: never pushed, never a source, and never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get. The topic articles (articles, wiki_topic_summary) stay, readable as they are, until the clients have moved to the documents.

statuses.ok: no more than rules.needsReviewAbove of its sentences are unsourced or unverified
statuses.needs_review: more than rules.needsReviewAbove of its sentences are unsourced or unverified: the whole document is marked for review

sentenceStatuses.sourced: it carries a footnote whose check passed (verdict verified)
sentenceStatuses.transition: it carries no footnote and brings no new fact: every fact token in it (factTokens) is already in a sourced sentence or a heading of the same document
sentenceStatuses.unsourced: it carries no footnote and states a fact no sourced sentence or heading of the document carries; the tokens that are new are stored with it
sentenceStatuses.unverified: it carries footnotes, and none of them passed its check
sentenceStatuses.withdrawn: a footnote of it came through an entry since rejected, retired or superseded, or whose anchor changed or went missing, or cites a repository file deleted or renamed on origin/main (withdrawal); it stays, struck through, until its section is written again

footnoteKinds.design_doc: a section of a design document in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end, and the section's heading
footnoteKinds.code: code in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end, and the symbol
footnoteKinds.contract: a contract in the repository: path@sha#Lstart-end
footnoteKinds.turn: a conversation turn, by its id
footnoteKinds.event: a run event — a reply, a thinking, a tool call's input or its result, an error — by its id
footnoteKinds.tool_call: a tool call's output, by its id
footnoteKinds.task: a task's title and description, by its id
footnoteKinds.task_comment: a task comment, by its id
footnoteKinds.approval: an approval's answers and note, by its id
footnoteKinds.owner_decision: a blocker the owner resolved with a note, by its id
footnoteKinds.merge_receipt: a merge receipt, by its id
footnoteKinds.note: a file orbit wiki import registered, by its id

verdicts.verified: the quote is in the original
verdicts.not_found: the quote is not in the original; a quote shorter than rules.quoteMinChars once folded is not checked, and is not found either
verdicts.no_quote: the footnote gave no quote, so nothing could be checked
verdicts.unresolved: the record it names is not one of this account's — another owner's, deleted, or none at all; a repository footnote is never unresolved

checkers.server: a record's footnote: the server read the record again and checked the quote itself
checkers.runner: a repository footnote: the writer checked the quote at sha, on the file as the runner read it, which the server keeps no checkout of (verification.repository)

blockKinds.item: a list item, cut into sentences
blockKinds.heading: a heading inside the section: its text, which counts as a heading for factTokens
blockKinds.code: a fenced code block: its text, which is not checked
blockKinds.diagram: a Mermaid flowchart the section drew (diagram): its source as the server wrote it out again, which holds no sentence

docs.rulesNote: Lengths are counted in characters (Unicode code points). needsReviewAbove is a share of all the document's sentences, withdrawn ones included: more than it marks the whole document, and exactly 5% does not. quoteMinChars counts the folded quote (verification.normalization). sectionsPerWrite is plan.rules.sectionsMax, so one write can carry a whole document. errorsMax is the most errors one refusal lists; its message counts them all. dispositionsPerSection is the most pieces of material one section's ledger lists (dispositions), and reasonMaxChars the longest reason one of them gives.
docs.schemaNote: Every field a write may carry, at each level, and no other: anything else is refused WIKI_DOC_INVALID. planVersion, repoSha (the origin/main commit the run read the repository at, 40 lowercase hex) and sections are required; model is not. A section needs key (a section of the confirmed plan's document, once per write), materialSha256 (64 lowercase hex), markdown (not blank, at most rules.markdownMaxChars) and footnotes (at most rules.footnotesPerSection, and may be empty). A repository footnote (repoKinds) needs path, sha (7-64 lowercase hex: one with no sha is refused), lines { start, end } (1-based, inclusive) and verified, the writer's own check of its quote at that sha; section, symbol, quote, excerpt and viaEntryId are optional. A record footnote (recordKinds) needs ref, the record's id; chars { start, end } (code points of the record's redacted text, end exclusive), quote and viaEntryId are optional. viaEntryId, when given, is an entry of the space. A quote is at most rules.quoteMaxChars; null or left out is no quote. A section's dispositions (optional; at most rules.dispositionsPerSection) are its material's ledger (dispositions): each names the material by the id the build gave it (material, at most 16 characters), its kind (a repoKind or a recordKind), where it is (ref: a repository path with its lines, path#Lstart-end, or a record's id), what became of it (action, one of dispositionActions), the material it was merged into (into: required for merge, null otherwise) and why (reason, not blank, at most rules.reasonMaxChars).

dispositionActions.adopt: the model's merge adopted it: it was handed to the writer
dispositionActions.merge: the model's merge folded it into another piece of the same section (into), which says the same thing with more weight or later; it was handed to the writer beside it
dispositionActions.drop: the model's merge dropped it — superseded, off the section's subject, or a guess — and the writer never saw it
dispositionActions.over_cap: the build never handed it to the model: the section's material was full (build.rules.materialMaxChars) before its turn came
dispositionActions.filtered: the build took it out by rule before the model saw it: a platform-generated template message (build.templates), or the same text as another piece of the section

docs.dispositions: What became of each piece of a section's material, kept with the section it explains (wiki_doc_section.dispositions, dispositionsMigration): the merge's word for every piece it was handed — adopt, merge into another, or drop, each with its reason — and the build's for the pieces it never handed over (over_cap, filtered). A write stores the ledger as it came, beside the section it replaces; the ledger of a section left unchanged is left as it was. The reads return it with each section (reads.doc, reads.writerDoc).
docs.markdown: A section's body is Markdown with footnote markers [n], n naming its section's footnotes[n-1]. A first line that is a heading is the section's own title, which the plan names, and is dropped. A fenced code block is one code block and is not checked, and one whose info string is mermaid is a diagram (diagram) or nothing; any other heading line is a heading block; a list item (-, *, +, 1., 1), 1、) is an item block, and an indented line under it continues it; other lines up to a blank line are one paragraph (a leading > is dropped, a line of three dashes, stars or underscores is skipped). Paragraphs and items are cut into sentences as articles.validation.sentences cuts an article — at 。！？, and at a full stop or an ASCII ? or ! before a space or the line's end, outside code spans — so a ； ends nothing. A marker outside a code span names a footnote; one outside 1 to the section's footnote count names none and is dropped (stats.markersDropped), and a run of markers with no words is not a sentence. A section with no sentence is refused.

diagram.means: A section may draw one diagram: a fenced block whose info string is mermaid, which the write prompt offers to the section kinds rules.kinds name (build.server). The server reads it as the flowchart syntax states and writes it out again in one spelling, which is the diagram block's text: its own node and subgraph ids (n1…, s1…), every label quoted, and " # < > & in a label written as Mermaid's entity codes. So a page draws only what was read. A block that is not that flowchart, or is past rules' sizes, is no diagram: it is dropped, and never kept as code.
diagram.syntax: The first line is flowchart or graph and a direction (TB, TD, BT, LR or RL; TB when there is none). After it, one statement a line, a trailing ; dropped and %% lines skipped: a chain of nodes joined by links; subgraph <id>, subgraph <id>[title] or subgraph <title>, closed by end; direction inside a subgraph; and style, classDef, class, linkStyle and click lines, which are skipped. A node is an id (words of [A-Za-z0-9_] joined by - or .) with a shape or none — [ ], ( ), ([ ]), [[ ]], [( )], (( )), { } or {{ }} — around its label, quoted or not; a :::class after it is dropped. A link is -->, ---, -.->, -.-, ==>, ===, <-->, <-.-> or <==> (a longer run of - or = reads as the same link), with a label as -->|text| or -- text -->. Either end of a link may be a list of nodes joined with &, which links each node of one end to each of the other, and every such link counts against rules.edgesMax. A node stands where Mermaid draws it: in the first subgraph that names it — in a statement of its own or in a link, before or after the node first appears — and in none when no subgraph names it, so a diagram that writes its links first and its subgraphs after keeps them. A subgraph's id may be a link's end; a node the diagram labels under the same id is a node of its own, and the link ends at the node. Anything else — another kind of diagram, an end with no subgraph, a subgraph never closed — is no diagram.
diagram.labels:
A label's text has its markers ([n], [D1]) and backticks taken out,
read as a space and its whitespace collapsed. The texts a diagram shows are each node's label (its id when it has none), each link's label and each subgraph's title (its id when it has none).
diagram.check: Once a write's footnotes are checked, a diagram is kept when every fact token (factTokens) of the texts it shows is found in its sources, or is one of rules.structureWords. Its sources are the section's sentences that carry a verified footnote; the quote and excerpt of those verified footnotes; the sentences that stand sourced in the document's other sections, as the document stands when the write arrives; and its headings as classification reads them, a heading of another written section included. A section being written gives nothing from its old text. A token of letters is compared without its ending (-ies and -ied read as -i, then -ing, -ed, -es or -s, then a last -e, and a last -y read as -i), so stored and store are one word; a code name, a path or a number is compared as it is. The words inside the sources' fact tokens count as well: a code name, a path or a compound read word by word, letters alone, so `sessionId` gives session and `wiki-worker` gives wiki and worker. That reading is of the sources only: a code name in a label is compared whole, so one made of a source's parts is not found. The first diagram that passes is kept, as rules.perSection allows. Every other one is dropped with its block, the sentences after it moving up a block. stats.diagrams counts the diagrams kept and stats.diagramsDropped the ones dropped, here or as no diagram. A diagram holds no sentence: it is in no count, and a section of nothing but a diagram says nothing.
diagram.fingerprint: A section of a kind rules.kinds names takes rules.version into its fingerprint, so raising the version writes each such section once more at the next build that takes it up.
diagram.pages: The web's document page and a shared document draw the diagram with Mermaid (strict security, the page's light or dark theme), and show its source as code when it does not draw. The macOS, iOS and Android apps draw it the same way, with the Mermaid build the web pins carried in the app, in a web view that loads nothing else, and show its source as code when it does not draw.

verification.records: The server reads the record again, among the account's own rows, through the one reader a record has (WikiService.sourceText, whose texts wiki-verify-evidence.ts defines: runEventText for an event, a tool call's name, input and output together, an approval's answers and note — and the plan it decided — a merge receipt's and an owner decision's line as the dossier writes them), so a document and an entry citing the same record check their quotes against the same words; it redacts it with the shared redactor and the owner's workspace.env values, and looks for the quote — redacted the same way — in it, both folded (normalization). chars, when given, narrows the search to that range. The range the quote was found at is stored (char_start, char_end: code points of the redacted text), and so are the record's session, number, time and label, for the page's link. A translated, paraphrased or spliced quote — two passages of the record joined as one — is not found.
verification.repository: The server has no checkout. A repository footnote carries the writer's check of its quote against the lines it names (verified), made on the file as the runner read it at the commit it names (sha, repoOps.kinds.read); a footnote with no sha is refused. excerpt, when the writer gives it, is those lines as read, redacted, for the page to show.
verification.normalization: Before a quote is compared, quote and original alike are folded: Unicode NFC; the full-width punctuation ，。：；（）！？「」“”‘’、『』【】—– read as its ASCII counterpart; ** and __ and backticks dropped; a Markdown escape read as the character it escapes; every whitespace dropped. The original is compared a second time with each line's leading comment marker (//, ///, /*, *, */ or #) taken off, so a quote of a comment's words is found. A quote is one passage: an ellipsis is not a gap to skip.

docs.factTokens: A sentence's fact tokens: each code span (its content); each ASCII identifier or path ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_./-]*[A-Za-z0-9_]) of at least 3 characters that is not one of the, and, for, with, not, are, can, its, but, via; each number of two or more digits; and each number with a unit (秒 分钟 小时 天 个 条 次 % ms s MB KB) — matched in that order, lowercased, whitespace dropped.
docs.classification: A sentence with a footnote is sourced when one of its footnotes is verified and unverified when none is; withdrawn when one of them came through an entry withdrawal names. A sentence with none is a transition when every fact token in it is among those of the document's sourced sentences and headings — its plan sections' titles, the heading blocks of its written sections, its title and its question — and unsourced otherwise, its new tokens stored with it.
