The whole document is classified again each time a section of it is written, so a transition answers to what the other sections say now. The document is needs_review when its unsourced and unverified sentences are more than rules.needsReviewAbove of all of them; withdrawn sentences are not counted among those: they wait for their section to be written again.
docs.fingerprint: materialSha256 is the build's (docs.build.server): sha256 over the section's definition in the plan (title, kind, covers, length, sources) and the material it gathered for it, as it gathered it. An overview's material is its document's other sections: its fingerprint is taken over its definition and theirs, so it is written again whenever one of them is. The repository's commit is not in it — only what was read at it — so a commit that changed nothing a section cites leaves the section as it is. A section of a kind diagram.rules.kinds names takes diagram.rules.version into it as well (diagram.fingerprint). The server does not recompute it; it compares it with the one stored.
docs.repoSha: Every section is stored with the origin/main commit it was generated at (repoSha, from the write that wrote it), and a document with its last write's. A maintenance run compares a section's repoSha with origin/main as it stands, and writes again a section whose design documents, code or contracts changed since (owner 2026-09-29: the wiki follows what agents write into docs/); that comparison is the run's, and the server only keeps the sha and hands it back (reads.writerState, reads.doc).
docs.regeneration: A section whose stored materialSha256 is the one a write names, and from which nothing was withdrawn (stale_at null), is not written again: its outcome is unchanged and its rows are left as they are. Every other section a write names is replaced whole, its sentences and footnotes with it. A write names the confirmed plan version it was written from (planVersion); one that is not the confirmed version is WIKI_PLAN_STALE and writes nothing. A section the confirmed plan's document no longer has is dropped when the document is next written. No clock rewrites anything (hard constraint 5): the maintenance run writes after facts arrived.
docs.withdrawal: When an entry is rejected, retired or superseded, or its anchor state becomes changed or missing, every sentence with a footnote that came through it (via entry) is withdrawn — status withdrawn, with when, why (withdrawReasons) and the entry — and its section is marked stale (stale_at), so the next maintenance run writes it again. It happens in the entry's own transaction, at its single state writer (WikiService.recomputeFlags, which every applyOp branch ends in; storage.singleWriter), so no path that moves an entry can forget it. A write with a footnote that comes through such an entry stores that sentence withdrawn, and its section stale, at once; and it takes its via entries FOR SHARE before anything else, so a rejection racing it waits for it and then withdraws what it wrote.
docs.withdrawalPaths: A repository file a section's footnotes cite that a maintenance run found deleted or renamed on origin/main (maintenance.job.docs.byRepo) withdraws every sentence of the space's documents with a footnote citing it — status withdrawn, anchor_missing, with when and the path (withdrawn_path) in place of an entry — and marks its section stale (WikiDocs.withdrawPaths). A sentence names the entry or the path that withdrew it, one of the two (migration 0340's CHECK). The documents are taken in id order as a write and an entry's withdrawal take them.

affected.means: What a maintenance run writes again because of the entries, and what it may propose (reads.affected): the server's half of maintenance.job.docs. The repository's half is the run's, read at the space's snapshot through the runner (maintenance.job.docs.byRepo).
affected.fit: An entry fits a section's session condition when a keyword is in its title, summary, fields or aliases, one of its anchors' paths is under one of anchorPaths, or — when it is of one of entryKinds, or the condition names none — one of its topics is one of topics, or one of its live sources is a record of a session or a task of one of projects (a session of one of the project's tasks, or its coordinator's; the task, or a comment on it). It scores 3 a keyword, 2 a path, 1 a topic, 1 a kind, 1 a project. material.entries picks a section's entries by the same rule.
affected.sections: A written section of the confirmed plan is written again when an entry that fits it had an op applied to it after the section was generated, or when it is stale.
affected.unplaced: An entry an op applied to since the space's first plan version was made, live and with its anchors standing, that fits no section of the confirmed plan and that no proposal of the space names, whatever became of the proposal — newest first, at most rules.unplacedMax, unplacedMore counting the rest.

links.sessionRecord: A footnote on a turn, an event or a tool call carries the record's id (recordId) and the session it is in (sessionId), both read when the write checked it: wiki_source keeps a record's id alone, and the page needs the pair to link the record — web sessionRecordHref(sessionId, recordId), iOS SessionRecordLink.url(session:record:), which open the session at it through GET /api/sessions/:id/events/page?around=<recordId>. Any other record carries what it is in: an approval or a merge receipt its session (sessionId), a task comment its task (taskId), an owner decision its project (projectId), a note its path (notePath).
links.repository: A repository footnote carries its path, sha and lines (path@sha#Lstart-end): the page links that file at that commit in the space's repository.

view.push: Never in <orbit_wiki_context>: the push reads wiki_entry and nothing else.
view.source: Never a source: no source kind names a document, a section, a sentence or a footnote (sourceRules.firstHand), so citing one is WIKI_SOURCE_UNRESOLVED.
view.agents: Never returned by wiki_search or wiki_get: both read entries alone, and a document's ids are no entry's.
view.readers: The owner, on the user door. Another owner's space or document is a plain 404.

who.write: The server's docs_build and maintain jobs (build.server; origin maintenance, no session and no user) — and, once it is a kind, the docs_follow job (follow), as theirs — and an import the API server's container runs itself (origin import, no session and no user). No door builds a document, and the user door's one write is the owner's restore of a version a section kept (versions.restore), which brings back text a job wrote and writes none of its own: any other caller is an error of the server's own code (WikiDocs.assertWriter). Every write asks requireConfirmedPlan first (plan.guard): with no confirmed plan it is WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED.
who.read: The owner, on the user door.

reads.directory: { spaceId, plan: { version, confirmedAt } | null, docs: { total, written }, categories }: the confirmed plan's categories in its order (number from 1), each with its documents (number <category>.<n>, title, question, written, status, updatedAt, planVersion, and lead: its two lines on the home, null for one not written — lead) and each document's sections (number, title, kind, written, stale). A space with no confirmed plan has none.
reads.doc: One document of the confirmed plan: its number, title, question, audience, scope (scopeOut's documents with their number and title), category, length, status, and when, from which plan version and at which origin/main commit (repoSha) it was written; its sections in the plan's order, each with the commit it was generated at and its blocks, a block's sentences each with its id (a public id: what a chat's selection names, chat.notes.wikiContext), its status, its footnote numbers, its new tokens and, once withdrawn, why, when, and through which entry or for which repository file (entryId, path — one of the two); its footnotes, numbered by first appearance — the same original and quote cited twice is one number — each with its kind, verdict, who checked it, its quote, its location (path@sha#Lstart-end, or <kind>:<record id>#c<start>-<end>) and what the page links to (links): a repository original's path, sha, lines, section, symbol and excerpt; a record's id (recordId), character range, session (sessionId, with recordId the pair a turn's, an event's or a tool call's deep link needs) and its title, number, time and label, task and project and their titles, a note's path; and its via entry; and the via entries as they stand now, with the footnotes each carried. A document of the plan not written yet is written false with its sections unwritten; one the plan does not have is a 404. counts and unsourcedShare are its sentences' as they stand.
reads.index: Every document of the confirmed plan, and every section whose title no other document of the plan shares — the ones every document has (known pitfalls, conventions, overview) are left out — each with its document's number and title, its category and whether it is written, in title order.
reads.writerState: { spaceId, planVersion, docs: [{ slug, planVersion, status, repoSha, updatedAt, sections: [{ key, materialSha256, repoSha, stale, generatedAt }] }] }: what is written, for a run to tell which sections to write again — a stale one, one whose material changed, or one whose repoSha origin/main has moved past in what it cites.
reads.writerDoc: One document as it is written, for the server's build and maintenance jobs: the same answer as reads.doc. A job reads it to write a document's overview when the sections it summarizes were left unchanged, their sentences and footnotes as they stand.
reads.material: A section of the document in the confirmed plan: { spaceId, slug, section, planVersion, condition, entries, records, unresolved } — the server's half of the section's material (material), gathered in process by the jobs that write (gatherDocMaterial): the section's session condition as the plan states it (null when it has none, and then nothing else), the entries it picked as the way in, and every record found through them or by the condition's projects, window and keywords, each redacted and placed.
reads.affected: { spaceId, plan: { version, confirmedAt, repoSha, draftedAt } | null, build: { jobId, state, version } | null, sections: [{ doc, key, repoSha, generatedAt, stale, entryIds }], unplaced: [{ id, kind, title, summary, topics, anchorPaths, changedAt }], unplacedMore, proposed: { entryIds, commits, paths }, topics: [{ slug, title, active }] } (WikiDocsAffected, affected): the confirmed plan (null with none: the run writes no document), the space's build that has not ended, the written sections to write again with the entries that fit them, the entries no section fits, what the space's proposals already name — their entries, commits and the design documents their changes cite — and the space's topics, oldest first, each with its active entries: the ones plan.gate.references takes in a session condition, which a run checks its proposal's new sections against before the gate does (2026-10-10). repoSha is the commit the plan's references were last checked at: the confirmed version's, or the newest of the versions it was made from. What the maintenance run reads in process (wikiDocsAffected).

lead.means: A written document's lead on the directory (reads.directory): the first rules.sentences sentences of its first section — first as the confirmed plan orders its sections — in their order, withdrawn ones left out, joined as they read (a space after a Latin stop, none after a full-width one) and, past rules.maxChars characters, cut there with an ellipsis (…). The sentences' text as the document page has it, inline marks and all. Null for a document not written, and for one whose first section is not written or has no sentence that is not withdrawn.

requests.write: { planVersion, repoSha, model?, sections: [{ key, materialSha256, markdown, footnotes: [{ kind, path, sha, lines, section?, symbol?, quote?, excerpt?, verified, viaEntryId? } | { kind, ref, chars?, quote?, viaEntryId? }], dispositions?: [{ material, kind, ref, action, into, reason }] }] }
requests.withdraw: { repoSha, paths: [{ path, change: deleted | renamed, to? }] }: the origin/main commit the paths are gone at (40 hex), and at most affected.rules.withdrawPathsMax paths. Answered { spaceId, withdrawn, sections: [{ doc, key }] }: the sentences withdrawn now, and the sections they are in. Malformed is WIKI_DOC_INVALID with every error.

material.means: The server's half of a section's material (reads.material): what only the database has. The repository's half — design-document sections, code and contracts at origin/main — is read at the space's snapshot of origin/main, through the runner (build.repository, build.server.repository).
material.entries: The space's live entries (status active, anchor state neither changed nor missing) that fit the section's session condition (affected.fit), best first: an entry scores 3 for each keyword in its title, summary, fields or aliases, 2 when one of its anchors' paths is under one of anchorPaths, 1 when one of its topics is one of topics, 1 when its kind is one of entryKinds, and 1 when it was taken from one of projects; only one that fits is taken — a keyword or a path found it, or, of the condition's kinds, a topic or a project did — the newest first among equal scores, at most rules.entriesPerSection. Each is the way in to the records its current revision cites (at most rules.sourcesPerEntry of its live sources, in the order it cites them): an entry is never the material itself.
material.search: With projects and keywords both named, the owner's own words in them (a message or a steer isOwnerTurn reads as the owner's, in a project's coordinator session or a session of one of its tasks) and the comments on their tasks, within since..until (days, until included) and carrying one of the keywords, case aside: the ones carrying the most keywords first, the newest among equal, at most rules.ownerTurnsPerSection turns and rules.commentsPerSection comments.
material.projects: A condition's projects are ids, however the plan reached its reader. A stored version names each project by the id its reference resolved to (plan.gate.references); a read of a version (plan.reads.version) names each { id, title }. Every reader of a condition takes either as the id and leaves out anything that is no id: reads.material, the server's documents build (build.server.material), the maintenance run's documents step, which reads the plan through that read (maintenance.job.server), affected.fit, and the plan's own reads and gate. (2026-10-09: the maintenance run's documents step passed the read's { id, title } on as ids, PostgreSQL refused them with 22P02, and the step wrote no section.)
material.records: Every record is read through the one reader a record has (WikiService.sourceText) and redacted with the shared redactor and the owner's workspace.env values, as a footnote's check reads it (verification.records). It is returned whole when it is at most rules.excerptChars long, and otherwise the rules.excerptChars around what found it — its entry source's quote, or the first keyword — with chars { start, end }: where the text is in the record's redacted text, in code points (a record footnote's chars). A record met twice is returned once, the first time. A source whose record is not one of this account's any more is listed under unresolved, never read.

weights.decision: the owner's own words: a message or steer isOwnerTurn reads as the owner's, an AskUserQuestion the owner answered, an owner's decision or comment
weights.merge: a record of what was merged or delivered: a merge receipt, an agent's delivery comment
weights.output: what a command or tool printed: a tool call (its command and output together), a tool's result, a background task's report
weights.error: what failed: a tool's error, an error event
weights.other: everything else: an agent's reply or thinking, another turn, a task, a note

material.weightsNote: The evidence weight the merge reads each record with: decision > merge > output > error, the newest first within one weight (owner 2026-09-28). A mechanism is the code's to settle, not a record's.

build.does: For each document of the confirmed plan, section by section: gathers the section's material — its design-document sections, code symbols and contracts from the space's snapshot of origin/main, read through the runner (server.repository), and the server's half (reads.material) — takes out the platform's template messages and repeated texts, and keeps what fits rules.materialMaxChars, a mechanism's sections taking documents and code first and the others records first; fingerprints it (fingerprint) and leaves a section whose fingerprint is the one reads.writerState holds, and from which nothing was withdrawn, unwritten, without asking the model. Otherwise the System model merges the material (adopt, merge into another, drop, each with a reason; decision > merge > output > error, the newest first; the code settles a mechanism) and writes the section from the pieces it kept, a verbatim quote for every footnote it marks; a repository quote is looked for at the snapshot's commit, and its lines are the lines it was found at. Each section is written as soon as it is done, with its dispositions. A document's overview is written last, from its other sections as they are written, citing their footnotes and quotes and nothing else.
build.repository: A design document's section is its heading's lines up to the next heading of the same or a higher level; a code symbol its definition with the comment above it, up to where its braces close; a code path with no symbols named its head comment and the declarations whose words match the section; a directory the first files under it; a contract the file — each cut at a line boundary to fit, and read at the commit the space's snapshot of origin/main names (repoSha, server.repository). A path that is no file or directory of that commit but holds a wildcard — an unescaped *, ? or [ — is read as an empty file, as git show reads such a pathspec (server.wildcard).
build.templates: A turn that begins About “ and says Orbit has not recorded it done is the project settlement card's message (the web composes it; the owner only presses the button), not the owner's words: it is filtered.
build.rulesNote: materialMaxChars is the most characters of material one section hands the model, each piece counted with materialHeaderChars for its header; the first piece is handed over whatever its size. parallel is the most sections of one document in flight at once.

server.made: The owner's confirmation of a version asks for its build (plan.jobs.request): it is made as a docs_build job of the wiki-worker (jobs.kindRuns.docs_build), the plan job made with the job's id (wiki_plan_job.job_id) and the job queued at `priority` with input { planJobId }, in one transaction. A space whose maintenance names no workspace holds it (plan.jobs.held.no_maintenance_workspace): the job reads the repository through that workspace's runner. No provider is asked about: no session's model is in it.
server.repository: The commit is origin/main as a snapshot names it (repoOps.kinds.snapshot, skipped when the space holds that commit's): the runner's fetch. The files a section's sources name are read whole at that commit (repoOps.kinds.read, no section: the whole file, cached by (space, sha, path) and read from the runner only once, packed into operations by the snapshot's sizes up to repoOps.read.operationBytes, `readsInFlight` operations at once, a failed one asked again up to `readAttempts` times in all), and the writer cuts a design document's section, a symbol, the declarations and a contract out of them exactly as `repository` says, at the same lines. A directory shows as git shows a tree, from the snapshot's paths. A file larger than repoOps.read.wholeFileBytes is not read at all: it is missing with that reason, and a heading, symbol or contract in it says so. A space whose runner has not declared the whole-file capability reads each file only to repoOps.read.boundedChars (repoOps.looks runner_upgrade): a heading or a symbol past that window is missing and says so, and in such a file only the heading a section names, by its words or its number, is looked for, never one that merely contains the name, which could be another section. Each operation is waited for holding the job's lease (the exception repoOps.waiting names), at most `repoWaitSeconds`; a space whose runner cannot be asked (repoOps.looks no_workspace, runner_missing or runner_offline), and an operation past its limit, are infra failures, tried again.
server.shown: A file is shown only once its read has landed. The sections of a document are built rules.parallel at a time and often name one file: a section whose file another section is already reading waits for that read, rather than starting none of its own and showing the file before it lands. (2026-10-09: version 27 named docs/article-durable-agent-work.md in several sections of one document, and every attempt of its build failed with «was shown before it was read».)
server.wildcard: A source's path that is no file or directory of the commit but holds a wildcard — an unescaped *, ? or [ — shows as an empty file, as git show shows it: git takes <sha>:<path> for a pathspec (looks_like_pathspec), exits 0 and prints nothing. A document source with no section is then a design_doc piece with nothing in it, a code source with no symbols a head piece with nothing in it, a contract one with nothing in it; a section or a symbol named in such a file is missing, as in any file that lacks it. An escaped wildcard (\*) is no pattern, and the path is missing as any path the commit lacks. The pattern is never expanded to the files it would match. The documents' build, a maintenance run's comparison of two commits and its proposal check all read through one reader (WikiDocsSnapshotRepo). The server read such a path as git show read it to the runner's writer, so both paths answered alike (2026-10-10); P11 kept the reading (2026-10-19): no confirmed plan of production names such a path (a read-only count, 2026-10-10), and reading it as no file would mean recomputing the documents' golden answers and the overview's expectations by hand — more risk than gain.
server.material: A section's session condition is read in process through src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-docs-material.ts, exactly as reads.material reads it: the entries it picks, the records they cite and the ones its projects, window and keywords find, each redacted with the owner's workspace.env values and placed.
server.calls: Every model call is a request through the queue (modelQueue): the system prompt `systemPrompt` (the runner's writer's, word for word), one user message, max_tokens `maxTokens`, the step one of `steps` — merge, write, rewrite (a paragraph marked only at its end, asked for once more), quotes (a footnote with no quote that holds, asked about once more) and overview — and a unit made of the document, the section and the sha256 of the prompt, so a replay reuses every answer whose question did not change. The queue retries a 5xx, a 429 and a dropped connection; a 401 stops the whole queue (modelQueue.retry). The prompts and every deterministic step — the filter, the cap, the fingerprint, the merge and the draft as read, the footnotes and their lines — are the runner's writer's: src/shared/src/wiki-docs-build.fixture.json, which its Go test wrote before P11, holds one answer, and src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-docs-build-golden.spec.ts holds the server's writer to it.
server.write: Through WikiDocs.write, the write route's own writer, as the server's own principal (origin maintenance, no session, no user: who.write): one section a write, the run's writes one at a time, model the System model's name. A refusal (WIKI_DOC_INVALID, WIKI_PLAN_STALE, WIKI_PLAN_UNCONFIRMED) fails its section, in the words the runner's writer used.
server.nul: Everything a section's write carries — the markdown, the footnotes' quotes and excerpts, the dispositions' reasons — goes to WikiDocs.write without any U+0000 (jobs.serverWrites): they are the lines a document shows, and Postgres keeps no NUL in text; a footnote's excerpt is the code's lines, which can have the NUL of a file, and a model can copy one into its text. The material the model is shown keeps it (modelQueue.requestEncoding), and the file it comes from is kept whole in the read cache (repoOps.storedText).
server.progress: As each document is taken up and at the end: the plan job's progress (plan.jobs.progress, a build's { docs: { done, total }, current }) and the job's own (jobs.progress: { step: snapshot | documents, docs, current }).
server.end: Every section it took up written or unchanged: the plan job ends succeeded with the confirmed version it wrote and the build's report (plan.jobs.buildReport), and the job succeeds with the run's summary as its report. A section left unwritten: the other sections are tried, then the plan job ends failed (`<n> sections were left unwritten`) and the job fails as content, its report on the row. A failure of the platform (the runner away, an operation or a request past its limit, the worker stopping) ends neither: the job is tried again and replays, and a section already written is left as it is by its fingerprint. A replay that finds its plan job already ended answers with that end. The job's report and the plan job's build report are the whole build's (jobs.carry): a section an earlier attempt wrote is carried on the job's row as it is written, and the replay that finds it unchanged by that fingerprint counts it written, once; the calls and usage are every request of the job, each once, and the seconds run from the job's first claim.
server.systemPrompt: You are Orbit's technical writer. You write only from the materials you are given, and invent no fact, name, number or path. Write in English; keep code names, paths and commands as they are. Output only what is asked for.

follow.phase: wiki chat, contract C2 (2026-11-06); docs/wiki-comment-to-session-design.md section 12.1 kept, its runner path dropped
follow.doc: docs/wiki-contract.md section 29; docs/wiki-chat-design.md sections 8.1 to 8.3 and 8.5
follow.means: Any change that reaches main, and any press of a chat's card, has the wiki follow at once: the sections it touched are written again by the wiki-worker, without waiting for maintenance to be due (twenty sessions or twenty-four hours) and without skipping a space that catches up (design section 8.1). A press's sections are always written; a merge's only where a file they cite changed.
follow.kind: docs_follow, a wiki_job the wiki-worker runs. It is in jobs.kinds, jobs.kindRuns and jobs.carry.kinds, and in wiki_job_kind_chk with jobs.onePerSpace's two indexes since migration 0477 (C4); the wiki-worker runs it (src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-docs-follow-job.ts), and the facts are joined in src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-docs-follow.ts. No runner runs it: P11 removed the runner's documents path, so there is no orbit wiki docs follow (the 2026-10-09 design's section 11.7 is void).

triggers.press: An Apply or Edit of a chat's card that has rewrites, and its Try again (chat.presses): the card's sections, forced, at priorities.press, made in the press's own transaction.
triggers.merge: A session's merge receipt into main — a landed result whose target is the repository's main (session_merge_receipt) — at priorities.chatMerge when the session is a chat, else priorities.merge, made after the receipt's transaction commits.
triggers.landing: A landing line's receipt into main — a MAIN line task's landing, or a project's promotion recorded MERGED (docs/project-integration-line-contract.md) — at priorities.landing, made after the receipt's transaction commits.
triggers.none: Nothing else makes one: no clock, no schedule, no sweep (hard constraint 5); with no fact there is no job. A commit pushed to main outside Orbit has no fact: the next follow job or maintenance run compares with main as it then stands and takes it in. A merge into any other branch is no fact until a landing takes it to main.

follow.space: The spaces of the receipt's owner whose repository is the receipt's (its session's workspace, or its project's codebase, normalized as space.repoUrlNorm normalizes it). A space with no confirmed plan writes no document, and none is made for it.
follow.queue: At most one queued follow job a space. A fact arriving while one is queued joins it in one write — its forced sections and their presses appended, its merges appended, its priority raised to the highest it now carries — and one arriving while one runs queues the next, which runs once it ends. Facts are joined under the space's row lock (wiki_space FOR NO KEY UPDATE, the lock the space's plan and maintenance writers take), so two facts at once make one job; a change of main a follow job of the space already carries — the same receipt delivered twice, or the receipts a promotion writes for each of its tasks, one range of commits — is carried once.

sections.forced: A press's sections are written whatever their fingerprint: the press marks each stale (stale_at, docs.withdrawal's mark) in its own transaction, so docs.regeneration writes it again.
sections.merges: For the merges it carries, each written section of the confirmed plan whose repoSha the job's snapshot of origin/main has moved past in a file it cites, by the comparison a maintenance run makes (maintenance.job.docs.byRepo, docs.repoSha) narrowed to the files those commits changed; a cited file the range deleted or renamed away is withdrawn first (docs.withdrawalPaths). A section whose fingerprint did not change asks no model and writes nothing (docs.regeneration).
sections.overview: A document some of whose sections were written has its overview handed to the writer as a build hands it, and written as its fingerprint decides.

follow.material: Each section's material is the build's (docs.material, docs.build), and a forced section is handed two things more (design section 8.2), so that entriesPerSection cannot squeeze out the entry the owner just applied and the section come back as it was: the entries the card wrote, as they stand after it, each with its live sources (docs.material.rules.sourcesPerEntry); and the owner's turns in the chat, as records the writer may cite — a turn is first-hand (sourceRules.firstHand), a document or a sentence of one never is (docs.view.source). A merge's sections are handed, besides, the files its commits changed, cut as docs.build.repository cuts a section's sources and read at the job's snapshot. Every sentence is still quoted from a first-hand original and checked word for word (docs.verification).
follow.catchUp: A space that catches up (maintenance.job.catchUp) still follows: catch-up skips a maintenance run's documents step, never a follow job, which writes only what changed.
follow.daily: Of the sections merges and landings ask for — never a press's — a space's follow jobs write at most rules.sectionsPerDay in one UTC day, counted as the sections its follow jobs wrote for them since midnight UTC (a section left unchanged costs nothing and is not counted). A job that would pass it writes them in the plan's order up to what is left and leaves the rest as they are — still behind main, so the next maintenance run writes them (maintenance.job.docs) — and its report says how many it left (report.left), which Activity says (docs.versions.reads.changes, copy.changes.leftOne and leftMany). A press's sections are neither counted nor left.
follow.priority: The highest of what it carries: priorities.press for a press, priorities.chatMerge for a chat's merge, priorities.merge and priorities.landing otherwise. At 1 it is the owner's work, ahead of background maintenance (jobs.priority), and its model calls carry it into the queue (modelQueue.priority).
follow.run: The wiki-worker runs it as docs.build.server runs a build, over its sections alone (runWikiDocsBuild's only): the snapshot of origin/main through the runner of the space's maintenance workspace — which need not be the chat's (design section 5) — the reads, the model calls through the queue under docs.build.server.steps and units of their own, so a replay reuses every answer, and each section written through WikiDocs.write as soon as it is done (docs.who.write).
follow.exclusion: It runs beside a job of its space that writes no document and waits for one that does (jobs.onePerSpace).

waiting.rule: Why a follow job that is not running waits, by wikiDocsFollowWaiting (src/shared/src/wikiChat.ts): a queued one first for a job of its space that writes documents and runs — maintain, docs_build, plan_draft or plan_revise, or another docs_follow, each reason naming which — then for the System model (its read state, systemModel.read, when it is not up), then for the runner its repository is read through (repoOps.looks, when it is not ready); a parked one (waiting_for) for what it is parked on. A queued job none of these holds up is merely in line: rewriting, not waiting. Each reason is said in copy.waiting, on the card and on Activity alike; Settings is offered beside no_workspace and runner_missing, which the owner fixes in Wiki settings.

follow.outcomes: Each section it takes up ends written (its sentences replaced), unchanged (its fingerprint the stored one, nothing withdrawn: only a merge's), gone (the confirmed plan no longer has it: design section 10's Section no longer in the plan; it is not written), or failed (left unwritten: the model failed, or its quotes did not check out). A forced section that was written reads updated when docs.versions.compare finds a sentence changed against the version it replaced, and same when none did: it reads the same, and the card says so rather than pretend (design section 8.3). The job succeeds when no section it took up failed, and otherwise fails as content with the others written, as a build does (docs.build.server.end); an infra failure is retried (jobs.retry).
follow.report: { sections: [{ doc, key, outcome, changed, versionId, forced, draftIds }], left, usage } on the job (jobs.progress, jobs.carry): the card read and Activity's changes read read it; the jobs read does not (jobs.read.never).
follow.activity: The job is a row of Activity's Runs card as any job (jobs.read). What it wrote is in Recently changed as Docs rows with their reasons (docs.versions.reads.changes), and a job that left sections for maintenance adds the row that says how many.
follow.versions: Every section it writes keeps the version it replaced (docs.versions), with the reason of the fact that asked for it: chat for a press, merge or landing for a receipt.

versions.phase: wiki chat, contract C2 (2026-11-06); docs/wiki-comment-to-session-design.md section 12.2 kept
versions.means: Any section written again — by maintenance, a build or a follow job — keeps the sentences it replaced and why, so the document page and Activity can say what changed and after what (design section 8.4), and a chat's Undo can put a section back.
versions.kept: Every write that replaces a section — any section a write names whose outcome is not unchanged (docs.regeneration) — keeps the section it replaced as a version, in WikiDocs.write's own transaction, whoever wrote it: a maintenance run, a build, a follow job or a restore. A section written for the first time replaced nothing and keeps nothing; one left unchanged was not written again and keeps nothing.
versions.row: Its owner, space, document slug and section key; the blocks, sentences (text, status, footnote numbers, new tokens, withdrawal) and footnotes the section held, as they were; the section's repoSha, materialSha256 and generatedAt then; why it was replaced (reasons); when; and what replaced it — the job, or the owner's restore.
versions.retention: At most rules.perSection versions a section: keeping one more deletes the oldest in the same transaction.

reasons.build: A build of a plan version (its job, the version).
reasons.merge: A follow job, for a session's merge into main (the session's title and the commit).
reasons.landing: A follow job, for a landing into main (the task's or the project's title and the commit).
reasons.chat: A follow job, for a chat's press (the chat's title and the card): After chat <title>.
reasons.words: wikiDocVersionReason says a reason as a row reads it (copy.reasons), wikiDocVersionHeading as See changes heads it, with the commit when there is one: After <title> merged · 7f3e2a1.

versions.compare: Sentence by sentence (design section 8.4: See changes), by wikiDocSentenceDiff: a version's sentences against the text that replaced it — the next version's, or the section as it stands for the newest — as their longest common subsequence, compared by text with outer whitespace trimmed and inner runs of it read as one space, a removal drawn before the addition where both orders are as long. Each sentence is same, removed (struck through) or added (shaded); changed counts each run of removed and added sentences as the larger of the two, so one sentence rewritten is one change. A heading, a code block or a diagram is no sentence and is not compared.

reads.doc: The document read (docs.reads.doc) gives each section its latest change — change: { versionId, reason, at, changed } or null — so the page can mark copy.card.sectionUpdated beside a section written since the reader last looked (wikiSeenKey, on the client) and open its versions.
reads.versions: { spaceId, slug, key, versions }: the section's versions, newest first, at most rules.perSection, each { id, reason, at, replacedBy, changed, rows } — rows and changed its comparison with the text that replaced it. A section the confirmed plan does not have is a 404.
reads.changes: { spaceId, changes }: Activity's Docs rows for Recently changed, newest first, at most rules.changesListed — { kind: section, doc, key, where, title, versionId, reason, at, changed } for a version kept, and { kind: left, jobId, at, left } for a follow job that left sections for maintenance — each said by wikiDocChangeLine (copy.changes). The timeline (GET /api/wiki/spaces/:id/timeline) keeps its items as they are, ops alone, so no client reading it meets a row it does not know.

versions.restore: The owner's one write to a document (docs.who.write): POST /api/wiki/doc-versions/:id/restore puts the section back as the version kept it — its blocks, sentences and footnotes, its repoSha and its materialSha256, so the section counts by its old fingerprint and the next maintenance run does not write it again for nothing (design section 8.4) — and the text it replaces is kept as a version too (reason restore), so a restore is itself undone the same way. It writes as WikiDocs.write does (the via entries FOR SHARE first; a sentence through an entry since withdrawn is stored withdrawn and its section stale) and asks requireConfirmedPlan first; a section the confirmed plan no longer has is a 409, and so is a version of another section's. User door, JWT only: a session header is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY, a personal access token OWNER_INTERACTIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED, another owner's version is the plain 404. A chat's Undo restores through the same writer (chat.presses.undo).
versions.who: Kept by WikiDocs.write and its restore, read by the owner on the user door; no tool reads or writes one (docs.tool).

docs.tool: none: no MCP tool reads or writes a document. Writing is the server's jobs' (who.write); reading is the owner's, in the Wiki.

chat.doc: docs/wiki-contract.md section 28; docs/wiki-chat-design.md sections 3 to 7 and 12
chat.why: The owner's decisions of 2026-11-06 (docs/wiki-chat-design.md section 12.1): a round button at the bottom right of every wiki page opens a chat docked beside it, to talk while reading and change the wiki while talking. The chat is an ordinary session — tools, approvals, permission modes, cost, the session list and the phone all as they are — of the workspace the owner chose for the space, in a worktree of its own started from origin/main. Its agent never changes a document's text, which the next rewrite would wash away: every request lands where a rewrite keeps it — an entry, a section's rewrite, the plan, or main (design section 6) — and the agent only drafts. Nothing is written until the owner presses Apply on the owner's door, which confirms what it writes, skips the machine's verification, and rewrites the sections it touches (docs.follow), each rewrite keeping the version it replaced (docs.versions).
chat.migrations: Made by the tasks that need them — session.wiki_chat_space_id with the chat (C5, migration 0476, beside conversation_turn.wiki_context: the ids a message's page and selection notes are read from at delivery; 0479 validates 0476's SOURCE CHECKs and builds session_wiki_chat_space_idx CONCURRENTLY), wiki_chat_draft with the presses (C6) — each numbered after a scan of main, every origin/project/* and the pushed orbit/* branches, and entered in the censuses: db-write-inventory, public-id-coverage's CONTROLLERS, PUBLIC_ID_FIELDS, the migration ledger and the personal-access-token decorators.
chat.rulesNote: selectionSentencesMax is the most sentences one selection attaches (design section 4.2): more is a section, which the page attachment names. rewritesMax is the most sections one card rewrites (design section 8.2). chatsListed is the most chats the list read names; its counts are over every chat of the space.

binding.rule: A nullable UUID on session, written by create alone, in the session row's own INSERT, and never afterwards: a session is a chat for its whole life or never. create writes only a space of the session's own owner, read under that owner. No foreign key (storage.ids: a reference into history): deleting a space leaves its chats as sessions, the id a tombstone, and their cards go with the space. Indexed by (wiki_chat_space_id, created_at) for list.
binding.is: A session is a chat exactly when wiki_chat_space_id is set. That alone makes its wiki_propose and the corrects of its wiki_note draft (agentSurface.chat), opens wiki_draft to it, has its first message carry notes.chat and its messages a wikiContext, gives it the SOURCE of source and a worktree of its own, keeps its draft calls out of the dossier (dossier), and puts it in list.
binding.read: GET /api/sessions/:id adds wikiChatSpaceId, the space's public id or null, so the session page can say where the chat came from (copy.panel.fromWiki) and open it beside the space's wiki. A chat is in its workspace's session list as any session is (design section 4.1).
binding.otherSessions: A session whose column is null is untouched by everything here: its wiki_propose, wiki_note and SOURCE are what they were.

workspace.eligible: A workspace of the space (space.binding: on its repository or named by a row, and not left out), not deleted and switched on (a session cannot start in one that is off), whose sessions run in worktrees of their own (workspace.enableWorktree). Nothing else is offered or stored: a chat never runs in a shared checkout.
workspace.choose: Chosen once for a space, at its first chat, among list.choices, and remembered in space.settings.chat.workspaceId; Runs in changes it (create with another workspaceId, or the settings PATCH). No default is worked out: the workspace a space's sessions last opened in, board 36's default, could carry the chat onto a production machine (design section 5.1). The orbit space's workspace, orbit-develop on HPC, is the owner's choice of 2026-11-06: their first pick there, never a name in the code.
workspace.none: With no eligible workspace the panel says copy.panel.noWorktree and offers no composer; the button is drawn as ever (design section 10).
workspace.gone: A remembered workspace that was deleted, left out or taken out of worktrees is neither used nor replaced: the panel asks again (list.workspace eligible false, copy.panel.chooseWorkspace).
workspace.offline: A workspace whose runner is offline stays the space's. A chat on it is made and waits for its runner as any session waits, the panel says copy.panel.offline with the machine's name, the wiki reads as usual, and nothing moves the chat to another machine (design section 5.1).

chat.source: origin/main, through the projects' SOURCE machinery (docs/project-source-contract.md SR54): create writes the selector in the session row's own INSERT — state SELECTED, kind CHAT_UPSTREAM, ref refs/heads/main, authority REMOTE asked through the remote origin, the chat workspace's repository as its identity, no codebase, no configRevision and nothing it must contain — and the first claim pins the commit through the three-step handshake (section 6.3 there), so the chat starts from main as it stood then, whatever the workspace's checkout has checked out. A resume, a reclaim or a takeover reads the pin and never resolves again. The runner tells by the session (needsSourcePin: a SOURCE state that is not UNBOUND), as for a project task. A refusal (section 10.1 there) is the chat's: on the session's SOURCE columns and in the panel with its fixAction, never on a task or a project; recovery is a new chat. Main moves while a chat goes on: each page and selection note carries its section's repoSha (notes), so the agent can tell a section written at an older main from the code it reads, and fetch origin/main when it matters (design section 5.2).
chat.branch: A chat that ends with no commit of its own leaves no branch: when its session ends, the runner deletes the worktree's branch if it holds nothing past the pinned commit (design section 5.2; a runner release). A chat with commits is any session's: its worktree bar, its Merge — the owner's press, never automatic — and, once the change reaches main, docs.follow.
chat.door: Every route is the user door's (JwtAuthGuard and WikiRolloutGuard), and another owner's space, chat or card is the plain 404 (refusalRules.notFound). A request with a session header (X-Orbit-Session-Id) is refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY whatever the session, as decide is (agentSurface.decide): no agent makes a chat, reads a card through this door or presses anything. The writes take only the owner's interactive credential — a personal access token is refused OWNER_INTERACTIVE_CREDENTIAL_REQUIRED, as the binding's writes are (space.binding.ownerChannel) — and the reads take a token with wiki:read. A :id is a public id, as every id on the user door; GET /api/wiki/chats/:id/drafts takes the chat's session id.

create.body: { workspaceId?, content, clientTurnId, wikiContext?, engine?, model?, permissionMode? }
create.rules: workspaceId, when given, must be eligible (workspace.eligible) and becomes the space's remembered one if it is another (Runs in); without it the remembered one is used, and with none eligible the request is a 400 saying to choose one. content is the owner's first message, word for word, and clientTurnId a UUID: the turn is filed as the session message door files the owner's — an explicit routing intent under the client's UUID — so its words are first-hand (reviewModes.tiered.auto.ownerWords) and a section may quote them as a source (docs.follow.material). wikiContext is held to notes.wikiContext. engine, model and permissionMode are New session's, each defaulting as a session of that workspace does.
create.makes: Through SessionsService.create, in one transaction: an ordinary session of the workspace — titled, listed, priced and approved as any — with wiki_chat_space_id set (binding), a worktree of its own required (a workspace that turned worktrees off meanwhile is refused 409, and nothing is made), the SOURCE selector of source, and its first turn. The first delivery appends notes.chat, then the turn's page and selection notes, to the owner's words.
create.answer: { sessionId, chat }: the session's public id, and its row as list serves it.

list.workspace: The remembered workspace as it stands — { id, name, runner, online, eligible } — or null when none is remembered: name and runner as space.workspaces names them, online by the runners list's own rule (isRunnerOnline), eligible as workspace.eligible reads it now. The panel asks to choose while it is null or not eligible.
list.choices: Every eligible workspace of the space, as { id, name, runner, online }, in the order space.workspaces lists them.
list.fab: { needsYou, working, updated } over every chat of the space not in Trash, counted as fab.counts says: a client draws the button from these three alone, so the button never depends on which chats a page happens to list.
list.chats: The space's chats not in Trash, newest first, at most rules.chatsListed: { sessionId, title, status, open, createdAt, updatedAt, drafts, needsYou } — open as fab.counts reads it, drafts how many cards it holds, needsYou how many of fab.needsYou are its. The button opens the chat holding the first card that needs the owner, else the newest open chat, else a new one (design section 3).

chat.turns: A chat's later messages go through the session's own message door, POST /api/sessions/:id/turns, as the owner's — an explicit routing intent under a UUID clientTurnId — with one optional field more for a chat, wikiContext (notes.wikiContext); a message to any other session that carries one is refused 400. Its content is the owner's words alone, whatever rides along (design section 4.2), so every turn of the owner's in a chat is first-hand.

notes.how: Each block below is appended at delivery, after the owner's words, as every control-plane note is (src/apiserver/src/runner-api/control-plane-note.ts, recorded beside the echo as controlPlaneNote): conversation_turn.content stays the owner's words alone, and a client draws each block as an Orbit attachment whose line is wikiChatNoteLabel of its opening tag's attributes (board 42 ②: Orbit attached: Wiki selection · 3.1 §3 · 1 sentence · 2 sources), its body folded open on a press. A client that does not know a tag names it as any unknown block — generically, as context — so the Android client and every older one draw them and count nothing from them (design section 9).

chat.when: the chat's first message, and no other
chat.text:
<orbit_wiki_chat>
You are chatting beside a page of this repository's Orbit wiki. The page the owner is reading, and any sentences they select, arrive as Orbit attachments.
The wiki's documents are written by the server from the code and from records. Never edit a document's text, and never cite a document or a sentence of one as a source.
Before you change anything, decide where the request belongs: knowledge goes into an entry (wiki_propose); a section behind main is rewritten from main, and a change to how a document is organized or written goes into the plan (both wiki_draft); a change to the system itself is a change to the code, or to the design document it cites.
Everything you propose or draft in this chat is a draft: nothing changes until the owner applies it. Say what each draft would change, never call one applied, and pass replaces with a draft's id when you revise it.
</orbit_wiki_chat>
chat.label: copy.notes.chat

page.when: a message whose wikiContext names its page
page.attributes: of (doc, entry or plan); for a document, doc (its number), slug, section (the section's number), key and repoSha (the section's); for an entry, entry (its public id) and title; for the plan, doc and slug
page.body: For a document's section, its title and its sentences as the document read serves them now, each with its footnotes (as selection's); for an entry, the entry as wiki_get answers it; for the plan, the document's definition as the plan read serves it — the page brings the plan, since a session reads none (plan.who).

selection.when: a message whose wikiContext carries a selection
selection.attributes: doc, slug, section, key, to (the last section's number, when the sentences run past the first), sentences and sources (how many of each the body holds), and repoSha (the first section's)
selection.body: Each selected sentence as the document shows it when the turn is delivered, in reading order under its section's title, with its footnotes: a repository original as path@sha#Lstart-end, a record as <kind> <record id> in session <session id>, and the entry it came through as via entry <id>. The server reads them at delivery, from the ids — the sentences, the footnotes as the document read serves them, redacted as that read redacts — never from text the client sends.
selection.label: copy.notes.selection

drafts.when: the owner's next message after one or more presses (presses.afterwards)
drafts.attributes: applied, edited, discarded and undone: how many cards each
drafts.body: One line per card pressed since the agent's last turn: its id, its label, what became of it (applied, edited, discarded or undone), for an applied one the entries it wrote with their trust, and how its rewrite stands then.
drafts.label: copy.notes.drafts

wikiContext.shape: { page?, selection? }: page one of { kind: doc, docSlug, sectionKey }, { kind: entry, entryId } or { kind: plan, docSlug }; selection { docSlug, sectionKey, sentenceIds } — sectionKey the section the selection starts in, sentenceIds from 1 to rules.selectionSentencesMax of the document's sentence ids, each once, which may run on into later sections of the same document. No other key.
wikiContext.shown: Each part is what the composer shows, and the owner may cross either out: what is not shown is not sent (design section 4.2). The page follows the reader and is frozen when the message is sent: a document page sends its document and the section nearest the scroll position, the entry drawer its entry, a plan page its document.
wikiContext.check: wikiChatContextErrors (src/shared/src/wikiChat.ts) names the path of each thing wrong, as validateWikiSources does; the door refuses a message whose wikiContext has any, WIKI_SCHEMA with those paths, before anything is filed. A sentence id the document does not hold at delivery is left out of the note and said so in it, never guessed.

drafts.what: A card is a row of its own, never a changeset (design section 7.1): it takes no place in pendingOpsPerSpace, leaves no proposed entry, is in no Review and no verification, and counts toward neither opsPerTurn nor opsPerSession, since it waits for no review; it holds at most limits.opsPerChangeset ops. It keeps its id, owner, space and chat session; its kind; the agent's rationale; for entry its ops as the request named them, each one checked, and similar[] beside an add or a supersede; for rewrite its sections and reason; for plan its change; its rewrites (rewrites); tainted, whether the chat had read the web when it was drafted; replaces, the card it replaced; the press (decision, decided_at, and the changeset it recorded); undone_at; and seen_at, the owner having opened its settled rewrite.

kinds.entry: Entry ops, from wiki_propose — add, amend, supersede, retire, reinforce and challenge — or the challenge of a wiki_note's corrects (agentSurface.chat). Label: copy.card.addKind with the new entry's kind, or the op's own (copy.card.amend …), or copy.card.changes for more than one op.
kinds.rewrite: A rewrite of sections from main (design section 6, second row: the section lags behind main), from wiki_draft: its sections are its rewrites. Its press only queues them (docs.follow): no entry is written. Label copy.card.rewrite; its Apply button is copy.actions.rewrite.
kinds.plan: A change to the plan, from wiki_draft (design section 6, third row), shaped as a plan proposal's change. Its press edits, confirms and rebuilds the plan through the plan's own doors in one go. It arrives with the plan card (design section 14, second step): until then wiki_draft refuses it (agentSurface.chat.draft.plan). Label copy.card.plan.

drafts.made: A card is made by the tool call that drafted it, in that call's transaction, and the call answers its id (toolResult). A request none of whose ops passed makes none. The card is drawn from that id, never from the conversation's text, and its state is read from the server (read), so every engine, the full session page and the phone draw the same card (design section 7.1).
drafts.replace: A card names the open card of the same chat it replaces (replaces, agentSurface.chat.replaces): that card reads Replaced from then on, whatever else holds, and only the newest of a chain can be pressed. A card that is not open, or another chat's, is no card to replace: the call is refused WIKI_SCHEMA at replaces, and nothing is made.

states.replaced: A newer card of the chat replaced it.
states.changed: An entry it changes moved off the revision it was drafted against (baseRevision), or left active, or a section it rewrites was written since it was drafted: Changed since this draft. Redo sends copy.card.redoMessage as the owner's next message, and the agent drafts again.
states.applied: Pressed Apply or Edit: Applied · Confirmed by you. Its rewrite stands under it (results).
states.not_applied: Its chat ended, or went to Trash, with it unpressed.

drafts.derivation: Read, never stored (design section 3: derived on read, as the landing session's liveness is): wikiChatDraftState (src/shared/src/wikiChat.ts) over the card's facts — its press, undone_at, whether a newer card replaced it, whether its chat is open (one of OPEN_SESSION_STATUSES, not in Trash) and whether its base moved — taking the first that holds of: applied or edited (undone once undone_at is set), discarded, replaced, not applied (its chat not open), changed, draft. A chat restored from Trash or resumed reads its unpressed cards as they read before it ended. tainted is a tag, not a state: copy.card.web with copy.card.webNote, on whatever state the card is in.
drafts.actions: What a card offers is wikiChatCardActions of its read (copy.actions): an open entry card Apply, Edit and Discard; a rewrite card Rewrite and Discard; a plan card Apply & rebuild, Open in Plan and Discard; a changed card Redo and Discard; an applied card Undo while it is undoable, Open entry for an entry card, and from its rewrite Settings (a waiting reason the owner fixes in Wiki settings), Try again (failed) or See changes (updated or read the same). Replaced, discarded, not applied and undone cards offer nothing.

results.rule: An applied card's rewrite is the newest docs_follow job that carried its press (docs.follow), read as: rewriting while the job is queued with nothing holding it up or runs; waiting, with docs.follow.waiting's reason, while something holds it up; and once the job has ended, each of the card's sections as docs.follow.outcomes says — updated (its sentences changed), same (it was written and reads the same), failed (it was left unwritten) or gone (the confirmed plan no longer has it) — and the card's as the first of failed, same, updated and gone that one of its sections is. A card with no rewrites has no rewrite; an applied card whose job has not run yet reads rewriting.
results.line: The line under the card is wikiChatResultLine (copy.result): Rewriting <sections>… — from main@<sha> once the job named its commit — Rewrite waiting · <reason>, Rewrite failed, or the sections as they came out, led by Wiki updated when one changed (board 42 ③: Wiki updated · 3.1 §3 — 1 sentence · 7.1 §2 — reads the same).
results.seen: seen is the owner having opened the card's settled rewrite (presses.seen): it settles a same or a failed rewrite for the waiting count (waiting) and the button's updated, and nothing else.
results.waits: A rewrite waits on the owner — the card adds one to the Wiki's waiting count (waiting) — while it is waiting, and while it read the same or failed and is not seen; it stops when the owner opens it, tries again (a new job), or undoes the card. Rewriting and updated never wait. Nothing is silent: each is on the card, and the ones that wait are counted (design section 11, Nothing blocks in silence).

drafts.rewrites: Worked out when the card is drafted and shown on it before it is pressed (design section 8.2), by wikiChatRewrites: the sections the chat's owner turns attached (page and selection notes), newest first; then the sections holding a sentence whose footnote came through an entry the card changes (its via_entry_id), in the plan's order; then, for a new entry, the sections it fits (docs.affected.fit) by their score, best first, ties in the plan's order — each section once, only written sections of the confirmed plan, at most rules.rewritesMax. A rewrite card's are the sections wiki_draft named. A card with none is applied without a rewrite. Before the press the page marks each with copy.card.wouldRewrite, and each opens beside the chat.
drafts.read: GET /api/wiki/chat-drafts/:id and GET /api/wiki/chats/:id/drafts (every card of a chat, oldest first) answer a card as { id, sessionId, kind, state, label, rationale, ops, sections, rewrites, similar, tainted, replaces, replacedBy, decision, decidedAt, undoneAt, undoable, changesetId, rewrite, createdAt }: state from derivation, ops as checked with each one's entry as it now stands, rewrites with each section's document number, section number and title, undoable as presses.undo decides it, and rewrite { jobId, result, reason, sha, sections: [{ doc, key, where, result, changed, versionId }], seen, settledAt } or null. The reads write nothing.
drafts.toolResult: What the drafting call answers (agentSurface.chat): { status: draft, draftId, … }. The transcript draws the card from draftId wherever the call is shown — the panel, the full session page, the phone — and a client that does not know the answer draws the call as any tool call (design section 9).

presses.oneCardOnePress: A card is pressed once, all its ops together (design section 7.2). A press on a card that is not open — replaced, discarded, not applied, undone, or applied already for apply, edit and discard — is a plain 409 naming its state, and writes nothing; the same press twice answers the first, marked replayed.
presses.apply: An entry card: in one transaction, the card's ops are checked again (sources, compare-and-set: an op whose base moved is refused WIKI_REVISION_CONFLICT, nothing is written, and the card reads changed), recorded as one changeset of origin agent whose session is the chat, and accepted by the owner in the same transaction (states.op pending to accepted), with the effect reviewModes.chat states: trust confirmed (trust.onApply.chatApplied), a principle's owner, no verification. Then, in the same transaction, the card's rewrites are queued as forced sections of a docs_follow job (docs.follow.triggers.press). A rewrite card: its sections queued, nothing else written. A plan card: the plan's edit, confirmation and build through their own doors (plan.routes), all or nothing — a gate it fails writes nothing and says so on the card (C12).
presses.edit: As Review's Edit (effectPolicy.decide.edit): the body { ops: [{ seq, changes }] } lays the owner's version over the card's ops, shaped as an amend's changes; the ops are recorded edited, each revision authored by the owner (trust.edited), and the rest is apply's. An entry card alone.
presses.discard: Marks the card discarded and writes nothing else: no rejection, no reason, no counter-example — nothing of it was ever an entry (design section 7.2).
presses.undo: Takes the card back, in one transaction: for an entry card, the changeset its Apply recorded is reverted through reviewModes.revert's own writes and idempotency key (revert:<changeset id>) — an add's entry retired, an entry an amend changed restored to the revision before the Apply with the trust it had then — though the owner accepted those ops; then each section the card's rewrite wrote is restored to the version that rewrite kept (docs.versions.restore), unless it was written again since, which is left as it is and named in the answer, as revert names an entry changed since. A rewrite that has not started loses the card's sections (a job left with nothing is cancelled); one that runs writes none of the card's sections it has not written yet, and the ones it wrote are restored. A card is undoable while it is applied and every op is an add or an amend — the two a revert can take back; a supersede and a retire end a lineage nothing brings back (states.entry), and a reinforce or a challenge is answered as any other, the challenge in Review — and a rewrite card is undoable while it is applied. The card reads Undone.
presses.retry: Try again: an applied card whose rewrite failed queues its sections again, forced, as its Apply did (docs.follow.triggers.press). Any other card is a plain 409.
presses.seen: The owner opened the card's settled rewrite — the panel showed it, scrolled to it from the button, or See changes opened it: seen_at is set, once, and the rewrite stops waiting if it read the same or failed (drafts.results.waits). It writes nothing else, and a card with no settled rewrite answers without writing.
presses.afterwards: Applied, edited, discarded and undone reach the agent with the owner's next message, as notes.drafts; no turn is opened for them (design section 7.2).
presses.floor: decide stays on the owner door alone, and no tool accepts or confirms (agentSurface.notTools): a press is the owner's, on the owner door, and a card is never a confirmation by itself (design section 11).

chat.trust: Apply and Edit write confirmed (trust.onApply.chatApplied): the press is the owner's acceptance, as Review's Accept is. A principle is the owner's own write: owner. The chat's own words are first-hand sources, which is why a card may cite them and say so on its Sources (copy.card.yourMessage) — and a share link with Footnotes on shows that quote to its visitors (share-links/public-wiki.ts), which the card's Sources say (design section 10).

fab.where: Every wiki page — but Settings and a share link — at the window's bottom right, an icon alone: 52 across and 24 from the edges on a desktop, 56 and 16 plus the safe area on a phone, in the brand's blue, fixed to the window. It hides while the panel or the sheet is open and comes back where it was. The page's foot keeps 88 clear for it, and it floats above the entry drawer The page header gets no Chat button, and its other buttons do not move (design section 3).
fab.counts: { needsYou, working, updated }, which list serves, counted by wikiChatFabCounts over the space's chats not in Trash: needsYou adds, for an open chat, the approvals and questions its session waits on the owner for (as the session list counts them), and for every chat each card that needs the owner — an open card (draft or changed) or a rewrite that waits (drafts.results.waits); working is an open chat with a turn queued or running, or a card whose rewrite is rewriting; updated counts the cards whose rewrite came out updated and is not seen.
fab.state: wikiChatFabState: needs you while needsYou is above 0 (copy.fab.needsYouOne or needsYouMany, an amber number), else working (copy.fab.working, a ring going round), else updated while updated is above 0 (copy.fab.updated, a green check, gone once opened), else idle (copy.fab.idle). Read on every list read, never stored (design section 3).

panel.header: The chat's title — pressed, the space's chat history (list) — then + (a new chat), ↗ (the full session page, where #-references, model switching and slash commands are) and ✕ (fold it away; the chat goes on). Under the title, one line always says where it runs: workspace · machine · engine · mode (board 42: orbit-develop · HPC · Claude Opus 5.5 · Default).
panel.address: The page's address carries ?chat=<session>: turning pages keeps the panel open, and a reload brings it back.
panel.composer: A short composer: text, the attachments (notes.wikiContext), send and Stop. Nothing else: the rest is the full session page's.
panel.belongs: A chat belongs to one space: another space's wiki shows that space's chats. It is in its workspace's session list too, its page headed copy.panel.fromWiki.

widths.atLeast1440: docked on the right, 400 wide by default, dragged between 320 and 560; the contents column as it is
widths.from1200: docked on the right; the contents column folds into the existing Contents drawer
widths.from640: slides in from the right over the right of the page, with no scrim; Contents drawer
widths.below640: a bottom sheet, half and full height; Contents drawer

panel.drawer: The entry drawer opens to the left of the panel. These widths are tuned against the real page when the panel is built (design section 4.1).
panel.clients: The web draws it (C8, C9); iOS draws a two-height sheet whose half height leaves the page scrollable (C11, design section 9); Android has none this phase.

waiting.means: What the chat adds to the Wiki's waiting count W (docs/wiki-design.md section 12.3.3: every thing that waits on the owner is in W, and every thing in W can be found): the space's applied cards whose rewrite waits (drafts.results.waits), one each — a rewrite held up, or one that read the same or failed and is not seen. It is space.list.chatWaiting, counted by wikiChatWaiting.
waiting.notCounted: An open card is not: drafts do not chase the owner (design section 11: no clock, drafts neither nag nor expire), and the button counts them. An approval is not: the session list counts it already, and W counts nothing twice.
waiting.banner: On Activity, one amber banner for the space's part, copy.waitingBanner (wikiChatWaitingBanner), opening the chat at the first such card; W's banners still add up to W.
waiting.android: Android has no chat this phase and reads no chatWaiting: its W stays pendingOps and planWaiting, every one of which it can open — counting a thing it cannot show would break W's one rule.

chat.dossier: A maintenance run's dossier of a chat leaves out its drafting calls — wiki_propose and wiki_draft, and a wiki_note that carries corrects — as it leaves out a call that reads the wiki (src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-dossier.ts): a card the owner discarded must not come back through the next run. The owner's turns stay in it, first-hand as ever (design section 7.1).
chat.realtime: wiki.changed (realtime) carries the space's id when a card is made, replaced or pressed, and when its rewrite's job is queued, held up, starts or ends: the panel, the button and Activity read again.
chat.boundaries: A share link's visitor has no button and sees no chat. A chat in Trash leaves the history; what was applied stands, and its unpressed cards read not applied. A quota or a slot shows as on any session (Waiting for slot). A possible duplicate is shown on the card before the press (similar[]), since semantic search is off (design section 10). A sent selection whose section was written again since — by maintenance or anything else — is drawn with copy.notes.outdated, its sentences kept as they were sent; a card drafted on it reads as drafts.derivation says (changed).

panel.emptyHint: Ask about this page, or say what should change.
panel.emptyNote: Nothing in the wiki changes until you apply it.
panel.placeholder: Ask about this page, or say what should change
panel.placeholderDraft: Reply, or say what to change in the draft
panel.noWorktree: Turn on worktrees for a workspace in this repository to chat here
panel.chooseWorkspace: Choose where this space's chats run
panel.offline: {machine} is offline. The chat waits for it to come back.
panel.mergeNote: Once this reaches main, Orbit rewrites what it touches.

card.redoMessage: This draft no longer applies: what it changes has changed since. Draft it again from what is there now.

waiting.runner_missing: The maintenance workspace has no runner
waiting.runner_offline: Waiting for the runner to come online
waiting.runner_upgrade: Upgrade the runner to read the repository

changes.leftOne: 1 section left for the next maintenance run
changes.leftMany: {n} sections left for the next maintenance run

reasons.build: after the build of plan version {version}

chat.vectors: src/shared/src/wiki-chat.fixture.json: the cards, the lines under them, the button, the waiting count, the follow job's waiting reasons, the pairs of jobs that may run at once, the rewrites, the sentence-level comparison, the attachment lines, wikiContext, and the Docs rows. wikiChatContract.spec.ts runs them through src/shared/src/wikiChat.ts; OrbitKit reads the same file for the client half (C11).

systemModel.why: The wiki's model calls are the server's (design section 0): the server's wiki-worker calls the deployment's own System model, whose address and key are in that service's environment and nowhere else, and every pipeline sends its calls through the persisted request queue (modelQueue). The worker probes the model and writes its state and heartbeat (health, read).

service.name: wiki-worker
service.context: NestFactory.createApplicationContext over WikiWorkerModule: Prisma and the worker's own providers, no controller and no port; enableShutdownHooks().
service.dependsOn: apiserver, service_healthy: the worker runs no migration, the apiserver applies them on boot.

envRules.configured: baseUrl, apiKey and model all set: an http or https URL, a key, a model name. With any of them missing or unusable the state is unconfigured and nothing is probed or called.
envRules.concurrency: Model requests in flight at once across every space, held by the request queue (modelQueue.concurrency). A value that is not a positive whole number is read as the default.
envRules.thinking: Optional, opt-in (owner 2026-11-01), for an endpoint that thinks unless it is told not to, as DeepSeek's V4 models at https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic do. One of thinkingValues puts thinking: {type: <the value>} into every call's body (request.body). Unset or empty sends no thinking field, so an endpoint that thinks only when asked (vLLM) gets the body it always got. Any other value is a problem, logged once, and no thinking field is sent. The worker's log line names the setting when it is set. It does not decide whether the System model is configured, the probe does not send it, and it is the worker's, not the call's: the request queue's request and request_sha256 do not hold it.
envRules.onlyOn: wiki-worker. The apiserver's environment holds none of the five (docker-compose.yml, test/compose-topology.test.mjs).
envRules.names: None is ANTHROPIC_*: Compose prefers the shell's environment to .env, and an agent session's environment carries those names (src/apiserver/src/wiki/wiki-compose-env.spec.ts).
envRules.problems: readWikiSystemModel(env) returns the configuration and the problems it found, and the worker logs them once. Neither the problems nor the log carry the key.

request.body: {model, max_tokens, system, messages: [one user message], stream: true}, then thinking: {type: disabled or enabled} only while env.thinking sets it (envRules.thinking). Every call gives its max_tokens explicitly and no tools are sent. With env.thinking unset or empty the body has no thinking field, byte for byte the body sent before the switch: thinking is then whatever the endpoint does unasked.
request.eventRules: The answer is the text of the text_delta deltas, in order. message_start carries the model and the first usage, message_delta the stop reason and the usage so far. A call has ended only at message_stop: a stream that closes before it is a dropped connection. ping, content_block_start, content_block_stop and any event not named here are read past.
request.usage: inputTokens and outputTokens are the last values the stream reported: message_delta's, else message_start's.
request.timeouts: Each call has a budget of its own, its step's limit (verify, extract, import and articles 15 minutes, docs 20, plan 60), and is disconnected after idleTimeoutSeconds without a byte whatever its budget. Both, and a cancel, abort it through one AbortController.
request.partial: The text received so far is handed to the caller after every delta, and carried by the error of a call that fails: what the request queue keeps as a request's partial (P1b).

errors.retryable: HTTP 5xx and 429; a connection refused, reset or closed, a name that does not resolve, a stream closed before message_stop, idleTimeoutSeconds without a byte; an SSE error event of type overloaded_error, api_error or rate_limit_error.
errors.unauthorized: HTTP 401, or an SSE error event of type authentication_error: the key was refused, and the state becomes auth_failed.
errors.other: Every other HTTP status and SSE error, an answer that is not an event stream, the call's own budget running out, and a cancel.

request.connections: Node's own fetch: connections are kept alive and reused, with no per-origin limit below the concurrency. After message_stop the stream is still read to its end, for a second at most, so that the connection goes back to the pool.

health.headers: authorization and anthropic-version, as a call sends them.
health.rule: An answer in upStatuses is up and one in authFailedStatuses auth_failed; any other status, no answer within timeoutSeconds, or no connection is down. Probed every intervalSeconds while configured, and each probe writes the state and the heartbeat together.

status.row: Exactly one, id 1, written by the worker alone with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE. The apiserver only reads it.

meaning.up: The probe answered one of health.upStatuses.
meaning.down: The probe got no answer, or another status. Requests are not taken while down (modelQueue.pause); the probe goes on, and the next up resumes them.
meaning.auth_failed: The endpoint refused the key (401), to the probe or to a call. It holds until the worker restarts, which is when a corrected key is read: every later call would be refused the same way.
meaning.unconfigured: env.baseUrl, env.apiKey or env.model is missing or unusable. Nothing is probed or called; the heartbeat is still written.

status.since: When the state began: kept while the state and the model stay what they were.
status.lastError: Why the state is not up, in words that name neither the address nor the key: an HTTP status, a connection error's code, a variable's name. Null while up.
status.checkedAt: When the probe last ran; null while unconfigured.
status.workerSeenAt: The worker's heartbeat, written with every probe, every health.intervalSeconds.

read.who: Any account the wiki is on for (JwtAuthGuard and WikiRolloutGuard; a personal access token needs wiki:read): it is the deployment's model, not a space's. It writes nothing.
read.workerNotRunning: No row, or a workerSeenAt older than status.workerStaleSeconds, reads as worker_not_running: what the settings page and the health line show as wiki worker not running. since is then the last heartbeat.
read.executor: jobs.executor.read (P9): { mode: server, serverExecutes: true }, since P11 the same for every account — what the wiki settings page reads to draw the System model. The other five fields are the deployment's and read the same for every account.
read.never: The System model's address, its key, and last_error: the read says the model's name and its state, and nothing else.

series.orbit_wiki_model_state: gauge, label state (one of read.states): 1 for the state the read answers, 0 for the others.
series.orbit_wiki_worker_heartbeat_age_seconds: gauge: seconds since workerSeenAt; absent while no worker has written.
