series.orbit_wiki_model_calls_total: counter, label outcome (succeeded, or one of request.errors): the queue's calls, read from its rows at scrape time (modelQueue.metrics).
series.orbit_wiki_model_call_duration_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long the queue's calls ran, over the rows that ended (modelQueue.metrics).

jobs.why: The wiki's pipelines run on the server (design section 0): they moved off the runner's maintenance sessions in P3 to P8, and the sessions' path was removed in P11 (2026-10-19). A unit of that work is a job: the server makes one, a wiki-worker claims it, and the model calls it makes go through the persisted request queue (modelQueue). The table, the claim, the lease and the retry are the contract, and what each kind runs is its pipeline's (kindRuns).

kindRuns.articles: The server's articles writer (P4, articles.serverExecution): the space's topic articles, written by the wiki worker with the System model. Its input is {}; it is made after a maintenance run of the space by the rule articles.regeneration states, at priority 0 (articles.job), and until it is first claimed it waits for its space's next round of maintenance, one round at most (priority). It reads the plan, takes up the topics whose fingerprint changed, groups a big topic (articles.serverExecution.steps), has the model name the groups and write the articles through the queue — step articles, a unit per topic, fingerprint and part — and writes them through WikiArticles.write. Its ref is the space's snapshot's sha, asked for once and parked on when there is none (repoOps.waiting). It succeeds when every topic it took up is written or unchanged, and fails as content, its report on the row, when one was left unwritten.
kindRuns.smoke: One model call, its answer and usage written into the job's report: the shortest route through the queue, and P1's end-to-end proof that claim, call, write-back and settle work together. It runs no pipeline and reads nothing; its input is { system?, prompt?, maxTokens? }, each with a default. A kind whose phase has not landed stays queued — the claim takes only the kinds the worker's build runs — so no deployment is handed work it would have to fail.
kindRuns.import: orbit wiki import's reading, on the server (P5, import.server): the notes the command registered, read by the System model through the queue — one request a note (step import, unit the note), one retry with what did not hold up (step import_retry) — checked as import.server.checks says, the anchors held to the space's snapshot, then a dry run and one proposal with origin import as the calling session, under a key made of the space and the ops. Its input is the create route's body with the session in it; its report is import.server.report, which the command prints and remembers. Made only by the runner door's create route, at import.server.priority.
kindRuns.verify: The server's verifier (P3, design section 8 and agentSurface.verify.serverExecution): the ops an Automatic space holds back, verified by the wiki worker with the System model. Its input is { sessionId } — the session whose waiting ops it verifies, which is the identity a verdict has to be reported under — and it runs the verifier (the runner's, ported before P11) step by step: read reviewModes.verification.list for that session (rules.verificationListMax at a time, the server's own evidence reader), build the one-op prompt with the entries numbered E1..En (agentSurface.verify.prompt), ask the System model through the queue — one request per op, step verify, unit the op's id, so a replayed job reuses the answers it holds — and report each verdict through WikiService.recordVerifications, the one writer, as soon as it is read. An answer that is not a verdict is reported as nothing and counted in the report ({ looked, verified, supported, partial, unsupported, duplicate, failed, failures[{opId, why, refused}], stopped, usage }); the job still succeeds, because the ops that got verdicts are its result, and those left without one keep waiting. A space that is no longer automatic ends the pass where it stands (verification.notAutomatic), and a call whose request ends in a way that is not the platform's (the queue's own classes) is that op's failure, not the pass's. The two passes a maintenance run makes and the adoption of ended sessions' ops (verification.adoption) are arguments of the same function, P8's to call.
kindRuns.plan_draft: A draft of the space's plan on the server (P6, plan.jobs.server): the four steps of plan.jobs.run — the catalogue, each category's details, each document's outline, the rules' draft — through the queue, gated on the space's snapshot and by the plan's gate, three rounds at most; stored as a version the wiki_job authored. Its input is { planJobId }; its report is { kind, planJobId, outcome, version, error, plan: plan.jobs.report }. Made by advanceWikiPlanJob for a draft the space's creation or its owner asked for, at plan.jobs.server.priority.
kindRuns.plan_revise: A revision of the space's plan on the server (P6, plan.jobs.server): plan.jobs.run.revise through the queue — the new catalogue with what each document is made from and the conventions it moves, then the documents that merge or are new — gated as plan_draft is. Its input and report are plan_draft's; the owner's instructions are the plan job's own. Made by advanceWikiPlanJob for the owner's redraft with instructions.
kindRuns.docs_build: The documents' build on the server (P7, docs.build.server): the documents of a confirmed plan version, written by the wiki-worker with the System model. Made by the owner's confirmation of the version (plan.jobs.server.build), at docs.build.server.priority; its input is { planJobId }. It reads the repository at a snapshot's commit through the space's runner, the records through the material read, writes each section through WikiDocs.write, says how far it got and how it ended on its plan job, and fails as content when a section was left unwritten.
kindRuns.maintain: A space's Wiki maintenance run on the server (P8, maintenance.job.server): run by the wiki-worker with the deployment's System model and the space's snapshot (a task's session ran it with orbit wiki maintain until P10). Its input is { runId } — the wiki_maintenance_run the trigger made beside it, which carries why the run was made, how far it must read and how the space stood; a backfill's also names its sessions (maintenance.job.server.backfill), and differs from what follows as that says — and the job executes exactly that run: the dossiers through WikiMaintenance.dossierPage, one request per dossier through the queue (step extract, unit the session's id, at most rules.extractConcurrency in flight), the checks and the one retry of wiki-maintain.ts, the dry run and then the batches of at most limits.opsPerChangeset ops with the run's own breaker (wiki-maintain-job.ts), the cursor advance through WikiMaintenance.advanceRecorded, its own ops verified twice and then up to rules.adoptOpsMax adopted (P3's verifyWikiOps with a maintenance-job principal), the anchors read in pages of anchorRules.verify.rules.listEntriesMax entries, an entry every anchor of which still holds at the snapshot's commit left out (anchorRules.verify.skip, after at most maintenance.job.server.rules.anchorDiffsMax diffs, one at a time), the entries left to check sent together whichever page they were read on, at most that many entries a wiki_repo_op — the most one operation may carry — and each written back in reports of at most anchorRules.verify.rules.reportEntriesMax entries — and the documents' step (maintenance.job.docs) with P7's writer and P6's plan gate — its comparison (maintenance.job.docs.byRepo) one diff a repoSha the snapshot reaches and none at the head, and then the files it compares read by commit: what the touched sections of one commit name in one read at that commit and all of it in one read at the head, the read cache first and more than one operation only where repoOps.read.operationBytes packs them so, each operation asked once the one before it has settled; a diff's names keyed as the runner's comparison keyed them (wikiGitChanges), by the path at the section's commit — a rename under its old path, the one withdrawn ({ path: the old path, change: renamed, to: the new path }), and its new path as added, either end touching a section that names it — and the files at that commit the head's less what the range added or renamed into place, plus what it deleted or renamed away, so a cited file deleted since is read there, as the runner read the commit itself, and its going is a change. It reports maintenance.job.report plus the token spend, and its end queues the articles a successful run owes (articles.regeneration); the round after it is claimed before that articles job, which yields it that one round (priority). A failure of the platform is thrown as infra and the job is tried again without counting against the space; a failure of the work ends the run (outcome failed, the space's streak one higher) and the job fails as content (§5.5).
kindRuns.docs_follow: The follow job (the wiki chat, C4, docs.follow): the sections a chat's press or a change that reached main touched, written again by the wiki-worker with the System model at once — not when maintenance is next due, and not skipped while the space catches up. Made by the press in its own transaction, or after a merge receipt into main commits (docs.follow.triggers), at the highest priority it carries (docs.follow.priorities); its input is { facts }, every fact that joined it while it was queued. It reads the repository at a snapshot's commit through the runner of the space's maintenance workspace, takes up a press's sections whatever their fingerprint and a merge's where a file it changed is cited and the section's own material changed (docs.follow.sections), within the day's budget (docs.follow.daily), writes each through WikiDocs.write with the reason of the fact that asked for it (docs.versions), reports { sections, left, usage } (docs.follow.report), and fails as content when a section was left unwritten.

jobs.waitingRule: Nothing writes `waiting` yet: this phase's worker keeps a job running while its model request waits, and the request's wait limit is what ends it. The transitions that park a job — on a repo operation (P2), or on the model being away — arrive with the phases that need them, and a waiting row holds no lease (the CHECK above).

lease.claim: One statement per claim: WITH the due jobs (state = 'queued' AND (next_attempt_at IS NULL OR next_attempt_at <= now()) AND attempts < retry.maxAttempts AND kind = ANY(the kinds this build runs) AND owner_id is one of the claim's owners — every account, for the worker), each with whether it waits for its space's round (priority), then WITH due AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT … WHERE the job is its space's next — the first by priority DESC, created_at, id of the space's due jobs that wait for no round — AND NOT EXISTS a running job of the same space … ORDER BY the space's place — its first due job's priority DESC, created_at, id, whichever of its jobs takes it — LIMIT n FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), UPDATE wiki_job … FROM due — each claimed row gets a new lease_generation, and started_at is the first claim's. The candidates are read once, so n is a bound whatever the plan: as a subquery of the UPDATE's FROM they could be read once per row of the table, each read locking past the rows the statement had already written. A space whose due jobs all wait for its round, the round backing off, takes nothing until the round is due again.
lease.hosts: lease_owner, lease_generation and lease_deadline_at are set together exactly while the row is running (`wiki_job_lease_chk` holds it both ways), and every settle clears them.
lease.cas: Every write that ends an attempt — succeeded, requeued, failed, handed back — is a compare-and-set on the claim's generation. A worker whose lease ran out and was taken over matches no row and settles nothing.
lease.sweep: A running job whose lease_deadline_at passed goes back to queued, attempts one higher and the next attempt on retry.backoffSeconds, failure_kind infra and the error `LEASE_EXPIRED: the worker holding this job stopped before settling it`; the takeover starts the job from the beginning, and the request rows it already made answer the replay (modelQueue.identity). These are the leases nobody handed back — the worker crashed, was killed, or exited before its hand-back was written — and their rule is unchanged: a stopped worker's jobs never reach the sweep (handBack).
lease.handBack: The owner's decision of 2026-10-09: a deploy does not count against a job's attempts (design section 5.4). A worker that is stopped (SIGTERM, modelQueue.shutdown) hands each job it runs back in one write, a compare-and-set on the claim's generation: state queued, the lease columns and next_attempt_at cleared, attempts as they were, failure_kind cleared, and the error `WORKER_STOPPED: the worker was stopped and handed this job back; the next one takes it over at once, without counting an attempt`. The next claim — the next process's first pass, or another worker's — takes it at once in its space's order (lease.claim, priority) — an articles job handed back has been claimed, so it waits for no round — never after a backoff; before this, the sweep counted a stop as a lost attempt and backed the job off, and on 2026-10-09 docs_build 79620f23 lost three of its ten attempts to three deploys and, backing off 30 s at 06:56Z, was overtaken by its space's priority 0 articles job. A job parked on a repository operation whose wait the stop cuts short is handed back the same way (repoOps.waiting). Its requests are let go as modelQueue.shutdown says and met again by the replay; its writes are made under their idempotency keys, so the replay writes nothing twice. It is no failure: it writes no run row and no cursor, so the space's consecutive failures are not touched; Activity draws the job queued with its place in line, never `retrying in` (nextAttemptAt is null) and no error (read), and orbit wiki import prints it as the job's last try (import.server.cli), its attempts as they were. What it finished that its replay will not do again is on its row already (carry), and the report the replay ends with counts it.

jobs.onePerSpace: At most one job per space runs at a time (design section 5.1, as the hidden list's maxConcurrent 1 was), with one exception, the owner's decision of 2026-11-06 (docs/wiki-chat-design.md section 8.5): a docs_follow job (docs.follow) runs beside a job of its space that writes no document — articles, verify, import or smoke — and waits only for the ones that do: maintain, docs_build, plan_draft, plan_revise and another docs_follow. So two jobs of a space run at once only when one is docs_follow and the other writes no document (wikiJobsMayOverlap in src/shared/src/wikiChat.ts); every other pair waits as before, articles and verify included. The claim takes a space's next due job in its own order (priority) that no running job of the space excludes, and the database holds the same rule for two schedulers that read at once with two partial unique indexes over space_id in place of wiki_job_space_running_key: one WHERE state = 'running' AND kind <> 'docs_follow' (of everything but the follow job, at most one runs), and one WHERE state = 'running' AND kind IN ('maintain', 'docs_build', 'plan_draft', 'plan_revise', 'docs_follow') (at most one job that writes documents). A follow job beside a verify cannot deadlock with it: a verdict withdraws sentences and marks sections stale in its entry's own transaction, entries first and documents after, the order a document write takes them (docs.withdrawal), so no cycle forms — src/apiserver/src/wiki-worker/wiki-docs-follow-job.pg.spec.ts proves it. Migration 0477 (C4) made docs_follow a kind and the two indexes, wiki_job_space_running_other_key and wiki_job_space_running_writer_key, in place of 0401's one. What it leaves: a press while maintenance writes the documents still waits for it, and Rewrite waiting says so (docs.follow.waiting); how long is design section 14's second measurement. A job that is waiting (waiting_for set) holds no lease and does not occupy the space.
jobs.priority: Integer, default 0. Owner-initiated work — a plan draft, a review, a build, an import from the command line — is made with a higher priority than background maintenance, and the claim takes the highest first; within one priority, the longest-waiting job first. A verify job is made with 1: the session that proposed the op is waiting for it, and the space knows nothing of what was proposed until the verdict arrives; the pass a maintenance run makes over what ended sessions left waiting (verification.adoption, P8) is background work at 0. Maintenance goes first, and an articles job yields one round at most (the owner's decision of 2026-10-10): an articles job that has never been claimed waits for its space's round — the first maintain job of the space made after it, of no lower a priority — until that round has ended, every attempt and backoff of it included, so the round is claimed first although it was made later. Once the round has ended, a maintain job made after it finds the articles job ahead in first-come order: the articles job yields that one round alone and is never starved. On the canary every round's end queued an articles job that ran for an hour and a half or more (1d4b9a86: 673 calls and 1.56 million input tokens, nearly every topic's fingerprint changed by the round's twenty-odd sessions), and the next round, queued moments later, waited behind it (61e91611: an hour and 47 minutes). The round is usually not made yet when the articles job is: a run's end queues the articles job, and the trigger made the next round only at the owner's next event about the space — 15 s later in that case, 99 s after 61e91611 (articles 3f3a8f90 claimed at 07:19:42, its round 96cd83f0 made at 07:21:20), 8.6 to 99.2 s after every canary run that queued one, while the worker's pass comes every 5 s. The trigger has no clock of its own, only events, so no fixed wait could be sure to cover that gap: instead the end of a server run that queued its space's articles job asks the trigger for the next round at once (maintenance.job.server.trigger), and a space still due has the round made then, right behind the articles job and before the run lets the space go — the claim takes it first, deterministically. A space no longer due makes no round, and its articles job runs at the next pass, not a moment later. A job claimed before — handed back (lease.handBack), put back for infra, parked on a repository operation — has had its turn and waits for no round, and a running job is never touched: only which queued job a claim takes changes. No priority changes for it: a job's calls carry its priority into the model queue (modelQueue.priority), where a lower one would rank the articles behind every other space's calls, and wiki_job_counts_chk holds every priority at 0 or above. Across spaces nothing moves: a space keeps the place in the line its first job by priority and first come gives it, whichever of its jobs takes that place (lease.claim, read.jobRules.ahead). The owner's work at 1 still goes before both.

retry.rule: An infra failure puts the job back to queued with attempts one higher and next_attempt_at now plus backoffSeconds[attempts], the same schedule the queue's calls use. A content failure ends it: state failed, failure_kind content, ended_at set. attempts counts the infra retries of the job's own row. A stop is neither: the job is handed back with attempts as they were and no backoff (lease.handBack), so a deploy never brings a job nearer its limit; a worker that crashed is the sweep's, counted and backed off as an infra failure (lease.sweep).
retry.limit: No job is put back for ever (2026-10-09: a docs_build job whose writer failed an assertion was put back every time its space was free). When the attempt that makes maxAttempts fails as infra, the job is ended instead of requeued: state failed, failure_kind infra, ended_at set, attempts counting that attempt, and on its row the error `Ended after <n> attempts: <the last attempt's error>` (2,000 characters at most), which Activity's Runs card shows (read). An error the build did not expect, which is neither the platform's nor the work's (a failed assertion, a TypeError), is retried as infra in case it was passing, but ends the job the same way at the attempt that makes unexpectedMaxAttempts, its error saying it was unexpected. The executor ends the attempt it settles. An attempt the lease sweep or a repository wait counted at the limit is never claimed (lease.claim), and the worker's next pass ends the job. A job ended this way settles what waits on it in the same transaction (settleWikiJobRows in wiki-worker/wiki-jobs.ts): its calls and repository operations still queued or running are cancelled, a maintain job's run ends failed / infra with the error (the space's streak is not touched, and the next run reads again what this one did not take in), and the plan job of a plan_draft, plan_revise or docs_build job ends failed with the error, still naming its wiki_job: the plan page reads the draft or build as failed, and the owner's next request makes a new one.

jobs.startup: A worker runs one pass the moment it starts — sweep, then claim — so a job left queued, handed back by a stopped worker (lease.handBack) or held by a dead one (lease.sweep) is picked up where it stands.
jobs.make: The pipelines enqueue a job as a row (kind, input, priority, state queued), for every account (P11, 2026-10-19). Each pipeline has its own route or trigger: since P3 a submission that recorded an op an Automatic space holds back (reviewModes.verification.waits) makes a verify job for the session that proposed it, after its own transaction commits, at the waiting priority (priority above) — and so does the owner reopening ops a verdict should not have decided (verification.reopen), whose sessions are usually long gone — with one queued job per session and space, since a job reads the ops that wait when it runs (a later submission rides it, while an op arriving mid-run gets a job of its own); since P5 the runner door's import-jobs route makes an `import` job (import.server.create); since P4 an articles job is made where the server records the end of a maintenance run, by the rule articles.regeneration states (articles.serverExecution.made); since P6 a plan job is made as a `plan_draft` or `plan_revise` job (plan.jobs.server.make); since P7 the owner's confirmation of a plan version makes a docs_build job (docs.build.server.made); since P8 the maintenance trigger makes a maintain job with its run (maintenance.job.server); since the wiki chat (C4) a chat's press, and a merge receipt into main once it commits, make or join the space's docs_follow job (docs.follow.triggers, docs.follow.queue); and smoke is made by the specs directly.
jobs.progress: A job's progress column is its own pipeline's to write (a step, a count, what it is doing), under its lease generation; report is what it ends with — the whole job's, whatever attempts it took — and until then holds only what its attempts carry to a replay (carry). The smoke job writes a report; the import job writes both (import.server.progress, import.server.report); the articles job writes its report (articles.serverExecution.ends), and so does the verify job (jobs.kindRuns.verify); the plan jobs write both (plan.jobs.server.progress, plan.jobs.server.finish), and so does the docs_build job (docs.build.server.progress, docs.build.server.end), and the docs_follow job (its step, and the sections done of those it took up with the commit it writes from; docs.follow.report).

carry.phase: server execution, the whole job's report — 2026-10-10, the canary's articles 3f3a8f90 and f917aef5 (P10)
carry.where: wiki_job.report, as { carry }, while the job has not ended: no read shows a job's report before its end — Activity's jobs read reads no report at all (read.never), and the import's read (import.server.cli) returns one only for an import job, which carries nothing — and the end writes the report over it. No column or migration of its own: the job row already holds an object column that nothing reads until the end.
carry.why: A job is replayed from its plan whenever an attempt ends short of its end — a stop handed it back (lease.handBack), the platform failed it (retry), its worker died (lease.sweep), it parked on a repository operation (repoOps.waiting) — and the plan no longer names what an earlier attempt finished: a topic written is no longer changed, a section written is unchanged by its fingerprint, an op given its verdict waits no longer, a page of dossiers is behind the cursor. The report counted the replay alone: on the production canary (P10, 2026-10-10) articles 3f3a8f90 reported 15 topics and 250 articles where its request rows say 20 and 370, and f917aef5 11 and 217 where they say 15 and 300; every deploy hands the running jobs back.
carry.rule: A job's report is the whole job's, whatever attempts it took: what an earlier attempt finished that its replay does not do again is counted as that attempt finished it, each item once, and the calls and usage are every request the job made, each once. What did not get done — a topic or a section that failed, an op left without a verdict, what waits for the next run — is the last attempt's: only finished work is carried, so a job ends as it would have and writes what it would have, and only its report changes.
carry.write: The running attempt writes it as it finishes each item a replay would not do again — a compare-and-set on the claim's generation, as progress is, without any U+0000 (serverWrites). The writes of one attempt go one at a time, each with the carry as it stands when it runs (wikiJobCarryWriter), and the pipeline goes on only once its write is in, so a stop leaves nothing finished and not carried. The next attempt reads it as it starts and folds it into the report it ends with. The job's end writes the report over it — succeeded, or failed as content — and an end at retry.limit clears it, as a job had no report before its end.

kinds.articles: The topics an attempt seeded (articles.seeding), every topic it wrote or found written with its parts and their stats as they were, and the ref it wrote them at. The report has every topic once, in the plan's order — a topic the replay took up again is the replay's — and the carried ref when the replay wrote no topic. A topic left unwritten is not carried: it is still changed, and the replay takes it up again.
kinds.verify: Each verdict the server recorded, counted by what it said: its op is no longer in the list the replay reads. looked, verified and each verdict's count add the carried ones; an op left without a verdict is not carried, and the replay asks about it again.
kinds.docs_build: Each section written, its run as it was, and each document's last write's answer. A section the replay finds unchanged by the fingerprint an earlier attempt wrote it with is counted written, once; the plan job's build report (plan.jobs.buildReport) is the whole build's too.
kinds.maintain: Once the cursor's advance is written, the pipeline up to it — the sessions and dossiers read, the entries taken, the ops recorded and refused, whether the cursor moved: the replay reads from the cursor it moved, and reads none of them again. Each verdict as it is recorded, the run's own and the adopted. The documents step's sections written, the sections it took up and why, the paths and sentences it withdrew, the plan proposal it stored, and the time it spent. The anchors are not carried: an entry an earlier attempt checked stands checked at this commit and a replay leaves it alone, and the report reads it back off the entry — a check made since the run first started is the run's (maintenance.job.server.anchors).
kinds.import: Nothing: its input is fixed, a replay reads every note again through the requests it already made, and proposes the same ops under the same key (import.server), so its report is the whole job's already.
kinds.plan_draft: Nothing: its materials are kept on its plan job at its first run (plan.jobs.server.materials), so a replay asks the same questions through the requests it already made and goes through every round again; its tokens are already every request of the job, and its seconds run from the plan job's start.
kinds.docs_follow: Each section written, as its report says it (docs.follow.report): a replay does not mark a press's section stale again and so does not write it twice, finds a merge's written at the head and leaves it, and the report counts each section once — the attempt that wrote it is its outcome.

carry.calls: The calls and usage a report gives are read off the job's own wiki_model_request rows, each once (wikiJobModelCalls): a replay meets the rows its earlier attempts made rather than making new ones, so a call it reuses is not counted again, and a call an attempt made that the replay never asked again is still counted. articles counts the requests that answered; docs_build and maintain also count the ones that ended in a failure of their own (a refusal, a budget), never one failed on its step's wait limit, which was the platform's and is asked again under the next attempt. maintain's tokens are every call of the run once (maintenance.job.run.tokens), its docs.tokens the documents' steps' and the plan proposal's; before this, the documents' calls were counted twice in the run's tokens, and the second verification pass counted its looked ops as calls though its requests — the first pass's units, asked with another prompt — were refused as already existing and never reached the model. Since it asks under units of its own (maintenance.job.server.verify), its requests are calls like any other.
carry.seconds: docs_build's seconds run from the job's first claim to its end, and maintain's from the run's first start, as a plan job's run from its plan job's start; maintain's docs.seconds is the time each attempt spent in the documents step, added up.
carry.articlesAfterRun: finishWikiMaintenanceJob asks whether the run recorded an op (articles.regeneration) of the whole run's report: a run whose ops were recorded before a stop, and whose replay recorded none, still owes its space the articles job a run nothing stopped owes.
carry.specs: wiki-articles-job, wiki-verify-job and wiki-docs-build-job pg specs one case each, and wiki-maintain-job four (stopped in the documents step, between the run's own verdicts, on the call of an op whose neighbours the run's verdicts then made live, and between two anchors operations): the worker is stopped mid-job and hands the job back, the next one finishes it, and the report is what the same job reports on a space of the same shape when nothing stops it — every verdict of the run's own once, the replay verifying the ops the stop left waiting (maintenance.job.server.verify); the op whose question changed while the job was handed back costs one call more, which the report counts.

executor.removed: P11 (2026-10-19; the owner's decision on card 34iAuONJEvJY2LIpuSMu4): the server executes every account's wiki, and there is no switch. ORBIT_WIKI_EXECUTOR and ORBIT_WIKI_EXECUTOR_CANARY_OWNERS are read by nothing — compose passes neither, and a deployment's .env that still sets them changes nothing — and the sweep that cancelled, at apiserver start, the jobs of an account the switch no longer served went with them. From P1b to P10 the switch chose who ran an account's wiki: runner (the default) its maintenance sessions, canary the accounts its list named, server every account.
executor.noWayBack: There is no path to go back to: the runner's maintenance sessions and its pipelines are gone (P11). To pause the wiki's model work, stop the wiki-worker container — its jobs and calls wait in the queue and nothing is lost, and the clients say the worker is not running once its heartbeat is older than systemModel.status.workerStaleSeconds — or turn the wiki off (ORBIT_WIKI=off, agentSurface.rollout).

read.rule: What a read tells the account that asks: { mode: server, serverExecutes: true }, the same for every account since P11 (the shared constant in src/shared/src/wikiJobs.ts). mode is one of modes: runner and canary are what a control plane from before P11 could say, and serverExecutes was false there for an account its switch left on the runner.
read.readBy: systemModel.read (executor) and maintenance.health (executor): the clients draw the server's settings, the Runs card and the status line's server reasons while serverExecutes holds — always, from a server since P11 — and none of them while a read does not say so (still loading, or a control plane that says otherwise or predates the field). Nothing of the runner's is drawn instead (2026-10-19): no provider to pick or show, no runner's sentence, no plan job's provider or the task it waited for.

runRows.why: Health and the day's count read runs, not the history of how they were made (design section 5.1).
runRows.doctor: wiki_maintenance_run.job_id and wiki_plan_job.job_id record the job that ran a run; task_id is nullable from 0401 on, and a CHECK requires exactly one maker per started row (a plan job is exempt while it is queued or held — it has made neither yet).
runRows.count: The day's runs (space.settings.maintenance.dailyRunLimit) count the run rows the space's maintain jobs made since midnight UTC, however they ended, less a run of active catch-up that ran on a local endpoint, failed or was cut short (wikiMaintenanceRunsToday). A run a maintenance task made, before the server made every run, has no job and is not counted. Plan jobs never count.

jobs.serverWrites: What a job writes out of a model's answer is handed to the shared writer without any U+0000 — a document's sections, footnotes and dispositions (WikiDocs.write), an article (WikiArticles.write), a changeset's ops (submitChangeset, maintenance and import), a verification (recordVerifications), a plan draft or proposal and the plan job's finish (its last draft and errors), and a maintenance run's report and error — as the runner gate drops U+0000 from what a runner reports (src/apiserver/src/runner-api/strip-nul.ts). The job's own progress, report and error, and a call's error, are written the same way. The answer itself is kept as the model sent it (modelQueue.answerEncoding) and parsed as such, so a raw NUL inside a JSON string fails the parse as Go's decoder does, and a NUL the model wrote as \u0000 is dropped at the hand-off rather than failing the write with 22P05.
jobs.runnerTurns: A run creates no task and no session: it does not touch runnerActiveTurns, and the runner's only part in it is the repository operations (repoOps).

read.who: The space's owner on the user door (JwtAuthGuard and WikiRolloutGuard; a personal access token needs wiki:read): another account's space is the plain 404. It writes nothing.
read.why: A server run has no task and no session to open (design section 2.2): what it is doing — its step, its calls, where they wait — is on Activity, and this read is what the Runs card and a run's page draw.
read.answer: { spaceId, jobs }: the space's newest limits.jobs rows of wiki_job, newest first by created_at.

jobRules.ahead: While the job is queued: how many queued jobs of the deployment the claim takes before it, in lease.claim's order: a space's jobs hold the places priority DESC, created_at, id give them, and the space's own order says which takes which — an articles job waiting for its round (priority) holds the place after the round's, and the round its; null in every other state.
jobRules.progress: The pipeline's own progress (jobs.progress) as { step, done, total }: done and total as the pipeline wrote them, or for the import's shape (import.server.progress) the notes read or failed against the notes it was handed; null when the pipeline wrote none.
jobRules.calls: Its calls counted by state — total, queued, running, succeeded, failed, cancelled — and the input and output tokens they reported, over every one of its rows.
jobRules.nextCall: Of its queued calls, the one the queue reaches first: { ahead, enqueuedAt }, ahead counted as request.ahead is; null while none waits.
jobRules.requests: Its newest limits.callsPerJob calls by enqueued_at, given oldest first; calls.total counts the ones left out.

requestRules.ahead: While the call is queued: how many queued requests of the deployment the queue takes before it (priority DESC, enqueued_at, id — modelQueue.concurrency.claim's order), whoever they are for; null in every other state.
requestRules.times: How long a call waited is from enqueuedAt to startedAt (or to now while it is queued), and how long it ran from startedAt to endedAt (or to now while it runs); startedAt is its first claim's, so a retry's time is the call's own.

read.never: A call's request (system prompt, prompt, max_tokens), its request_sha256, answer and partial, and the material it was made from (modelQueue.material); the lease columns of either table; the job's input and report; whose the runs and calls ahead in a queue are; and the System model's address or key, which no row of either table holds (systemModel.request.errors: the queue's words name neither).

modelQueue.why: All of the wiki's model calls go through one persisted queue, so that a deployment's System model answers at most ORBIT_WIKI_MODEL_CONCURRENCY requests at once whatever the pipelines were doing when a worker died (design section 0). The row is also the breakpoint: a pipeline replayed after a restart reuses the answer a finished call holds instead of issuing it again.
modelQueue.identity: (job_id, step, unit, attempt) is unique, and the pair (step, unit) is the call's own address inside its job: enqueuing it again MEETS the row it already has rather than making a second call. `attempt` is which attempt of that unit the row is (a genuine redo moves to the next), and `attempts` is how many times this row has been tried — a lease that ran out and a retry each count one, and the backoff reads it.
modelQueue.request: { system, prompt, maxTokens } — the call exactly as the client sends it, and its sha256, so the same unit twice with a different call can be told from the same call replayed.

material.rule: A nullable jsonb object beside the call: what the call was made from, written with the row by a caller that keeps one and never changed after (a row the enqueue meets keeps its own; wikiModelRequestsAsked reads it back with the call, from the row the next ask of the unit would meet). The maintain job keeps the case file of each session's first question — under step extract the dossier as it was handed out, its notes aside; under step claims the notes and their file — so that a replay asks what its earlier attempt asked and reads the answer against what it was asked from (maintenance.job.server.replay). Every other call keeps null. A material jsonb cannot hold (repoOps.storedText) is not kept. No read shows it (jobs.read.never).
material.why: The row is the breakpoint, but the question a pipeline makes is built from what it read, and a replay reads again: on 2026-11-06 two maintain runs of the orbit space lost their lease while the production host's CPU was saturated, and each replay built a session's case file again from records the earlier attempt had not read, asked the same unit another question, and failed.

modelQueue.answerEncoding: A model may copy into its answer the NUL of a code piece it was shown. An answer, and the partial a running call writes back, with a U+0000 in it is kept as its UTF-8 bytes in base64, `answer_encoding` / `partial_encoding` saying so (migration 0412, repoOps.storedText); every read decodes it, so a pipeline parses exactly the text the model sent. Before this a raw NUL failed the answer's write with 22021, and the call stayed running until its lease ran out, to be asked again.
modelQueue.requestEncoding: When the call's system or prompt has a U+0000 — a prompt carries the repository's text, and a source file can have one (repoOps.storedText) — `request` keeps both as their UTF-8 bytes in base64, with `encoding: "base64"` beside them; the claim decodes them, so the call the System model is sent is the one the pipeline made. `request_sha256` is the call's, not the column's.

concurrency.meaning: Requests in flight at once across every space and every worker of the deployment.
concurrency.claim: One transaction per scheduler: pg_advisory_xact_lock (one key for the whole queue), count the rows whose state is running and whose lease has not expired, then claim at most (concurrency − that count) — ORDER BY priority DESC, enqueued_at, id LIMIT that many FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, read once in a MATERIALIZED WITH as the job claim's are, each row under a new lease generation. However many workers run, running-plus-unexpired never passes the concurrency, and two schedulers claiming at once serialize on the lock rather than on rows.

modelQueue.priority: Integer, default 0, copied from the job. Owner-initiated work sorts above background maintenance, and within one priority the longest-waiting request goes first; perJob caps what one job can hold in flight, so no single job takes the queue.

lease.rule: A running row holds lease_owner, lease_generation and lease_deadline_at together (`wiki_model_request_lease_chk`), renewed while the call runs. The text received so far is written back with a renewal only when it grew, so a row that dies mid-call keeps what had arrived.
lease.sweep: A running row whose lease passed goes back to queued with attempts one higher and its partial KEPT; the next claim re-issues the call and hands the client the text it had. Every settle is a compare-and-set on the claim's generation, so a takeover's generation is not the dead worker's and its late write settles nothing.
lease.answer: A succeeded row's answer is written once, by the claim that owned it: an answer that arrives after the lease was taken over is dropped, and the takeover issues the call again.

retry.rule: 5xx, 429 and connection failures class retryable: the row goes back to queued, attempts one higher, not_before now plus backoffSeconds[attempts − 1] (0, then 10 s, then 30 s and every one after it). Nothing else is retried: the call's own budget running out, an answer that is not an event stream and an unclassified error end the request (state failed, error_kind other) and the job reads it.
retry.unauthorized: A 401 (and an authentication_error event) is its own case: the request goes back to the queue — it is the deployment's key to fix, not the work's to lose — and the worker reports the refusal to the model's state, which turns auth_failed and stops the queue (pause).

waitLimit.rule: How long a request may wait from its enqueue before it fails, by its step (the step's own name or one of its stages: extract*, docs*, import*, plan*). A request that waits past it ends failed with error_kind other and the wait limit's words; the job that made it reads that and fails as infra, so a model that is away for an hour ends a run rather than hanging it forever. The clock is the row's enqueued_at: a retry does not start it over.

callBudget.rule: One call's own budget, by step (design section 6): the call is disconnected when it runs out, and is also disconnected after the contract's idleTimeoutSeconds without a byte (systemModel.request).

pause.when: The model's state is not up (wiki_model_status): down and auth_failed both stop the claim, so requests stay queued and undelivered (design section 5.3).
pause.resume: down resumes by itself — the probe keeps asking, and the next up makes the next pass claim again. auth_failed holds until the worker restarts with a corrected key, which is when every later call would stop being refused.

shutdown.plan: A, the owner's decision of 2026-10-07: the worker does not wait for calls in flight.
shutdown.rule: Stop claiming; abort each call in flight; each saves the text it had into partial and sets its lease_deadline_at to now, so the next process's sweep takes the row over at once and re-issues the call with what had arrived. A job interrupted the same way is handed back to the queue with nothing counted (jobs.lease.handBack), and its kind's pipeline is what decides, from the request rows, whether an interrupted call is continued or redone.

notify.rule: A settled request sends pg_notify on the channel with its id, and the worker that made it LISTENs on one dedicated connection (the shape realtime.service.ts uses) so the waiting job wakes as the answer lands.
notify.fallback: pollSeconds: a waiter re-reads its row on that interval whatever the announcements did, so a notification that never arrived costs latency and never an answer.

series.orbit_wiki_model_calls_total: counter, label outcome (succeeded, or one of systemModel.request.errors): read from the queue's rows at scrape time — a succeeded row is `succeeded`, a failed row its error's class, and a request that failed and was requeued counts under that failure's class until it succeeds or the wait limit ends it.
series.orbit_wiki_model_call_duration_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long the queue's calls ran (started_at to ended_at), over the rows that ended.
series.orbit_wiki_model_queue_depth: gauge: requests queued, waiting for a slot.
series.orbit_wiki_model_requests_in_flight: gauge: requests running right now, their lease unexpired — never above concurrency.claims.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_wait_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long settled calls waited from their enqueue to their first byte.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_run_seconds: summary, quantiles 0.5 and 0.95: how long settled calls ran.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_tokens_total: counter, label direction (input, output): tokens the succeeded calls spent.
series.orbit_wiki_model_request_errors_total: counter, label status: failed calls by the HTTP status that refused them, `none` for a failure with no answer (a connection, a timeout).

repoOps.why: The server runs the wiki's pipelines but never touches a repository: the credentials are on the runners (design section 1.4). A step that needs to know what the repository says asks the machine its space's workspace runs on, and the answer comes back through a row — no session, no concurrency slot and no model call on the runner (G2).

kindRuns.snapshot: Everything the server asks of one commit at once: fetch origin/main, resolve the sha, and build the index the pipelines query — every path with its size, every document's title and headings, every source file's symbols, the commits reachable from origin/main, and the README's first paragraph. A sha the server already holds is not sent again (`input.skipSha`). Above `fragments.inlineBytes` it travels in fragments.
kindRuns.read: The whole text of named paths at a named sha — the file itself, not a window of it (owner 2026-10-08). One file may be up to `read.wholeFileBytes` (2 MB); a larger one is not read at all: its item answers found: false with reason `too_large` and its size, and the pipelines treat it as missing and say why. An answer larger than `fragments.inlineBytes` travels in fragments as a snapshot's index does, and is reassembled by its sha256 and byte count before anything is cached. What a pipeline gives the model is cut server-side by `read.docSectionChars`, `read.contractChars` and `read.sectionChars`; those are cutting rules, not read limits. A runner that has not declared `readCapability` answers with the old window: at most `read.boundedChars` characters an item, the whole request answering `read.sectionChars`, its end marked `truncated`.
kindRuns.diff: `git diff --name-status -M` between two commits, and the design documents the range added or copied (`--diff-filter=AR -- docs/`) — what a maintenance run looks for.
kindRuns.anchors: The anchor checks a maintenance run already makes (`src/runner-go/wiki_anchors.go`), reused: a path exists, a symbol's region hashes as it is held to, a commit is reachable from the snapshot's commit set.

dispatch.claim: One statement per operation, up to perHeartbeat of them: WITH candidate AS (SELECT … JOIN workspace w ON w.id = o.workspace_id WHERE w.runner_id = this runner AND (state = 'queued' OR (state = 'running' AND heartbeat_at < now - staleSeconds AND lease_owner IS DISTINCT FROM this process)) ORDER BY created_at, id LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), UPDATE wiki_repo_op … FROM candidate — every claimed row a new claim_generation. A WITH that locks is read once, so the statement takes one row whatever the plan.
dispatch.route: workspace.runner_id: an operation is handed only to the machine the space's workspace runs on, and the workspace's work_dir travels with it.
dispatch.wake: The enqueue NOTIFYs the runner wake channel, so the machine beats at once instead of on its 30-second tick.

routes.result: POST /runner/wiki/repo-ops/:id/result — fenced on (lease_owner, claim_generation) and the runner token; a write from a claim that was taken over answers 409 STALE_CLAIM and settles nothing.
routes.progress: POST /runner/wiki/repo-ops/:id/progress — the heartbeat renewal that keeps a long operation from being taken over.
routes.fragments: POST /runner/wiki/repo-ops/:id/fragments — one call per fragment, fenced the same way, staged on the operation until its result arrives.

fragments.why: The API's request body is capped at 10 MB (src/apiserver/src/main.ts) and a plan's repository index is larger than that (design section 4.3). A snapshot that fits travels inside the result; one that does not is uploaded in fragments and reassembled — by sha256, and by the byte count the result names — before it becomes the space's snapshot. A read's answer is the same: above inlineBytes the whole answer (whole files and all) is staged as fragments of the operation and reassembled there.

cache.perSpace: One snapshot per space, replaced whole when a newer one lands: the index and the fragments it is kept in. Owner-scoped like everything else, and deleted with the space (the composite foreign key into wiki_space). The files read at a sha are kept one row per (space, sha, path) and are the same: a file already held is never read from the runner again, a snapshot landing drops every row of another sha, and the space's deletion takes them with it.
cache.visibility: The owner's and nobody else's: no route returns it, and what reaches the System model reaches it through the same redactor the notes go through (design section 9).

repoOps.safety: An operation checks its checkout before it reads it: the repository's origin URL must be the space's `repo.urlNorm` and the checkout's root commit must be the space's `rootCommitSha`. Otherwise it fails, says which repository it found, and reads nothing.
repoOps.waiting: A job that needs a repository operation is parked (wiki_job state waiting, waiting_for 'repo', no lease) and woken by a NOTIFY on the wiki_repo_op channel when the operation settles. A runner that has not declared `wiki-repo-op/v1` is handed nothing: the operation stays queued, the job stays parked until its wait limit, and the space's health line says the runner has to be upgraded. The import's snapshot (import.server.snapshot) is the exception: it is waited for holding the job's lease, a bounded wait with a fallback, so a runner that is away costs the import its fresh anchors and never the run. The documents' build (docs.build.server.repository) waits for its snapshot and its reads the same way, each bounded by docs.build.server.repoWaitSeconds: they are many and short, and a job parked on each would replay the build each time; one past its limit fails the attempt as infra.

storedText.why: Postgres keeps no U+0000 in text or jsonb (22021, 22P05), and a source file can have one: three files on main carry a raw NUL in a literal. On 2026-10-09 the read of one was refused with 22P05 and answered 500; the runner gave up after five tries, and the operation stayed running while its job waited out 300 seconds a read.
storedText.rule: A text the server keeps is kept as it is (`text`) unless Postgres cannot hold it as it is; then it is kept as its UTF-8 bytes in base64 (`base64`), and the row says which: `wiki_repo_file.content_encoding` for a file's text in the read cache, `encoding: "base64"` beside the system and the prompt of a `wiki_model_request.request` that carries one (modelQueue.requestEncoding), `answer_encoding` / `partial_encoding` for a model's answer (modelQueue.answerEncoding). Every reader decodes before it reads, so what a pipeline is handed — the documents' build, the plan's symbol fallback, maintenance — is, byte for byte, what `git show` printed on the runner.
storedText.operationRow: The raw answer of a read or a snapshot — the files' text, the index — is never written into wiki_repo_op.result: the row keeps what the settle made of it (a read's state and chars per item, a snapshot's sha, bytes, digest and fragments). A diff's paths and an anchor check's states are the answer itself and are kept as they are; none of them has a NUL.
storedText.notText: A lone surrogate — JSON can spell one (\ud800), no byte sequence decodes to one, and the runner's encoder writes every invalid byte as U+FFFD — is not a text the runner read, and is refused (INVALID_RESULT) wherever it comes: a read item's path or text, a fragment, a snapshot's index, a diff's or the anchors' result. A raw U+0000 in a fragment or in an index is refused the same way: both are JSON text, where a NUL is written \u0000, and a path in a tree never has one.

unsettled.rule: A result or a fragment the server refuses (INVALID_RESULT, 400) or cannot store (UNSTORABLE_RESULT, 422: the database refused the write — a value it cannot hold, a constraint — and the reason names its SQLSTATE) settles the operation failed with the reason, under the claim it was written with, before the route answers. The runner stops on a 4xx, and the job waiting on the operation is woken by the settle's NOTIFY rather than at its limit.
unsettled.passThrough: Two kinds of miss leave the operation as it is. STALE_CLAIM (409) and NOT_FOUND (404): it is another claim's, or nobody's. A conflict the database rolled back, or the database itself failing: the write did not happen rather than being refused, the route answers 503 or 500, and the runner sends it again. A close that itself fails leaves the original error standing, and the runner's retry comes back to it.
unsettled.why: Before 2026-10-09 a result the database refused was a 500: the runner sent it five more times and gave up, and the operation stayed running under a claim nothing would ever settle.

abandoned.rule: Every pass of the wiki-worker, before it claims anything, settles failed — with the reason on the row — a running operation nothing will ever settle: its job has ended (succeeded, failed or cancelled), or its claim has been silent for `seconds`. Either way it has been quiet for at least dispatch.staleSeconds, so a result about to arrive is not raced, and each one ended is announced on the wiki_repo_op channel. A result that arrives afterwards is answered with the row's state.
abandoned.why: A runner renews its claim only by staging fragments, and no job waits longer than 300 seconds for one operation. Before this an operation whose result the runner gave up on stayed running under its claim for good: three reads of 2026-10-09, refused with 22P05, outlived their maintain job.

refusals.when: The wiki is off for this account (ORBIT_WIKI rollout).
The calling session's workspace is in no space and could not be bound on first use, or the owner left it out. The message says which in one sentence.

The op, its entry, its anchors or its sources do not have the shape this contract gives them: a kind's fields (KIND_SPECS), a limit, a phase-3 kind, an amend of a decision, a baseRevision where one is required or forbidden, a source ref of a kind in sourceInput.rowIdKinds that is neither spelling of an id. errors[] names every field that failed.
A non-owner op adds, amends or supersedes a kind only the owner writes (kinds.<kind>.ownerOnlyOps).
A source does not resolve among the owner's own rows (errors[] names it by its path), cites a wiki entry or view, or an op that must cite a source cites none.
A quote, whitespace-normalized, is not a substring of the text of the record it cites.
An amend, supersede or retire names a baseRevision that is not the entry's current revision. The answer carries the current revision and a diff.

A session's new note is past agentSurface.note.rules.perSession. Or the op is past limits.opsPerChangeset in its request; or it would wait for the owner and pass limits.opsPerTurn for the request or limits.opsPerSession for the calling session (limitNotes.quota); or the review mode would apply it and the changeset would pass the circuit breaker (reviewModes.floors).
The op would wait for review and the space already has limits.pendingOpsPerSpace pending ops that wait on the owner's decision (spot checks and ops waiting for their verification not counted).
The title or text, or a session's note (agentSurface.note.probe), reads as a tool probe (test, probe, TEST_WRITE_CHECK). The message says the tool works and not to retry.

A decide, a revert, an entry's Reject or Confirm, a reopening of verifications, a change of the review mode or of automaticSpotChecks, or any request of the plan's on the user door (plan.who.owner) arrived with a session header, whatever the session's role: each is the owner's, on the user door, with no acting session. So is every route of the wiki chat (chat.door: making or listing chats, reading cards, and the presses — apply, edit, discard, undo, retry, seen) and a restore of a section's version (docs.versions.restore).

The calling session verifies, forems or judges work (task.verifiesTaskId, task.isForeman, a judgment session). Knowledge is not evidence, so such a session neither reads nor proposes. And wiki_draft from a session that is not a wiki chat (agentSurface.chat.draft.who): it drafts for the owner of a chat, and no other session has one.
An idempotency key the owner already used arrived with a different request (its normalized digest differs). The same request under the same key is a replay and gets the recorded answer.

A succeeded run asked to advance the cursor to a token behind the space's watermark: another run already went further, and the cursor only moves forward (maintenance.cursor.advance). The answer carries the cursor as it stands.
A cursor token that no dossier page of this space handed out: one that does not decode, one of another space, or a position past the furthest page the space's dossier route has issued.

An article write named an entry-set fingerprint that is not its topic's current one: the topic's entries changed while the articles were being written (articles.regeneration). Nothing is written; the next run writes them from the entries as they stand.

A runner that predates server execution asked the runner door for what the server now does itself: a note registered without readBy server — an orbit wiki import that would read it with the session's own model (import.server.door). Nothing is read or written.

A plan draft, an owner's edit of the plan, a proposed change to it or the acceptance of one did not pass the plan's gate (plan.gate): errors[] lists everything it found, each with its check and where it is. Nothing is stored.

A plan request was built on a version that is no longer the space's newest (plan.versions), confirmed a version that is no longer a draft, or answered a proposal already decided. Nothing is written; read the plan again.
A space's documents were to be written, or a change proposed to its plan, and the space has no plan its owner confirmed (plan.guard).

A document write does not have the shape docs.schema gives it: a field it does not name, a repository footnote with no sha or no lines, a record footnote with no id, a section the confirmed plan's document does not have, a via entry that is not an entry of the space. errors[] lists everything it found, each { path, message }, the first docs.rules.errorsMax. Nothing is written.

refusalRules.orderNote: The order each op is checked in (design section 4.1); redaction, taint, effect and similar refuse nothing, they mark the op. changesetSize is limits.opsPerChangeset, read off the op's position alone. quota comes after the effect because what it counts depends on it: the review queue, the ops that wait (limitNotes.quota), and the circuit breaker, which counts what the review mode applies.
refusalRules.perOp: Each op is judged on its own. The ops that pass are recorded in one transaction; a refused op writes nothing.
refusalRules.status: A request none of whose ops was recorded answers with the HTTP status of its first refusal and every op's outcome in the body. A request that recorded something answers 200.
refusalRules.dryRun: Checks every op and answers as the request would, recording nothing and publishing nothing: every op's outcome, under the status the request would be answered with (status) — 200 when an op would be recorded, and the first refusal's otherwise. Its answer also carries breaker: the circuit breaker as the request found it, before any of its ops — {scope, activeAtStart, changed, remaining}: scope run for a maintenance run's changeset (maintenance.job.breaker) and changeset otherwise, activeAtStart the active entries it is counted against, changed the entries already changed through the review mode, and remaining how many more distinct entries the mode may change before an op is refused, null where no op is held to the breaker (a Manual space, the owner's own write, a space holding fewer than reviewModes.rules.breakerMinActiveEntries active entries). A request of the same ops recorded now refuses exactly the ones past remaining.
refusalRules.idempotency: An idempotency key is the owner's: the same key with the same normalized request returns the recorded answer, marked replayed, and writes and publishes nothing.
refusalRules.notFound: Another owner's space, entry or changeset is a plain 404 with no wiki code, the same answer as one that does not exist.
refusalRules.serviceToken: A service token is refused on both doors (403), as session_search refuses it: entries derive from conversation text on other machines.

agentSurface.why: An agent reads the wiki and proposes to it; it never decides. Five tools, split by risk rather than by entity: the fifth, wiki_draft, a wiki chat's alone (chat.draft).

wiki_search.returns: entries only: id, kind, title, summary, trust, anchorState, match (searchMatches), score, and how old each one is (age)

age.why: So that a caller can judge for itself how old what an entry says is (the wiki_search review, 2026-11-06): anchorState verified says that the last check found the anchors as recorded (anchorStates), never that what the entry says still holds. Every hit carries all four, on the runner door and on the owner's GET /api/wiki/search alike; a time is ISO 8601 in UTC.
age.recordedAt: When the entry was recorded: the birth of its lineage (wiki_entry.recorded_at), when it was first proposed or written. No amend moves it; a supersede is a lineage of its own.
age.changedAt: When its current revision was written (the created_at of the wiki_entry_revision at its current_revision): the last change to what it says. An anchor check writes no revision and leaves it as it was. Null only for an entry deleted while the search read it.
age.anchorCheckedRef: The ref its anchors were last checked at (wiki_entry.anchor_checked_ref): a commit of the space's main, as the maintenance run reports it. Null until the first check, and again after an amend that gives the anchors anew (anchorRules.verify.aggregate); an amend that leaves them alone keeps it, so a check can be older than changedAt.
age.anchorCheckedAt: When that check was made (wiki_entry.anchor_checked_at); null exactly when anchorCheckedRef is.

wiki_get.returns: whole entries; each anchor with its last check (the ref and the time); each source with its orbit-* link

params.replaces: optional, in a wiki chat alone: the id of an open card of the chat that the new one replaces (chat.drafts.replace)

wiki_propose.returns: per op: pending (with waitsFor verification when an automatic space's verification, not the owner, decides it), applied, conflict (current revision and diff) or refused (reasons); similar[] beside an add or supersede. In a wiki chat: { status: draft, draftId, ops, similar[], rewrites } (chat.propose)

params.corrects: optional: the id of the entry this says is wrong
params.replaces: optional, in a wiki chat alone: the id of an open card of the chat that the challenge's card replaces (chat.drafts.replace)

params.kind: required: rewrite or plan (chat.drafts.kinds; entry ops are wiki_propose's)
params.sections: rewrite: required, 1 to chat.rules.rewritesMax of { doc, section }: a document's slug and a section's key, each a written section of the confirmed plan (WIKI_SCHEMA naming it otherwise)
params.change: plan: required, shaped as a plan proposal's change (plan.proposals)
params.reason: required: why, in a sentence or two; the card shows it
params.replaces: optional: the id of an open card of this chat that this one replaces

wiki_draft.returns: { status: draft, draftId, kind, rewrites }, or refused with its reasons (chat.draft)

agentSurface.notTools: No tool accepts, confirms, decides, hard-deletes or overwrites a page. Confirmation exists only on the owner channel.

chat.doc: docs/wiki-contract.md section 11 and section 28.4; docs/wiki-chat-design.md section 7.1
chat.who: A chat session (chat.binding: session.wiki_chat_space_id set). Its space is that one, the space its workspace is in — create chose an eligible workspace of it (chat.workspace).
chat.propose: In a chat, wiki_propose drafts. Every op — add, amend, supersede and retire, and the reinforce and challenge that apply at once elsewhere — is checked as ever (refusalRules.order: schema, sources, quotes, redaction, compare-and-set, the taint mark; not quota, review queue or breaker, which a draft takes no place in) and the ops that pass become one card (chat.drafts), written nowhere else: no changeset, no entry, no Review, no verification. It answers { status: draft, draftId, ops: [each draft, or refused with its reasons], similar[] }; a request none of whose ops passed makes no card and answers as it would have. dryRun checks and makes nothing. A principle op is not refused WIKI_KIND_OWNER_ONLY in a chat: it waits for the owner's press, which is the owner's own write (reviewModes.chat). In every space and every review mode alike: the mode never touches a card.
chat.note: In a chat, wiki_note's corrects drafts its challenge: the note is kept as anywhere (note.stored), and the challenge becomes a card, not an op; challenged answers { status: draft, draftId }. A note without corrects is unchanged: it was only ever a lead for maintenance.
chat.replaces: In a chat both tools take one parameter more, replaces: the id of an open card of the same chat that the new one replaces (chat.drafts.replace). It joined toolSpecs.wiki_propose.params and toolSpecs.wiki_note.params with the runner that serves it (C6), as wiki_draft joined tools; any other session's call leaves it unread.
