draft.returns: { status: draft, draftId, kind, rewrites }, or refused with its reasons
draft.who: A chat alone. Any other session is refused WIKI_SESSION_EXCLUDED, its message saying that wiki_draft works only in a wiki chat; a verifier, foreman or judgment session is refused it as every wiki call (excludedSessions).
draft.plan: The plan kind arrives with the plan card (design section 14, second step). Until then a plan draft is refused WIKI_SCHEMA at kind, its message saying plan drafts are not open yet.
draft.description: Draft, for the owner of this wiki chat to apply, a change that is not an entry: a rewrite of wiki sections from main, when the code changed and a section did not follow it, or a change to how the wiki's documents are planned. Nothing is written until the owner presses Apply on the card, so never call a draft applied. A change to what the wiki knows is an entry: use wiki_propose. Works only in a wiki chat.
draft.arrival: It joined tools, toolSpecs and cli with the runner that serves it (C6, which needs a runner release): TestWikiAgentSurfaceIsTheContracts (src/runner-go/wiki_tools_test.go) holds tools to the tools a binary serves, so the fifth name arrived with the binary that serves it. This block stays its contract, word for word; the cli/mcp parity, the help coverage and agent_instructions' three family tables took it with the tool. A runner older than that release offers no wiki_draft, and a chat on one drafts its entries through wiki_propose alone.
draft.notTools: It accepts nothing, confirms nothing, decides nothing and overwrites no page: it makes a card the owner may press. notTools holds as written.

chat.unchanged: Outside a chat nothing here applies: wiki_propose, wiki_note, their descriptions and every answer are what they were.

agentSurface.proposeDescription: Record only what someone could not read from the code: a decision and what was rejected, a pitfall and its fix, a convention. Cite the turns or records it came from; a claim you cannot cite is not ready. Whether it takes effect depends on the space's review mode, and what has taken effect other sessions can find in a search: tell the user what each op's status says, and never call a pending op saved.
agentSurface.noteDescription: Tell the wiki something this session learned that someone could not read from the code: a decision and why, a trap and its fix, a rule the owner gave. One claim, in one or two sentences. Maintenance reads it later against this session's records and writes an entry only if they bear it out, so it is not in the wiki yet and may never be. Not for progress or status: use task_progress_report. If your engine keeps its own memory, what you write there is read the same way: do not write both. To say an entry is wrong, pass corrects with its id: the entry is flagged at once.

note.body: { text, paths?, corrects? }, each held to note.rules, and a field that fails is named (WIKI_SCHEMA). corrects is an entry's id, in either spelling.
note.who: A session this runner hosts for its owner (X-Orbit-Session-Id): a note is read against that session's records, so a headless call is refused 400, and one naming a session the runner does not host 403. A verifier, foreman or judgment session is refused WIKI_SESSION_EXCLUDED. The space is the one the session's workspace is bound to, never an argument: a workspace in none is refused WIKI_SPACE_UNBOUND.
note.stored: A row of import.tables, through the writer an import uses (import.note.redaction, import.note.dedup): redacted before it is hashed or kept, its session in wiki_note.session_id with no foreign key (storage.noteSessionMigration), and its path session/<the session's public id>. paths, trimmed, each once and in one order, are appended to the text as a last line 'Paths: a, b', so the same claim about the same paths is one note. A note imported from a file keeps a null session_id.
note.dedup: One text is one note in a space, whoever wrote it: a text the space already holds answers that note with created false, writes nothing and counts toward no limit. It stays with whoever wrote it first, so it is not read in the dossier of a later session that says the same.
note.probe: A text that reads as a tool probe (looksLikeProbe) is refused WIKI_PROBE_REFUSED before anything is written.
note.quota: A session writes at most rules.perSession notes; the next new one is refused WIKI_QUOTA. Read and not locked: two at once can pass it by one, and nothing counts on it exactly.
note.review: A note is no op: it makes no changeset, takes no place in the review queue and counts toward no limit of limits. Nothing reads it but the maintenance run (maintenance.dossier.memory); no search, read or push shows it.
note.corrects: Submits one challenge op through the one write entry point, as the session, with the note's text as its reason and an idempotency key of the note's and the entry's ids: the entry is flagged at once (the challenge's own rules, opRules), the owner answers it in Review, and asking again is the same challenge. It is a challenge like any other, so it is held to limits.opsPerTurn and limits.opsPerSession. An entry the session may not read, another owner's or another space's, is answered as one that does not exist. The note is kept whichever way the challenge goes.
note.answer: { noted: true, noteId, created, readBy, challenged? }. readBy is the server's words for what reads it: 'the next maintenance run'; 'no maintenance run yet: maintenance is off in this space'; or, for a text the space already held from elsewhere, 'not this session's maintenance run: the space already holds this text from elsewhere'. challenged, when corrects was given: { status, changesetId, opId, entryId } from the op's answer, or { status: refused, reasons: [{ code?, message }] }. A refused challenge is still a 200: the note was recorded.
note.oldServer: A runner newer than its server answers a plain 404 here, naming no wiki refusal. wikiNoteCallError in src/runner-go/wiki_tools.go says in a sentence that the server is too old for wiki_note and that nothing was recorded, and neither the tool nor the command crashes. WIKI_DISABLED is told apart, as everywhere on this door (rollout.off).

runner.guard: RunnerAuthGuard, plus the calling session (X-Orbit-Session-Id) checked the way runner-watches.controller.ts checks it
runner.verificationNote: The session that proposed the ops, and no other (reviewModes.verification.who.runner): X-Orbit-Session-Id is required, and another session's op or another owner's anything is a 404.
runner.importNote: phase 2 (import): orbit wiki import's registration of a file as a note, for a session of the space's owner — X-Orbit-Session-Id is required, and another owner's space is a 404. It takes only readBy server (import.server.door).
runner.importJobNote: server execution, P5 (import.server): which path an import takes, the notes handed to an import job, and the job read back — for a session of the space's owner, X-Orbit-Session-Id required, another owner's space or job a 404.

verify.serverExecution: The server verifies what a session proposed, and the session runs nothing: an op the space's Automatic mode holds back (reviewModes.verification.waits) is queued as a verify job for the session that proposed it the moment it is recorded (jobs.kindRuns.verify, jobs.make), the wiki worker asks the System model through the queue, and each verdict is reported through the one writer (reviewModes.verification.who.server) with the prompt and the strict reading this entry describes. The command asks the server to verify these ops and waits for the result (does): since P11 (2026-10-19) it has no model of its own, and a server whose list does not say servedBy server is too old for it. A maintenance run is not a session either: it verifies its own ops in its own process (maintenance.job.server.verify).
verify.tool: none: a CLI verb with no MCP tool beside it. It waits for the server's verdicts as long as they take, which is a runner's work rather than a tool call's, and it reports only what the server recorded.
verify.precondition: Verify only the ops this session proposed into an automatic space, and never write a verdict yourself: each verdict is the System model's, read on the Orbit server against the op's own sources, and a verdict that cannot be read is reported as nothing.
verify.does: Asks the server to verify the ops this session proposed into --space that wait for their verification (reviewModes.verification.routes.request), then reads the list's waiting count (routes.list) until it reaches zero, and prints how many the server verified. A list that does not say servedBy server — a server from before it verified itself — is refused: nothing is verified, and the ops keep waiting. The command exits non-zero when the wait runs out with ops still without a verdict: they keep waiting, and the next run asks for them again.
verify.prompt: Hand-written, one op at a time: the entry's kind, title, summary and fields, the text of each source, and the neighbours a duplicate may name — each by a number of its own, E1 to En in the order listed, and never by its id: a local model copies a 21-character id wrong (09-30 to 10-02, 34XhYj76NhjjOJTEFEtFE came back as 34XhYj76NhjjOJTEFE run after run, and its op never got a verdict). The answer is one JSON object: {"verdict": one of reviewModes.verification.verdicts, "reason": one sentence, "duplicateOf": the number of the neighbour it duplicates, for a duplicate}, and the verdict reported names the id that number stands for (reviewModes.verification.report). The object is read as encoding/json reads a struct: the keys in any case — {"Verdict": …, "Reason": …} names verdict and reason — and the reason's leading and trailing spaces trimmed as Go's strings.TrimSpace trims them (U+0085 among them).
verify.unreadable: An answer that is not that object — no JSON, another verdict, no reason, a duplicate naming no listed neighbour by its number — is not a verdict: nothing is reported for its op, which keeps waiting, and it counts as a failure in the verify job's report (jobs.kindRuns.verify). A number is one the prompt listed, exactly: an id, whole or cut short, is none, and nothing is guessed from a prefix; the verdict and the number are read as plan.gate.values reads a closed-set value. A maintenance run verifies its own ops in its own process, asks once more about those left without a verdict, and what is still without one fails nothing (maintenance.job.run.steps, verify).

decide.sessionHeader: refused WIKI_OWNER_CHANNEL_ONLY whatever the session's role (the precedent is refuseSessionAuthoredConfirmation in coordinator-authority.ts)
decide.why: The confirmation card in the runner is not a gate: the server never checks it and a headless call passes it. So only the owner channel decides.

agentSurface.readBoundary: A session reads a space's entries only when its workspace is in that space (space.binding): being in a space is the owner agreeing to share confirmed entries across the space's workspaces, which the owner takes back by leaving one out. A pending proposal is visible only to the session that made it.
agentSurface.excludedSessions: Verifier, foreman and judgment sessions are refused every wiki_* call (WIKI_SESSION_EXCLUDED) and are never pushed to. wiki_draft is refused the same way to every session that is not a wiki chat (agentSurface.chat.draft.who).

rollout.canary: only the accounts ORBIT_WIKI_CANARY_OWNERS lists (comma-separated ids) have the wiki; every other account is as under off
rollout.off: the apiserver answers 404 WIKI_DISABLED on every route of both doors, the claim carries wikiDisabled, the runner mounts none of the tools, no <orbit_wiki_context> is pushed, and an orbit-wiki: link card reads as unavailable

agentSurface.doorMissing: A runner newer than its apiserver says in a sentence that the server has no wiki door yet, as watch_tools.go's watchDoorMissing does. wiki_note's door is newer than the rest, so it says the server is too old for it (note.oldServer).

realtime.scope: the space's owner, on the user-scoped control-plane stream (GET /api/events). The envelope names no session.
realtime.id: the space whose entries, review queue, bindings, settings, articles or plan changed
realtime.redaction: The space's id and nothing else: no entry, title, status, op or count. A client re-reads what it shows, and that read decides what it may see.
publishedWhen: a changeset recorded something, after its transaction commits
the owner decided ops, after the transaction commits
a space was created, its settings changed, or a workspace was added to it, turned back on or left out
a space was deleted, after its transaction commits
the owner reverted a changeset or rejected an entry, after the transaction commits
a verdict was recorded, after its transaction commits
pending ops expired or were withdrawn
a topic's articles were written, or a space's topics seeded, after the transaction commits
a version of a space's plan was stored or confirmed, or a change to it proposed or decided, after the transaction commits
a document's sections were written, or sentences of it withdrawn for a repository file gone from origin/main, after the transaction commits
a chat's card was made, replaced or pressed, or its rewrite's job was queued, held up, started or ended (chat.realtime), after the transaction commits
a section was restored to a version it kept (docs.versions.restore), after the transaction commits
realtime.correctness: Nothing depends on it. Dropping every announcement changes only how long a client waits: clients re-read on focus and on reconnect.
realtime.clientGroup: The web maps it to the wiki query group, never to groupsFor's default sessions group; Swift decodes it as ControlEvent.wikiChanged.

draft.title: Knowledge is stored as entries, not pages
draft.summary: The wiki stores atomic entries; pages, the decision log and the agent slice are views of them.

fields.context: People ask what is true now; agents need pitfalls and conventions.
fields.decision: Store atomic entries with sources and anchors, and project every page from them.

alternatives.whyRejected: Whole-page rewrites collapse, and a page cannot be reviewed item by item.

fields.consequences: Every view can be rebuilt; review and measurement are per entry.

vectors.why: A decision carries what was rejected and why; anchors of two types.

fields.fix: Run pg specs through scripts/run-pg-spec.sh, which provisions PostgreSQL and counts a skip as red.

vectors.why: Every trigger key present; detector is optional.
